body:
After selecting an entire row or column to copy or cut (with the right-click menu),  when you use the same right-click menu to paste, there's no option to "Insert Copied Cells", only options to "Insert" (which inserts a blank row) and "Paste".

title: Implement sequential keyboard shortcuts with Alt
author: eylenburg
body:
If you work in an industry like finance or accounting, you'll see people who have memorised hundreds of keyboard shortcuts for Excel. You  can use every function in Excel without ever using the mouse. 

In Excel, when you press "Alt", there are tooltips on the ribbon which you can sequentially press. e.g. you Alt -> H [Home] -> A [Align] -> R [Right] allows you to apply "Align Right" formatting.  Alt -> H -> V -> S opens the "Paste Special" menu where you can then use more shortcuts without ever using the mouse, e.g. Alt + E for transpose paste. You can use this for anything on the ribbon, no matter how deep down in some submenu it is.

There are also other shortcuts started with Alt and sequential key presses. I think a lot of them come from pre-ribbon Excel. For example, Alt -> E -> S -> T/V/F/C pastest only Formatting/Values/Formulas/Comments, respectively. Or Alt -> O -> C -> A is a legacy shortcut for auto-fit column width (the shortcut based on ribbon tooltips would be Alt -> H -> O -> I). 

The end goal of should be not only to implement sequential shortcuts starting with Alt, but generally making Gridcraft usable completely without mouse while using the exact same keyboard shortcuts as Excel.

author: Lord-Taw
body:
Several popup UI elements remain open after losing focus:

- Row/column header context menus
- Table filter dropdowns

Expected behavior:
Context menus should close when the user clicks outside them. Filter dropdown behavior may be configurable, but it should remain consistent and predictable.

Actual behavior:
These UI elements remain open after clicking elsewhere in the application and appear to require keyboard interaction (such as ESC) to close.

Details:

When I right-click a row or column header, the context menu opens correctly. However, if I left-click elsewhere in the application, the menu remains open instead of closing.

I noticed the same behavior with table filter dropdowns. For context menus, this seems like a usability issue because users generally expect them to close when they lose focus. For filter dropdowns, keeping them open after losing focus may actually be useful in some workflows. If this behavior is intentional, it could be exposed as an optional setting so users can choose their preferred behavior.

However, if filter dropdowns are intended to remain open, they should only be visible while working in the table where they were opened. Currently, the dropdown remains in the foreground when switching to another table in the same workbook, obscuring the content of the active table.

1. Open GridCraft.
2. Right-click a row or column header and/or open a filter dropdown.
3. Left-click anywhere outside the menu.

title: Feature request: Spanish-localized formula function names and separators
author: funkholio
body:
## Summary

Please add support for Spanish-localized formula syntax in GridCraft.

Currently, formulas appear to require English function names and comma-separated arguments. This makes GridCraft harder to use for Spanish-speaking users and reduces compatibility with workbooks created in localized versions of Microsoft Excel or LibreOffice Calc.

## Requested functionality

Allow GridCraft to recognize Spanish aliases for Excel-compatible function names, while preserving English function names as the canonical/internal syntax.

Examples:

| Spanish formula | English equivalent |
|---|---|
| `=SUMA(A1:A10)` | `=SUM(A1:A10)` |
| `=PROMEDIO(A1:A10)` | `=AVERAGE(A1:A10)` |
| `=SI(A1>0;"Sí";"No")` | `=IF(A1>0,"Sí","No")` |
| `=SUMAR.SI(A1:A10;">0")` | `=SUMIF(A1:A10,">0")` |
| `=CONTAR.SI(A1:A10;">0")` | `=COUNTIF(A1:A10,">0")` |
| `=BUSCARV(A2;D:E;2;FALSO)` | `=VLOOKUP(A2,D:E,2,FALSE)` |
| `=HOY()` | `=TODAY()` |
| `=VERDADERO` / `=FALSO` | `=TRUE` / `=FALSE` |

## Separator support

For Spanish locales, please also consider accepting semicolons (`;`) as function argument separators, in addition to commas (`,`).

For example:

```excel
=SI(A1>100;"Alto";"Bajo")
```

could be interpreted equivalently to:

```excel
=IF(A1>100,"Alto","Bajo")
```

## Why this matters

Spanish is widely used across Latin America and Spain. Supporting localized function aliases would:

- Improve usability for Spanish-speaking users.
- Help users migrate existing Excel and LibreOffice spreadsheets.
- Improve formula compatibility with localized spreadsheet workflows.
- Allow GridCraft to remain internally English-based while providing locale-aware parsing and display.

A first implementation could focus on a small set of common functions (`SUMA`, `SI`, `PROMEDIO`, `CONTAR`, `SUMAR.SI`, `BUSCARV`) and expand over time.

Thank you for considering it.

title: Rotated text with Wrap Text on is drawn horizontally (grid and print)
author: LloydNicholson
body:
Cells with **both** a text rotation (e.g. 90°, `textRotation="90"`) **and** Wrap Text on are drawn horizontally: the rotation is ignored and the text is word-wrapped into the column width instead. This is common in mark sheets and schedules, where narrow columns have tall, upright headers.

**Repro** (no real data needed):
```sh
gridcraft-cli run --cmd 'cell.set={"cell":"A1","input":"Term 1 : Drama : Continuous Assessment"}' \
  --cmd 'home.orientation={"range":"A1","angle":"up"}' \
  --cmd 'home.wrapText={"range":"A1","on":true}' \
  --cmd 'home.columnWidth={"cols":"A:A","chars":4}' \
  --cmd 'home.rowHeight={"rows":"1:1","height":267}' --out rotated.xlsx
gridcraft rotated.xlsx
```
The same happens opening an `.xlsx` saved elsewhere with `<alignment textRotation="90" wrapText="1"/>` on narrow columns.

**Expected:** the text reads bottom-to-top inside the tall cell (wrapping, if needed, along the rotated direction). Rotation without wrap already works.

**Actual:** horizontal text broken into 3–4 characters per line ("Ter / m 1 / Dra / ma…").

**Cause:** in `crates/ui-egui/src/grid.rs`, the wrap branch draws the galley and `continue`s before the rotated-text path is reached. `crates/engine/src/cmd/print.rs` has the same gap (`if rot != 0 && rot != 255 && !wrap`), so printing/PDF is affected too.

**Environment:** Fedora 44 x86_64, gridcraft `main` @ 51b531b (0.3.0).

I'm preparing a PR for this.

title: General numbers in small fonts show #### in narrow columns though they fit
author: LloydNicholson
body:
In narrow columns, General-format numbers in a font smaller than 11pt show `####` even though they fit. Common in mark sheets: 9pt marks such as `100` in columns with a stored width of 4 (28px).

**Repro** (no real data needed):
```sh
gridcraft-cli run --cmd 'cell.set={"cell":"A1","input":"100"}' \
  --cmd 'home.fontSize={"range":"A1","size":9}' \
  --cmd 'home.columnWidth={"cols":"A:A","width":28}' --out narrow.xlsx
gridcraft narrow.xlsx
```
**Expected:** `100` (it is ~16px wide at 9pt × the 0.8 display scale, in a 22.4px column). Printing already shows `100`.
**Actual:** `##`.

**Cause:** `grid.rs` measures the digit width once, for an 11pt cell font (`char_w`), and `display_text` decides how many General digits fit from that, whatever the cell's own font size. At 9pt the real digit is ~20% narrower, so `100` is judged 2 digits wide at most. (`print.rs` already measures with the cell's own font and size.)

**Environment:** Fedora 44 x86_64, gridcraft `main` @ 51b531b (0.3.0).

I'm preparing a PR for this.

(`crates/ui-egui/src/widgets.rs:54`).

paths, for example `/usr/share/fonts/dejavu/DejaVuSans.ttf` and
`/usr/share/fonts/noto/NotoSans-Regular.ttf`. Fedora installs these fonts in other folders:

| Font | Fedora path |
|---|---|

| Cantarell | `/usr/share/fonts/abattis-cantarell-fonts/Cantarell-Regular.otf` |

non-ASCII characters in `crates/ui-egui/src` against those fonts (Ubuntu-Light,
NotoEmoji-Regular, emoji-icon-font). These are missing from all three:

`← ↑ → ↓ ↳ ⇒ ⇧ ⌃ ▲ ▸ ▼ ▾ ✓ ✕`

title: `=0.1+0.2=0.3` returns FALSE: comparisons, MATCH and COUNTIF don't use Excel's 15-significant-digit equality
author: wzsxb233
body:
**Summary**

Excel and LibreOffice treat two numbers as equal when they agree to 15 significant digits, so floating-point noise doesn't break comparisons. GridCraft compares raw f64 values. As a result, common spreadsheet logic gives different answers from Excel. Examples are `IF(A1+A2=A3, …)`, exact `MATCH`, and `COUNTIF(range, 0.3)`. These formulas look right because the cells display `0.3`.

**Environment**
- GridCraft `main` @ 51b531b (v0.3.0), `gridcraft-cli` release build
- Linux x86_64 (Debian 13), Rust 1.99
- Reference: LibreOffice 25.2.3 headless recalculation of the same .xlsx

**Steps to reproduce**
```sh
gridcraft-cli eval '=0.1+0.2=0.3'                              # FALSE
gridcraft-cli eval '=1.1*3=3.3'                                # FALSE
gridcraft-cli eval '=IF(0.7+0.1=0.8,"eq","ne")'                # ne
gridcraft-cli eval '=MATCH(0.3,{0.1,0.30000000000000004},0)'   # #N/A
gridcraft-cli eval '=COUNTIF({0.30000000000000004},0.3)'       # 0
```
Workbook version: put `=0.1+0.2` in B1, then use `=COUNTIF(B1:B1,0.3)` and `=MATCH(0.3,B1:B1,0)`. `gridcraft-cli cat` shows B1 as `0.3`, but the formulas return `0` and `#N/A`.

**Expected** (Excel and LibreOffice)
`TRUE`, `TRUE`, `eq`, `2` and `1`. LibreOffice gives these results for the same workbook (`soffice --convert-to csv`).

**Actual**
`FALSE`, `FALSE`, `ne`, `#N/A` and `0`.

**Notes**
Excel compares values after rounding them to 15 significant digits. LibreOffice does the same with `rtl::math::approxEqual`. Applying this to `=`, `<>`, `<`, `>`, `<=` and `>=`, and to the exact-match paths of MATCH, XLOOKUP, VLOOKUP, COUNTIF and SUMIF, would match both apps. Related: ROUND to 15 or more digits also leaves the noise in place (separate issue).

title: ROUND(x, n) returns x unchanged when n reaches 15 significant digits: `ROUND(0.1+0.2,15)` = 0.30000000000000004
author: wzsxb233
body:
**Summary**

`round_half_away` (`crates/functions/src/util.rs`) builds a 15-significant-digit decimal string. When the requested digits reach the end of that string (`keep >= d.len()`), it returns the original `x`, not the 15-digit value. So `ROUND(x,15)` and similar calls, which people use to remove floating-point noise, leave the noise in place. In Excel, `ROUND(0.1+0.2,15)=0.3` is TRUE.

**Environment**
- GridCraft `main` @ 51b531b (v0.3.0), `gridcraft-cli` release build; Linux x86_64

**Steps to reproduce**
```sh
gridcraft-cli eval '=ROUND(0.1+0.2,15)'               # 0.30000000000000004
gridcraft-cli eval '=ROUND(0.1+0.2,15)-0.3'           # 5.551115123125783e-17
gridcraft-cli eval '=ROUND(0.1+0.2,15)=0.3'           # FALSE
gridcraft-cli eval '=ROUND(1.0000000000000002,15)=1'  # FALSE
gridcraft-cli eval '=ROUND(0.1+0.2,14)=0.3'           # TRUE (works below 15 digits)
```

**Expected**
`ROUND(0.1+0.2,15)` should return 0.3, and the comparisons should be TRUE, as in Excel and LibreOffice (LibreOffice checked headless).

**Actual**
The unrounded value is returned whenever `e + 1 + digits >= 15`.

**Suggested fix**
In the `keep >= d.len()` branch, return the value parsed back from the 15-significant-digit string, for example `format!("{:.14e}", x).parse()`, not `x`. The same probably applies to ROUNDUP/ROUNDDOWN if they share this helper.

title: XLSX writer omits `_xlpm.` prefix on LET/LAMBDA parameter names, so Excel refuses to open the file
author: nihilist-narwhal
body:
## Summary

Workbooks containing `LET` or `LAMBDA` are written with bare parameter names, e.g.

```xml
<f>_xlfn.LET(x,Data!A3*2,y,x+1,x*y)</f>
<f>_xlfn.LAMBDA(a,b,a^2+b)(3,4)</f>
```

In the file format Excel expects the parameter names to carry the `_xlpm.` prefix:

```xml
<f>_xlfn.LET(_xlpm.x,Data!A3*2,_xlpm.y,_xlpm.x+1,_xlpm.x*_xlpm.y)</f>
<f>_xlfn.LAMBDA(_xlpm.a,_xlpm.b,_xlpm.a^2+_xlpm.b)(3,4)</f>
```

Without it, Excel refuses to open the whole workbook, so a single `LET` anywhere makes a GridCraft-saved file unopenable in Excel.

## Repro

1. In GridCraft, set any cell to `=LET(x,2,x*3)` (or `=LAMBDA(a,a+1)(1)`).
2. Save as `.xlsx`.
3. Open in Excel → the file does not open.

I bisected a 108-formula test workbook one formula per file: only the `LET` and `LAMBDA` files are rejected. After adding `_xlpm.` to the parameter names by hand, Excel opens the file and calculates both formulas to the same values GridCraft computes (`LET` → 3472632 with `Data!A3` = 931.5, `LAMBDA(...)(3,4)` → 13).

## Where

`crates/xlsx/src/fmla.rs` (`to_file`) adds `_xlfn.` / `_xlfn._xlws.` prefixes but nothing handles `_xlpm.`; there is no occurrence of `_xlpm` in the repo. The reader probably needs the reverse too (strip `_xlpm.` when loading Excel-authored files), since Excel always writes the prefix.

Also applies to the other functions that bind names: `LAMBDA` used through `MAP`/`REDUCE`/`SCAN`/`BYROW`/`BYCOL`/`MAKEARRAY`, and `LAMBDA`s stored in defined names.

## Environment

GridCraft `51b531b` (main), Excel for Mac 16.113.2, macOS 26.3.

title: Non-spilling array formulas are saved without the dynamic-array flag (`cm`), so Excel applies implicit intersection: `SUM(A1:A20*B1:B20)` becomes `#VALUE!`
author: nihilist-narwhal
body:
## Summary

The XLSX writer marks a formula as dynamic-array (`cm="1"` + `xl/metadata.xml` `XLDAPR`) only when the formula **spills**. A formula that returns a single value but relies on array evaluation of ranges is written without the marker, so Excel loads it as a pre-dynamic-array formula and applies implicit intersection, which changes its result.

## Repro

`Data!A1:A20` and `Data!B1:B20` hold numbers; on another sheet, in row 107:

```
=SUM(Data!A1:A20*Data!B1:B20)
```

- GridCraft: `165321.5` (array evaluation, which is what Excel 365 gives when the formula is typed in)
- Same file opened and fully recalculated in Excel: `#VALUE!`, i.e. Excel treats it as a legacy formula, as if written `=SUM(@Data!A1:A20*@Data!B1:B20)`

Written XML:

```xml
<c r="B107"><f>SUM(Data!A1:A20*Data!B1:B20)</f>...
```

So the same workbook gives different numbers in GridCraft and in Excel after a round trip. Formulas whose array-ness comes from a "new" function (`SUM(FILTER(...))`, `ROWS(UNIQUE(...))`) or from `SUMPRODUCT` / `INDEX(...,0)` are fine; the problem is ordinary operators or functions applied to ranges where a scalar is expected.

## Where

`crates/xlsx/src/sheet_write.rs`, `write_cell`: `cm="1"` is written only when `dynamic.is_some()` (a spill range exists). As far as I can tell Excel 365 marks any formula whose legacy evaluation would differ (one that would need an `@` in an older Excel), not only spilling ones.

## The reading side

The converse also seems to hold: a formula in an Excel-authored file **without** `cm` is a legacy formula, and Excel evaluates it with implicit intersection. GridCraft evaluates it with array semantics, so on such files GridCraft will show `165321.5` where Excel shows `#VALUE!` (or a different scalar, when the range intersects the formula's row/column). Possibly the reader should keep a "legacy" flag (or insert `@`) for formulas without `cm`.

## Environment

GridCraft `51b531b` (main), Excel for Mac 16.113.2, macOS 26.3. Found while dif…

title: Add a System theme option that follows the macOS light/dark appearance
author: coygeek
body:
## Summary

Add a System choice to GridCraft's interface theme setting that follows the macOS light/dark appearance live, so the app changes with the rest of the desktop when macOS switches appearance automatically.

## Problem to solve

macOS can switch between Light and Dark appearance automatically (System Settings → Appearance → Auto changes it at sunset and sunrise), and many Mac apps offer a "System" theme choice that tracks it.

GridCraft offers only a manual dark-mode switch. `UiState.dark` in `crates/ui-egui/src/lib.rs` is a boolean defaulting to light and persisted in `ui.json`. Users change it with the View ribbon checkbox "Dark Mode" or the macOS menu View → Dark Mode. Each frame the app reapplies its saved light/dark visuals, so OS appearance changes never reach the interface.

Because GridCraft only has manual choices, a user whose macOS appearance switches automatically has to change the app theme by hand at least twice a day, or leave it mismatched with every other app.

## Proposed behavior

Add System to the existing theme choice. With System selected, the app applies a light theme while macOS is in Light mode and a dark theme while it is in Dark mode, both at launch and immediately when the OS appearance changes while the app is open. The saved choice stays System; only the displayed theme changes. The existing manual choices keep working as they do today.

## Acceptance criteria

1. The theme control offers a System choice (for example "System" or "Use system setting") alongside the existing manual choices, and every place that exposes the theme (the View ribbon and the macOS View menu) shows it.
2. With System selected, the app starts in its light theme when macOS is set to Light and in its dark theme when macOS is set to Dark.
3. With System selected and the app running, changing the macOS appearance, including the scheduled change made by macOS Appearance "Auto", switches the whole interface (panels, menus, dialogs and custom-painted surfaces)…

title: Bug: Key navigation focus reverts to initial click coordinates on Enter
author: onemannoplan
body:
**Description**

When navigating the grid using the keyboard, pressing Enter on a cell updates focus down as expected, but pressing Enter on a subsequent cell causes the focus to bounce back to the cell originally selected via mouse click.
Steps to Reproduce

    Click on a cell (e.g., A1) with the mouse.

    Press Enter to move focus down to A2.

    Press Enter again on A2.

**Expected Behavior**

Focus should move down sequentially to A3 (and continue relative to the active cell position).

**Actual Behavior**

Focus resets back to A1 (the cell where the mouse pointer originally clicked).

**Root Cause Hypothesis**

The keyboard navigation handler updates the visual focus buffer, but does not commit/synchronize the active cell indices back to the primary selection anchor state. On subsequent edit actions or re-renders, the component falls back to the original mouse click coordinates.

title: Feature Request / Bug: Double-clicking column header dividers does not auto-fit column width
author: onemannoplan
body:
**Summary**

In standard spreadsheet software (Excel, Google Sheets, LibreOffice Calc), double-clicking the resize handle/divider line between column headers automatically adjusts the column width to fit the longest cell content in that column. In gridCraft, double-clicking this divider line performs no action.
Steps to Reproduce / Observed Behavior

    Enter text into a cell that exceeds the visual width of its column (e.g., column A).

    Hover over the vertical divider line between column headers A and B.

    Double-click the header divider line.

    Result: Nothing happens; the column width remains unchanged.

**Expected Behavior**

Double-clicking the column header divider should calculate the maximum rendered width of all populated cells in that column (plus padding) and resize the column to fit that content.

**Suggested Implementation Notes**

    Event Handling: Add a double-click event handler (OnDoubleClick or GtkGestureClick with n_presses == 2) on the column header separator hitboxes.

    Width Calculation: Iterate over the active rows for that column, calculate the required text rendering width for the longest entry using the canvas font metrics, add cell padding (e.g., 8–12px), and update the column's width property in grid_state.

title: Crash on startup on Windows with Intel UHD Graphics (Access Violation 0xc0000005 in igvk64.dll)
author: quantavil
body:
### Description
  IN Windows machines with Intel UHD Graphics, GridCraft (v0.4.0) crashes silently within milliseconds of launch
  without rendering a window.

    The crash occurs because `wgpu` queries available Vulkan physical devices during initialization, triggering a
  known access violation in Intel's Vulkan driver (`igvk64.dll`).

    ### Environment
    * **GridCraft Version:** `0.4.0` (both `gridcraft-0.4.0-windows-x64.msi` and portable `.zip`)
    * **Operating System:** Windows 10 / 11 (x86_64)
    * **GPU:** Intel(R) UHD Graphics 630
    * **Driver Version:** `31.0.101.1999`
    * **Faulting Module:** `igvk64.dll` (Vulkan ICD driver)

    ### Steps to Reproduce
    1. Install GridCraft v0.4.0 using `gridcraft-0.4.0-windows-x64.msi` (or run portable `gridcraft.exe`) on a system
  with Intel UHD graphics running driver `31.0.101.1999`.
    2. Launch `gridcraft.exe`.
    3. The process exits almost immediately with no UI window or visible error dialog.

    ### Crash Logs (Windows Application Event Log)
    ```text
    Faulting application name: gridcraft.exe, version: 0.4.0.0, time stamp: 0x6ac995f7
    Faulting module name: igvk64.dll, version: 31.0.101.1999, time stamp: 0x62968a74
    Exception code: 0xc0000005
    Fault offset: 0x0000000000636952
    Faulting application path: C:\Program Files\GridCraft\gridcraft.exe
    Faulting module path: C:\WINDOWS\System32\DriverStore\FileRepository\iigd_dch.inf_amd64_6cad38383965216e\igvk64.
  dll
  (Note: The identical crash occurs with wordcraft.exe v0.3.0).
  ──────
  ### Current Workaround
  Setting the WGPU_BACKEND environment variable to dx12 completely resolves the crash:

    # Temporary (current session)
    $env:WGPU_BACKEND = "dx12"
    .\gridcraft.exe

    # Permanent (User environment)
    [System.Environment]::SetEnvironmentVariable('WGPU_BACKEND', 'dx12', 'User')

  Once WGPU_BACKEND=dx12 is set, GridCraft opens and functions smoothly using Direct3D 12.

title: Recalculation is quadratic in range formulas: large sheets take minutes to open or edit
author: LloydNicholson
body:
Recalculation time grows quadratically with the number of range formulas, so large sheets take minutes to open or edit. The values are correct; only the time is affected.

**Repro:** a sheet with `=SUM(E{r}:J{r})` on every row (no real data needed; any numbers in E:J).

| Rows | Headless open + recalc |
|---|---|
| 12.5k | 0.4 s |
| 25k | 1.5 s |
| 50k | 8.6 s |

A 50k-row × 20-column workbook takes about 65 s to open in the app. Editing a cell that 100k formulas depend on freezes the UI for about 30 s. Filling 50k formulas down takes over a minute.

**Expected:** roughly linear time; Excel opens these in about a second.

**Cause** (profiled):
- `Evaluator::trim` calls `Sheet::used_range` on every range read, and that walks every stored row, so a full recalc costs rows × range formulas.
- `Graph::dependents` scans each column's whole list of range precedents, and removing a formula runs a `retain` over it (`crates/calc/src/recalc.rs`), which makes fill, paste and sort quadratic.

**Environment:** macOS 26.6.2 arm64, gridcraft `main` @ 51b531b (0.3.0).

Fix in #66.

title: SUMIF/AVERAGEIF with a smaller sum_range give wrong totals
author: LloydNicholson
body:
`SUMIF` / `AVERAGEIF` with a sum range smaller than the criteria range give wrong totals. Excel uses a range that starts at sum_range's top-left cell and has the criteria range's size; GridCraft only uses the cells actually given.

**Repro:** A1:B3 = `a, 1` / `b, 2` / `a, 3`.

| Formula | Expected (Excel) | Actual |
|---|---|---|
| `=SUMIF(A1:A3,"a",B1)` | 4 | 1 |
| `=AVERAGEIF(A1:A3,"a",B1)` | 2 | 1 |
| `=SUMIF(A1:A3,"a",B1:B2)` | 4 | 1 |

**Cause:** `if_numbers` (`crates/functions/src/math.rs`) gets the sum range's values, not its reference, so it can't resize. Its comment says it does.

**Environment:** macOS 26.6.2 arm64, gridcraft `main` @ 51b531b (0.3.0).

Fix in #67.

title: DATE(1900,2,29) returns 61 instead of 60
author: LloydNicholson
body:
In the 1900 date system, Excel (following Lotus 1-2-3) keeps 29 February 1900 as serial 60, and `DAY(60)` already returns 29. But turning that date back into a serial gives a different number:

| Formula | Expected (Excel) | Actual |
|---|---|---|
| `=DATE(1900,2,29)` | 60 | 61 |
| `=DATEVALUE("2/29/1900")` | 60 | 61 |
| `=DATE(1900,3,0)` | 60 | 59 |
| `=EOMONTH(60,0)` | 60 | 59 (before its own input) |

Typing `2/29/1900` into a cell also stores 61.

**Cause:** `serial_from_ymd` (`crates/core/src/date.rs`) works out the real calendar date (1 March) and then shifts serials up to 60, so it can never produce 60.

Only dates in January–February 1900 are affected.

**Environment:** macOS 26.6.2 arm64, gridcraft `main` @ 51b531b (0.3.0).

Fix in #68.

title: fix(csv): re-importing a single-column export splits semicolon and tab text
author: coygeek
body:
## Summary

GridCraft can change two ordinary text cells when a user exports a one-column workbook to CSV and opens that export again. An unquoted semicolon or tab inside the first cell becomes a column separator, so the original value moves into two cells without an import warning. This report concerns CSV produced by GridCraft from a known one-column workbook.

## Steps to reproduce

Use the source-built CLI from the baseline in Runtime or environment, available as `gridcraft-cli` on PATH. Run the following script with Python 3. It creates disposable synthetic workbooks, exports them, imports the exports into new XLSX files, and inspects each result in fresh CLI processes. These operations were executed for both values.

```sh
python3 - <<'PY'
import json
import shutil
import subprocess
import tempfile
from pathlib import Path

cli = shutil.which('gridcraft-cli')
assert cli, 'Put the source-built gridcraft-cli on PATH'
work = Path(tempfile.mkdtemp(prefix='gridcraft-csv-'))

def run(*args):
    result = subprocess.run([cli, *args], cwd=work, text=True,
                            capture_output=True, timeout=60, check=True)
    return result.stdout

author: Jagalite
body:
**Environment**

- macOS on Apple Silicon; unmodified official GridCraft v0.4.0 web archive, locally served. Archive SHA-256 `83e2c336a2fdec055a27ddf1235f31f6db2594ba60f529533162fb214deebdd3`.
- T3 Code collaborative browser, Electron 44.4.2 / Chromium 152.0.7977.130; matching source-built native CLI control.

**Steps to reproduce**

1. Open a valid owned XLSX through the production Open action. This workbook has `Owned PRINT-A` in A1, `Owned PRINT-B` in A20, and print area `Sheet1!$A$1:$B$5`.
2. Click the top-right command-search icon and type `Export as PDF`.
3. Click the enabled `Export as PDF` result, labelled `File > Export`.
4. Observe the editor and browser file delivery. Repeat on a fresh page with the same valid workbook. In the repeat, observe for at least 35 seconds.
5. Press Command+S as a healthy browser delivery control.

**Expected**

The enabled PDF export action initiates a PDF download or another supported file-delivery route. If unavailable, it reports that clearly.

**Actual**

Both runs close the search palette and return to the unchanged workbook without a file picker, PDF download or explanatory feedback. title: macOS: workbook opened from Finder shows a format error and freezes the app
author: DDKatch
body:
## What happens

GridCraft is the default app for `.xlsx`. The user double-clicks a workbook in Finder.

- macOS shows an alert: *"GridCraft cannot open files in the 'Excel Workbook' format."*
- The alert is modal. The app never creates its first window, so it looks frozen.
- Dock-icon reopen (clicking the Dock icon while the app runs with no windows) does nothing.

Both reproduce with `open -a GridCraft.app workbook.xlsx`.

## Cause

Two layers.

1. **winit 0.30 handles no Apple Events.** The `odoc` event ("open documents") reaches the Apple Event Manager and finds no handler, so macOS runs its built-in document handler. That path ends in `NSDocumentController`, which cannot open a workbook and shows the alert.
2. **The launch case is worse.** On current macOS, documents passed at launch never reach `NSAppleEventManager` at all. LaunchServices hands them to AppKit, AppKit asks the app delegate to answer `application:openURLs:` (and the `openFiles:` / `openFile:` variants), and with no answer falls back to `NSDocumentController` — the same modal alert, this time before the first frame exists.

Because of layer 2, registering an `NSAppleEventManager` handler early cannot fix Finder opens: the event never arrives there. (An early registration alone also does not survive AppKit installing its own default handlers at `finishLaunching`.)

## Fix

New crate `gridcraft-macos-events` (PR to follow):

- Adds `application:openURLs:`, `application:openFiles:`, `application:openFile:` and `applicationShouldHandleReopen:` to `NSObject`, process-local. winit's delegate inherits them, so launch-time and running-instance opens land in the crate's queue.
- Registers `NSAppleEventManager` handlers for `odoc` / `rapp` as a second path (AppleScript, and `open` targeting a running instance).
- The app polls the queue each frame and opens the paths; Dock reopen opens the last workbook when no document is open.

The crate is the repository's single `unsafe` module: the Apple Event and del…

title: Calc engine at Excel scale: topological scheduler, lookup index, multi-threaded recalc
author: arhammusheer
body:
I'd like to take on calc performance and scaling, in five reviewable PRs. I'm posting the plan first so it doesn't collide with other work in `crates/calc`. If you're already changing the recalc scheduler or range evaluation, please say so here and we can split the work.

## Where it stands (upstream `main` at 90b3c41, Apple M2 Pro, release build)

I measured these with an extended `crates/engine/examples/perf.rs`, which comes with the first PR. Every scenario runs through `Session::execute` and checks its answer.

| Scenario | Time |
|---|---|
| 10k exact VLOOKUPs over a 10k-row table | 2.6 s |
| 10k XLOOKUPs / 10k MATCHes | 3.2 s / 2.1 s |
| Edit one table cell with 30k dependent lookups | 5.8 s |
| 1,000 × `SUM(A:A)` over 50k rows, then one edit | 0.65 s / 0.65 s |
| 20k-cell chain where each cell reads the one below it | wrong result: `#CIRC!` |

Lookups scale as O(n²): every range read copies the range (`range_values` returns a fresh `Vec<Value>`), and every exact match then scans it. The reverse chain fails because `PassHost::compute` treats recursion depth above 2,000 as a cycle (`recalc.rs`, `self.depth > 2000`). The same recursion overflows the stack and aborts the process with heavier formulas at around 1,000 cells, and `catch_unwind` can't catch a stack overflow.

## Plan

1. **Topological scheduler.** Order the dirty set with Kahn's algorithm over the existing graph, and evaluate it iteratively. Only real cycles become circular. On-demand evaluation stays for dynamic references (INDIRECT, OFFSET). Reverse chains become correct, the depth limit and the stack overflow go away, and we get dependency levels for step 3.
2. **Shared ranges and a lookup index.** Materialise each distinct range once per pass and share it. Build an exact-match hash index or sorted index once per lookup range and reuse it, as Excel 365 does for VLOOKUP/MATCH. Target: 100k lookups in about 1 s.
3. **Multi-threaded recalculation.** Evaluate each dependency level on N threads, with t…

## Summary

Help a person connect an agent to GridCraft from the desktop app, with a checked CLI invocation and usable MCP configuration.

## Problem to solve

A desktop installation does not tell the user whether an agent can find the CLI, initialize MCP, or reach the open workbook. macOS distributes the CLI separately. Windows and Linux package it in different locations, sometimes inside a portable or container package. Copying a bare executable name leaves those differences unresolved.

## Proposed behavior

Extend the existing Agent Control entry. The [current dialog](https://github.com/storytold/gridcraft/blob/90b3c41eec691797129303603d4073269aebab73/crates/ui-egui/src/dialogs.rs#L685-L690) already shows headless and connected MCP commands.

Locate CLI candidates, show the selected command and version, and allow another installation. If none works, offer a matching official platform and release download or installation route. Check the resulting command before using it. Support today's separate CLI downloads independently of improvements to desktop packaging.

Explain headless MCP as a separate session and connected MCP as access to the running app. Produce client-ready configuration or a registration command with the actual executable path or wrapper arguments. Identify the connected target and explain launch or authorization prerequisites.

Offer a local check that starts the selected command, initializes MCP, and discovers tools without editing the workbook. Show client registration separately through instructions or an explicit action. A successful local check cannot establish registration in an external client.

## Acceptance criteria

title: feat(distribution): provide reliable CLI access with desktop packages
author: coygeek
body:
## Summary

Give desktop installations of GridCraft a documented CLI invocation that people, scripts, and agents can use on Windows, Linux, and macOS.

## Problem to solve

Including a CLI executable in a package does not always make a shell command available. Windows installs the CLI beside the app; Linux native packages install it in `/usr/bin`, while AppImage and Flatpak keep it inside their package. macOS publishes a separate CLI download. Users need a supported invocation that matches their desktop installation without guessing its location or modifying global settings.

## Proposed behavior

Provide a callable CLI with each desktop distribution or an integrated installation route where needed, and document the exact invocation outside the agent setup UI. Preserve the existing CLI commands and MCP subcommand.

For Windows MSI, document full-path invocation of the installed CLI and make any shell exposure an explicit choice. Portable ZIP users can run its included executable without a global installation. For Linux DEB/RPM, preserve the existing `/usr/bin` CLI. Provide supported AppImage and Flatpak invocation through a wrapper or command override with the required arguments. For macOS, supply a compatible CLI with the desktop distribution or through its integrated installation route so users need not manually coordinate another download.

Define update, relocation, and removal behavior for each advertised invocation. Managed launchers must not become stale or overwrite a separately installed CLI. Keep the standalone CLI download supported for users who do not want the GUI.

## Acceptance criteria

- Linux tarball users can invoke the extracted CLI using the advertised path or optional installation procedure without building from source.
- A fresh Windows MSI installation has a documented full-path command that reports its matching CLI version. A fresh portable ZIP works from its extracted directory, including paths with spaces.
- Fresh Linux DEB/RPM installatio…

author: musaad-sharikh
body:
Arabic text in GridCraft's own interface (the workbook name in the title bar, sheet tab names) is drawn in DejaVu Sans, whatever Arabic fonts are installed. This is about the **interface font**, not the cell fonts covered by #4 / #9.

### Steps to reproduce

1. Install the GridCraft 0.3.0 Flatpak bundle from the GitHub release on a Linux desktop that has an Arabic UI font (for example Vazirmatn) installed in `~/.local/share/fonts` and set as the fontconfig default for Arabic.
2. Open a workbook whose file name is Arabic, or rename a sheet to an Arabic name.
3. Look at the title bar and the sheet tabs.

### Actual

The Arabic text is rendered in DejaVu Sans from the Flatpak runtime.

### Expected

The interface uses an Arabic-capable font the user has installed, or offers a setting to choose the interface font.

### Environment

- GridCraft 0.3.0, Flatpak bundle (`org.freedesktop.Platform` 25.08), x86_64
- Linux, Wayland session
- CachyOS Linux
- niri (Wayland compositor)
- Also present in `main` at `9f896c1`: the UI candidate list is unchanged

- `candidates("ui")` / `candidates("ui-bold")` in `crates/ui-egui/src/theme.rs` probe a fixed list of files under `/usr/share/fonts` and `/usr/local/share/fonts` (Cantarell, Noto Sans, DejaVu Sans, Liberation Sans). Fontconfig and the user font directories (`~/.local/share/fonts`, `$XDG_DATA_HOME/fonts`) are never consulted.
- Inside the Flatpak sandbox `/usr/share/fonts` is the runtime's, and the only candidate that exists there is `dejavu/DejaVuSans.ttf` (plus `DejaVuSans-Bold.ttf`). Watching file opens at startup shows only the runtime's DejaVu files being read, and nothing from the user font directory.

title: Add an interface scale / UI font size setting

gridcraft-cli run \
  --cmd 'range.setValues={"range":"A1","values":[[1],[2],[3],[4],[5]]}' \

**Actual**

```xml
<conditionalFormatting sqref="A1:A5"><cfRule type="iconSet" priority="1"><iconSet iconSet="3Arrows"></iconSet></cfRule></conditionalFormatting>

title: Feature request: AutoSave with pluggable storage (local folder, Google Drive, OneDrive, S3/R2 via rclone), version history, and a path to self-hosted co-editing
author: fernandodilland
body:
## TL;DR

In Excel, AutoSave, Version History and co-authoring only work when the file lives on OneDrive/SharePoint. ROADMAP.md says features that need Microsoft cloud services (e.g. co-authoring through OneDrive) will be replaced by open equivalents or left out. This issue proposes that open equivalent: a single, central **"Save target"** setting so a workbook can autosave to storage the user owns (local/NAS folder, Google Drive, OneDrive, S3-compatible such as Cloudflare R2, or anything rclone supports), with automatic version history, a lease/lock file to prevent overwrites, and an optional later phase for real-time co-editing (P2P or relay).

Principles: local-first, opt-in, no GridCraft-run servers, no telemetry, never lose data.

## Why

- Saving automatically is core to spreadsheet work. The "never crash / don't lose people's numbers" rule (AGENTS.md) and the alpha gate "autosave/recovery check" (ROADMAP) point the same way.

title: fix(macos): shipped DMG app fails strict signature verification with FinderInfo metadata
author: coygeek
body:
## Summary

The official GridCraft macOS DMG contains an app that fails `codesign --verify --deep --strict`, both inside the mounted image and after copying it with `ditto`. Removing only `com.apple.FinderInfo` from the disposable copied app restores strict verification, and Gatekeeper then accepts it as `Notarized Developer ID`. This affects package verification; I did not test or establish a GUI launch failure.

## Runtime or environment

- Tested release: [v0.5.0](https://github.com/storytold/gridcraft/releases/tag/v0.5.0), the latest published release at this check.
- Artifact: `gridcraft-0.5.0-macos-universal.dmg`.
- SHA-256: `e372170ad95a7625e37b315b168d8be2a5d2547de6de252f838e81bb7de98513`. The fresh download matched both the release asset digest and the published `SHA256SUMS.txt` entry.
- Host: macOS 27.0.1, build 26A434, Apple silicon, `arm64`.
- Source inspection: current default branch `main`. Its macOS packaging script is byte-identical to the script at the tested release tag. This was an isolated test of the published binary, not a source rebuild.

## Steps to reproduce

Download the official artifact into a disposable directory and mount it read-only. These steps were executed on the measured host with a fresh download:

```sh
work=$(mktemp -d /tmp/craft-dmg.XXXXXX)
curl -fL 'https://github.com/storytold/gridcraft/releases/download/v0.5.0/gridcraft-0.5.0-macos-universal.dmg' -o "$work/release.dmg"
shasum -a 256 "$work/release.dmg"
```

Confirm that the checksum matches the value above, then mount and check the app:

```sh

hdiutil attach -readonly -nobrowse -mountpoint "$work/mount" "$work/release.dmg"
codesign --verify --deep --strict "$work/mount/GridCraft.app"
xattr -l "$work/mount/GridCraft.app"
ditto "$work/mount/GridCraft.app" "$work/GridCraft.app"
codesign --verify --deep --strict "$work/GridCraft.app"

```

title: [Bug] Formatted tables do not automatically expand when entering adjacent data
author: AlissonFA
body:
### Problem Description
    
When working with formatted tables (`ListObject`), entering data into cells directly adjacent to the table (in the row immediately below or the column immediately to the right) does not expand the table boundaries.
    
In other programs, tables are designed to automatically grow as data is entered, maintaining data integrity by extending calculated columns, cell formatting, and validation rules. In GridCraft, entries in adjacent cells remain plain disconnected cells outside the table, requiring manual resizing and manual formula copying.
    
### Steps to Reproduce
    
1. Create a table with headers and data (e.g., in range `A1:C3`), where column `C` contains a formula (e.g., `=A2*B2`).
2. Type a value into cell `A4` (the row immediately below the table).
3. Observe the table boundaries and the cells in row 4.
4. Alternatively, type a value into cell `D2` (the column immediately to the right of the table).
    
### Expected Behavior
    
- **Row Expansion:** Typing in the row immediately below the table should automatically expand the table range to encompass the new row.
- Calculated column formulas should automatically propagate to the new row with relative references adjusted.
- Column number formatting, styles, and data validation rules should be inherited by the expanding row.
- **Column Expansion:** Typing in the column immediately to the right of the table should automatically add a new column to the table, creating a unique header if necessary.

### Actual Behavior

- The value is treated as a regular cell outside the table.
- The table's range remains unchanged (`A1:C3`).
- Formulas, data validation rules, and formats from the table are not propagated.
- The user must manually resize the table and manually copy down formulas.

title: Let an end user add a font without rebuilding
author: tonguyenducmanh
body:
## Ask

Let an end user add a font without rebuilding:

- **Paste a link** — Google Fonts `/css2?family=…`, any stylesheet with `@font-face`, or a direct
  `.ttf` / `.otf` / `.woff2` URL.
- **Upload a file** — drag-drop or picker.

On the web this is currently blocked at the source: there are no system fonts, nothing is bundled
beyond egui's Latin defaults, and changing it means a source edit.

## Current behaviour

GridCraft has the least font machinery of the four, which cuts both ways — more to build, but less
to integrate around.

- No `fonts` crate, no `craft-fonts` wiring.
- `crates/ui-egui/src/theme.rs` reads **system** font files from hardcoded `/usr/share/fonts/…`
  paths — on wasm there's nothing to read.
- The web shell avoids the problem rather than solving it:

  ```rust
  // apps/gridcraft-web/src/web.rs
  // Follow the browser's language, except a CJK one: the web build has no system
  // CJK fonts (none are bundled), so that interface would render as tofu.
  let browser = gridcraft_ui_egui::i18n::Language::system();
  if !matches!(browser, Language::Zh | Language::Ja | Language::Ko) {
      app.ui.language = browser;
  }
  ```

## Why this one matters most

`localization` is last on ROADMAP.md at 100–165 h, and much of that is presumably font coverage — a
spreadsheet UI can't localise into scripts it can't render. A user-installed font doesn't get
GridCraft to full localisation, but it does unblock the individual user immediately. Someone who
needs Japanese sheet names today simply can't use the app.

## Suggestion

If the full version is too big for the current milestone, a minimal one would be
`font.install_file` only (drop the URL path). `photocraft-web`'s `indexed_presets.rs` is a good
reference for the IndexedDB bridge — `MAX_STORE_BYTES`, the single whole-read deadline, and the RAII
`Listeners` that detach handlers on timeout.

## Why this fits

Four entries in the `CommandSpec` registry, and the web UI, CLI, MCP surface and JSON control
channe…

title: Parity: XLSX › threaded comments and persons parts round trip

- Read and keep the `dT` timestamps, and read note visibility from the VML shapes.

title: Parity: XLSX › keep unmodelled parts on save (pass-through)
author: vangel76
body:
`docs/gaps.md` §3: content GridCraft doesn't model is dropped when an `.xlsx` is opened and saved (custom XML, external links, connections and query tables, form controls, OLE objects, slicers, timelines, data model). Open, edit, save silently simplifies colleagues' workbooks.

Plan (pass-through, in a separate module of `crates/xlsx`):
- On read, keep the raw bytes of unmodelled parts with their content type and relationship graph (owner part → rel id → type → target, followed transitively, external targets kept as text and never opened), per owner: package root (custom properties, custom UI), workbook (customXml, externalLinks + `<externalReferences>`, connections) and sheet (query tables, form controls, ActiveX, OLE embeddings + the sheet's `<oleObjects>` / `<controls>` XML and their legacy VML shapes).
- On write, re-attach them under fresh part names with new relationship ids, rewriting the `r:id`s in the kept XML fragments; content types emitted as overrides.
- Conservative: anything whose relationship graph reaches a part GridCraft rewrites (worksheets, drawings, charts, tables, pivots…) is not kept; sheet-level content goes away with its sheet and is not duplicated by Copy Sheet. Size caps and hostile-input tests.
- VBA is left to #19; slicers/timelines/data model only if they can be kept consistently (they depend on pivot caches and drawings GridCraft rewrites).

title: [Windows] 0.5.0 exits at startup: DXC runtime (dxcompiler.dll + dxil.dll) not shipped -> "Parent device is lost"
author: engmgs
body:
**gridcraft 0.5.0 (portable x64 zip and MSI, 2026-10-07 release) exits ~0.1 s after the window appears (exit code 1)** on Windows 11 Pro 10.0.26100, NVIDIA GeForce RTX 4090 (driver 32.0.16.1088), DirectX 12 default backend.

Same root cause as storytold/craft-launcher#126 (opened the same day) and storytold/lightcraft#471 (fixed there by #484). Of the twelve Craft apps installed on this machine the same log appears in cadcraft 0.5.0, wordcraft 0.5.0, deckcraft 0.5.0, soundcraft 0.5.0, vectorcraft 0.9.0; photocraft, filmcraft, lightcraft, pdfcraft, effectcraft and designcraft tolerate it.

**Log** (`%APPDATA%\GridCraft\logs\gridcraft.log`, identical every start):
```
ERROR [main] wgpu_core::indirect_validation: indirect-validation error: ComputePipeline(Internal("DXC compile error: warning: DXIL signing library (dxil.dll,libdxil.so) not found.  Resulting DXIL will not be signed for use in release environments.\r\n\n"))
WARN  [main] gpu_allocator::allocator::free_list_allocator: leak detected: { ... (wgpu internal) zero init buffer ... }
ERROR [main] eframe::native::run: Exiting because of error: WGPU error: Parent device is lost
Error: Wgpu(RequestDeviceError(RequestDeviceError { inner: Core(Device(Lost)) }))
```

**Cause**: the build uses DXC for DX12 shader compilation (the wgpu `indirect_validation` compute pipeline) but ships neither `dxcompiler.dll` nor `dxil.dll`. The unsigned-DXIL warning is treated as a compile error, the pipeline fails, and the device is lost before the first frame.

**What I verified**
1. `WGPU_BACKEND=vulkan` -> starts (as the cadcraft README troubleshooting section says).
2. A **matched** `dxcompiler.dll` + `dxil.dll` pair next to `<app>.exe` -> starts on DX12 from a plain double-click, no env var. Pair used: the one shipped with Microsoft Edge 154.0.4258.62.
3. `dxil.dll` alone (Chrome 154's copy) is **not** enough: `DXC compile error: error: validation errors / DXIL container mismatch for 'PSVRuntimeInfoSize' between 'PSV0' part:('48') …

title: [Bug] Resizing multiple Ctrl-selected rows or columns only affects the last selected item
author: aaronholoday
body:
**Description**

When multiple rows or columns are selected using Ctrl+click, resizing only affects the most recently selected row or column.

Resizing works for individual rows or columns and for an entire sheet selection, but not for a selection containing more than one and fewer than all rows or columns.

**Steps to reproduce**

1. Open a worksheet in Gridcraft.
2. Click the header for column B.
3. Hold Ctrl and click the headers for columns D and F, leaving B, D, and F selected.
4. Resize column F using its header boundary.
5. Observe which columns change width.
6. Repeat the same process with nonadjacent rows to test row height.

**Expected behavior**

All selected columns should receive the new width, while unselected columns remain unchanged. In this example, columns B, D, and F should resize together; columns A, C, E, and all other unselected columns should retain their existing widths.

The same behavior should apply to row heights: resizing one selected row should apply the new height to all selected rows, without affecting unselected rows.

This would provide parity with Excel’s handling of multiple selected rows and columns.

**Actual behavior**

Only the most recently selected column or row is resized. Other selected columns or rows retain their previous dimensions.

**Impact**

Users must resize each row or column individually to give a selected subset consistent dimensions, making worksheet formatting unnecessarily repetitive.

**Tested on Version 0.5.0 on CachyOS**

title: Feature request: German-localized formula function names and separators
author: ScottGri
body:
## Summary

Thanks for adding the German interface language and Spanish formula localization (#45)! Could the same formula localization be added for German?

German Excel and LibreOffice users are used to German function names, `;` as the argument separator and `,` as the decimal separator. Right now GridCraft only accepts English syntax, so `=SUMME(A1;A3)` fails with "expected `,` or `)`, found Semicolon".

## Requested functionality

When the interface language is German, accept and display German function names, keeping English as the canonical/stored syntax (as with `FormulaLocale::Es`).

| German | English |
|---|---|
| `=SUMME(A1:A10)` | `=SUM(A1:A10)` |
| `=MITTELWERT(A1:A10)` | `=AVERAGE(A1:A10)` |
| `=WENN(A1>0;"Ja";"Nein")` | `=IF(A1>0,"Ja","Nein")` |
| `=ANZAHL(A1:A10)` | `=COUNT(A1:A10)` |
| `=SUMMEWENN(A1:A10;">0")` | `=SUMIF(A1:A10,">0")` |
| `=ZÄHLENWENN(A1:A10;">0")` | `=COUNTIF(A1:A10,">0")` |
| `=SVERWEIS(A2;D:E;2;FALSCH)` | `=VLOOKUP(A2,D:E,2,FALSE)` |
| `=XVERWEIS(...)` | `=XLOOKUP(...)` |
| `=RUNDEN(A1;2)` | `=ROUND(A1,2)` |
| `=HEUTE()` | `=TODAY()` |
| `WAHR` / `FALSCH` | `TRUE` / `FALSE` |

## Separators

- `;` as argument separator
- `,` as decimal separator (e.g. `=A1*1,5`)
- Array constants would probably also need German-Excel-compatible separators.

## Context

Tested on GridCraft 0.5.0 (Linux AppImage). The formula engine itself is great: everything from IFNA up to LAMBDA and REGEXTEST worked in English syntax.

title: VLOOKUP/XLOOKUP/LOOKUP return 0 instead of blank for an empty target cell (ISBLANK FALSE, concatenation inserts 0)
author: rex4539
body:
## Summary

When `VLOOKUP`, `XLOOKUP` or `LOOKUP` lands on an **empty** cell, GridCraft returns the number `0`. Excel returns a blank, so `ISBLANK()` of the result is `TRUE` and string concatenation treats it as `""`. In GridCraft `ISBLANK()` gives `FALSE` and concatenation inserts a literal `0`.

`INDEX`, `OFFSET` and `IF` returning an empty cell already behave like Excel, so the gap is specific to the lookup functions.

This breaks a common template pattern, `IF(ISBLANK(VLOOKUP(...)),"",VLOOKUP(...)&"...")`. In GridCraft every row whose lookup column is empty produces `"0..."` text instead of an empty string.

## Steps to reproduce

```python
# uv run --with openpyxl make.py
import openpyxl
wb = openpyxl.Workbook(); ws = wb.active
ws["A1"] = "k"; ws["A2"] = "j"; ws["B2"] = "v"   # B1 (the value for key "k") is empty
for i, f in enumerate([
    '=ISBLANK(VLOOKUP("k",A1:B2,2,0))',
    '="x"&VLOOKUP("k",A1:B2,2,0)&"y"',
    '=CONCATENATE("x",VLOOKUP("k",A1:B2,2,0),"y")',
    '=ISBLANK(XLOOKUP("k",A1:A2,B1:B2))',
    '="x"&XLOOKUP("k",A1:A2,B1:B2)&"y"',
    '=ISBLANK(LOOKUP("k",A1:A1,B1:B1))',
    '=ISBLANK(INDEX(B1:B2,1))',
    '=ISBLANK(IF(TRUE,B1))',
], 1):
    ws.cell(i, 4, f)
wb.save("blank_lookup.xlsx")
```

```
gridcraft-cli run --in blank_lookup.xlsx --cmd 'formulas.calculateNow={}' --print D1:D8
```

## Expected (Excel for Mac 16.78)

| Cell | Formula | Excel |
|---|---|---|
| D1 | `ISBLANK(VLOOKUP(...))` | `TRUE` |
| D2 | `"x"&VLOOKUP(...)&"y"` | `xy` |
| D3 | `CONCATENATE("x",VLOOKUP(...),"y")` | `xy` |
| D4 | `ISBLANK(XLOOKUP(...))` | `TRUE` |
| D5 | `"x"&XLOOKUP(...)&"y"` | `xy` |
| D6 | `ISBLANK(LOOKUP(...))` | `TRUE` |
| D7 | `ISBLANK(INDEX(...))` | `TRUE` |
| D8 | `ISBLANK(IF(TRUE,B1))` | `TRUE` |

A bare `=VLOOKUP("k",A1:B2,2,0)` still *displays* `0` in Excel. Only the value's blankness differs.

## Actual (GridCraft 0.5.0)

D1 `FALSE`, D2 `x0y`, D3 `x0y`, D4 `FALSE`, D5 `x0y`, D6 `FALSE`. D7 and D8 are correct (`TRUE`).

The same results come from th…

title: shrinkToFit alignment is ignored: text spills or is clipped, numbers show ###
author: rex4539
body:
## Summary

GridCraft ignores the cell alignment flag `shrinkToFit="1"`. When content is too wide for its cell, Excel shrinks the font until it fits. GridCraft instead draws it at full size:

- **Text** spills into the next empty cell, or is clipped.
- **Centred text in a merged range** is clipped on both sides, so the start and end of the sentence are lost.
- **Numbers** show as `###`.

Form-style templates (schedules, reports, invoices) rely on shrink-to-fit heavily. A workbook that looks correct in Excel can then show truncated labels and `###` in a large share of its cells.

## Steps to reproduce

```python
# uv run --with openpyxl make.py
import openpyxl
from openpyxl.styles import Alignment
wb = openpyxl.Workbook(); ws = wb.active
ws.column_dimensions["A"].width = 10
ws.column_dimensions["B"].width = 5
ws["A1"] = "Executive Producer"; ws["A1"].alignment = Alignment(shrinkToFit=True)
ws["A2"] = "Executive Producer"                       # control: no shrinkToFit
ws.merge_cells("A4:D4")
ws["A4"] = "THIS CENTRED SENTENCE IS MUCH TOO LONG FOR THE MERGED RANGE A4:D4"
ws["A4"].alignment = Alignment(horizontal="center", shrinkToFit=True)
ws["B6"] = 0.0; ws["B6"].number_format = "h:mm:ss"
ws["B6"].alignment = Alignment(horizontal="center", shrinkToFit=True)
wb.save("shrink.xlsx")
```

Open `shrink.xlsx` in the GridCraft desktop app.

## Expected (Excel for Mac 16.78)

- A1 is drawn in a smaller font, fully inside column A. A2, the control, spills into B as normal.
- A4 is drawn in a smaller font, and the whole sentence fits inside A4:D4.
- B6 shows `0:00:00` in a smaller font.

## Actual (GridCraft 0.5.0)

- A1 is drawn exactly like A2, spilling into column B.
- A4 is drawn at full size and clipped on both sides, so only the middle of the sentence shows.
- B6 shows `###`.

## Environment

GridCraft 0.5.0 desktop app, macOS 15.8.2 x86_64. Reference: Microsoft Excel for Mac 16.78.

title: Merged range border: right and bottom edges are not drawn (only the anchor cell's border is used)
author: rex4539
body:
## Summary

When a merged range has a border around it, GridCraft draws only the **top and left** edges. The right and bottom edges are missing.

Excel stores a merged range's outline on the cells along each edge: the right border on the last column's cells and the bottom border on the last row's cells. GridCraft appears to take the merged cell's border only from the top-left (anchor) cell, which carries just `left` and `top`. So a boxed merged range renders as an open "Γ" shape.

## Steps to reproduce

```python
# uv run --with openpyxl make.py
import openpyxl
from openpyxl.styles import Alignment, Border, Font, Side
wb = openpyxl.Workbook(); ws = wb.active
t = Side(style="thick")
ws.merge_cells("B2:E5")
ws["B2"] = "13:00"
ws["B2"].font = Font(size=36, bold=True)
ws["B2"].alignment = Alignment(horizontal="center", vertical="center")
for r in range(2, 6):
    for c in range(2, 6):
        ws.cell(r, c).border = Border(left=t if c == 2 else None, right=t if c == 5 else None,
                                      top=t if r == 2 else None, bottom=t if r == 5 else None)
wb.save("merged_border.xlsx")
```

This is the layout Excel itself writes when you merge B2:E5 and apply "Thick Outside Borders". Open the file in the GridCraft desktop app.

## Expected (Excel for Mac 16.78)

A closed thick box around B2:E5.

## Actual (GridCraft 0.5.0)

Only the top and left thick edges are drawn. The right edge (column E) and the bottom edge (row 5) are missing.

## Environment

GridCraft 0.5.0 desktop app, macOS 15.8.2 x86_64. Reference: Microsoft Excel for Mac 16.78.

title: Text box formatting ignored: run size/bold/font/outline, centre alignment, vertical anchor and noFill outline
author: rex4539
body:
## Summary

Text boxes (`xdr:sp` with `txBox="1"`) are drawn with default styling. GridCraft ignores what the drawing XML specifies:

- **Run properties** (`a:rPr`) are ignored: size (`sz="5400"`), bold, `a:latin` typeface, text fill and text outline (`a:ln` inside `a:rPr`). The text is drawn small, regular, black and in the default font.
- **Paragraph alignment** `a:pPr algn="ctr"` and **vertical anchor** `a:bodyPr anchor="ctr"` are ignored. The text sits in the top-left corner.
- **Shape outline** `a:spPr/a:ln/a:noFill` is ignored. A border is drawn around the box when there should be none.

Workbooks often use text boxes for large stamp-style labels such as "DRAFT" or a revision colour. In GridCraft these become small boxed captions.

## Steps to reproduce

The script below writes a minimal, valid workbook with one text box. Its drawing XML is the same as what Excel writes for a WordArt-style label.

```python
import zipfile
D = ('<xdr:wsDr xmlns:xdr="http://schemas.openxmlformats.org/drawingml/2006/spreadsheetDrawing" '

body:
## Summary

When a workbook opens, GridCraft ignores the saved scroll position in `<sheetView topLeftCell="...">`. Every sheet opens scrolled to A1. The saved selection is restored, so the active cell can be off-screen when the file opens.

Excel restores both the scroll position and the selection. Long templates are usually saved scrolled to the section being worked on, and in GridCraft they always reopen at the top.

wb = openpyxl.Workbook(); ws = wb.active
for r in range(1, 61):

ws.sheet_view.topLeftCell = "A31"
ws.sheet_view.selection[0].activeCell = "A31"
ws.sheet_view.selection[0].sqref = "A31"
wb.save("scrolled.xlsx")

Open `scrolled.xlsx` in the GridCraft desktop app.

Row 1 is the first visible row. A31 is selected, but it is only visible because the sheet is short.

title: Legacy formulas without `cm` spill instead of implicitly intersecting
author: marcbraun
body:
**Component:** `crates/xlsx` (`sheet_read.rs`) / `crates/calc` (`eval.rs`)
**Commit tested:** `1ea549b` (main, 2026-10-11)

## Summary

A normal `<f>` formula whose cell has no `cm` attribute is a pre-dynamic-array
formula. Excel evaluates it with implicit intersection: a range in scalar
context collapses to the cell on the formula's own row or column. GridCraft
reads the `cm` flag (`sheet_read.rs:436`) but only consults it for
`t="array"` formulas (`sheet_read.rs:475`). A plain formula is parsed with
`Formula::new(text)` and evaluated as a dynamic array, so it spills and every
dependent of the top-left cell reads the wrong value.

This affects every workbook saved by Excel 2007–2016, by SheetJS, and by
LibreOffice, since none of them write `cm`. In the Apache POI
`FormulaEvalTestData_Copy.xlsx` corpus (authored in real Excel), 111 of
1,295 formula cells recompute to `Spill` instead of their cached scalar.

## Minimal reproducer

`sheet1.xml` (no styles, no `cm`, cached values written by a legacy writer):

```xml
<worksheet xmlns="http://schemas.openxmlformats.org/spreadsheetml/2006/main"><sheetData>
<row r="1"><c r="A1"><v>1</v></c></row>
<row r="2"><c r="A2"><v>2</v></c><c r="B2"><f>A1:A3*10</f><v>20</v></c><c r="C2"><f>SUM(B2:B2)</f><v>20</v></c></row>
<row r="3"><c r="A3"><v>3</v></c></row>
</sheetData></worksheet>
```

Zip it with the usual `[Content_Types].xml`, `_rels/.rels`, `xl/workbook.xml`
and `xl/_rels/workbook.xml.rels` (a Python one-liner is at the bottom), then:

```
$ gridcraft-cli cat implicit.xlsx --range A1:C3
1
2  10  10
3  20
```

Expected (Excel 2007–2016, LibreOffice 24.x `--convert-to csv`):

```
1
2  20  20
3
```

`B2` should be `A2*10 = 20` (row intersection), not `10` with `20` and `30`
spilled into `B3:B4`; `C2` should therefore be `20`, not `10`.

Row/column case: `=A1:C1*10` in `B2` intersects on the column and yields
`B1*10`. A range that shares neither the row nor the column yields `#VALUE!`.

title: CSV: saving a `;`-separated file rewrites it with `,` (separator detected on open is forgotten)
author: vedran-dobos
body:
### What happens

Open a semicolon-separated CSV (the usual "CSV" wherever `,` is the decimal separator — most of
continental Europe, Latin America, …) and save it: every `;` becomes `,`. The next program in the
chain can no longer read the file.

Reproduced on `main` (a513787) and 0.4.0 with a 74-row cut list exported by a furniture CAD/CAM
program (`;`-separated, CRLF, no BOM):

```
gridcraft-cli convert cutlist.csv out.csv
```

| | original | after save |
|---|---|---|
| row 1 | `1;720.0;579.0;K1_led_1;HDF_BIJELI;3.0;;;;;;` | `1,720,579,K1_led_1,HDF_BIJELI,3,,,,,,` |
| separator | `;` | `,` (all 74 rows) |

(The `720.0` → `720` and `1244121406E6` → `1.244121406E+15` changes in the same file are a separate
issue about data conversion and will be filed separately.)

### Cause

`read_csv` sniffs the delimiter (`sniff_delimiter`, `crates/xlsx/src/csv.rs`), but the result isn't
kept, and `save_bytes` (`crates/engine/src/io.rs`) calls `write_csv(sh, wb, b',')` with a
hard-coded comma. `file.save`, Save As `.csv`, `file.exportCsv`, `file.saveBytes` and
`gridcraft-cli convert` all go through that line.

### Expected

A workbook opened from CSV saves back with the separator it was opened with (Excel keeps a CSV in
its list-separator dialect too). Workbooks that didn't come from CSV keep today's `,`.

### Relation to open PRs

- #191 makes CSV save use the region's list separator. That helps when the region matches the
  file, but a comma file opened in a `;` region (or the reverse) would still be rewritten. The two
  fit together: the separator a file was opened with wins, otherwise the region's list separator.
- #422 (CSV writes displayed values) keeps the hard-coded `b','`, so it doesn't change this; the
  two touch the same line in `save_bytes`, a one-line rebase for whichever lands second.

I have a fix with regression tests ready and will open a PR referencing this issue.

title: Support Localized Excel Formula Names (Non-English Function Names)
author: Lord-Taw
body:
Currently, formula parsing appears to support only the English function names used by Excel. This creates friction for users working with localized versions of Excel, where function names and argument separators vary by language.

Examples:
=SUM(A1:A10) --> =SOMA(A1:A10) | =SUMA(A1:A10)
=IF(A1>0,"Yes","No") --> =SE(A1>0;"Sim";"Não") | =SI(A1>0;"Sí";"No")
Add support for localized Excel function names and regional formula syntax.

Many users never interact with formulas in English because Microsoft localizes function names by language. Supporting localized formulas would significantly improve the experience for users in regions such as Latin America and Europe, where translated function names are the default behavior.

Reference: https://www.guiadoexcel.com.br/traducao-das-formulas-excel-ingles-portugues/

title: Add Power Query, Power Pivot and DAX Compatibility
author: Lord-Taw
body:
Gridcraft currently focuses on traditional worksheet formulas and spreadsheet structures, but many modern Excel workbooks rely heavily on Power Query and Power Pivot for data transformation, modeling, and analytics.

When importing or working with workbooks that use these features, users may lose access to significant business logic embedded in:

- Power Query (M) transformations
- Power Pivot data models
- Relationships between tables
- Calculated columns
- DAX measures
- Data model metadata

This limits compatibility with real-world Excel files used for reporting, BI, financial analysis, and operational dashboards.

title: Implement Excel-Compatible ALT+↓ (Down Arrow) Keyboard Navigation for Dropdown Controls and Filter Access
author: Lord-Taw
body:
The application currently requires mouse interaction to access most dropdown-based controls, including AutoFilter menus, Ribbon dropdowns, ComboBoxes, and data-entry suggestion lists.

Users familiar with spreadsheets expect Alt + Down Arrow to open the most relevant dropdown associated with the currently focused UI element. The absence of this shortcut reduces keyboard productivity during data entry, filtering, and spreadsheet navigation.


The Alt + Down Arrow shortcut should be context-sensitive and open the most relevant dropdown available for the current focus target.

### **1. AutoFilter**
When the active cell belongs to a column header with an enabled AutoFilter: Alt + ↓ should open that column's AutoFilter Dropdown.

### **2. Ribbon Controls**
When focus is on a Ribbon control exposing a dropdown menu, ComboBox, Gallery, or Flyout: Alt + ↓ should open the control's associated dropdown.

  - Font Family Selector

  - Number Format Selector
  - Conditional Formatting Menu
  - Sort Menu
  - Insert Menu
  - Data Validation Lists
  - Any ComboBox-based control

### **3. Data Validation Dropdowns**
When the active cell contains a Data Validation List: Alt + ↓ should open the Data Validation dropdown.

### **4. Column Value Picker**
When all of the following conditions are true:
- The active cell **does not** contain a Data Validation List.
- No contextual dropdown is available.
- The active cell is inside a worksheet grid.
Alt + ↓ should open a Column Value Picker containing distinct values found in the current column.

The application should resolve Alt + ↓ using the following priority order:
  1. Data Validation Dropdown
  2. AutoFilter Dropdown

  4. ComboBox Control
  5. Column Value Picker

title: MCP server: add --automation-read-root / --automation-write-root, like VectorCraft
author: Dunai000
body:
## Runtime or environment

gridcraft-cli 0.5.0, macOS universal release build (commit 9f896c1).

## Summary

`gridcraft-cli mcp` gives the client agent the full file access of the user running it. `open_workbook`, `save_workbook`, `execute_command` (any engine command) and commands such as `file.saveAs`, `file.exportPdf`, `insert.picture` and CSV import take any path. A workbook carrying prompt-injected cell text can ask the agent to import a file from outside the working folder and read it back with `read_range`.

VectorCraft already solves this. Its `mcp` subcommand takes `--automation-read-root DIR` and `--automation-write-root DIR`, which confine every read and write the agent's commands make. In gridcraft-cli 0.5.0, `mcp` accepts only `--connect`, `--in` and `--sample` (`apps/gridcraft-cli/src/main.rs:493`), and passing the VectorCraft flags exits with "unknown option".

## Steps to reproduce

```sh
gridcraft-cli mcp --automation-read-root /tmp/work --automation-write-root /tmp/work
```

## Actual

The server exits: `gridcraft-cli: unknown option --automation-read-root`.

## Expected

The same two flags as VectorCraft, with the same rule that a root left out grants none of its access, so the server can be registered for an agent confined to one folder.

title: PDF export draws non-Latin text as "?" (unembedded Helvetica/Times, WinAnsi encoding)
author: Dunai000
body:
## Runtime or environment

gridcraft-cli 0.5.0, macOS universal release build (commit 9f896c1).

## Summary

`file.exportPdf` writes every cell in an unembedded base-14 font (Helvetica, or Times-Roman for workbooks styled that way) with WinAnsi encoding. Any character outside Windows-1252 becomes "?" in the PDF: Cyrillic, Greek, CJK and so on. The workbook itself stores and displays the text correctly. We hit this on a Ukrainian-language form, where every label came out as question marks.

## Steps to reproduce

```sh
gridcraft-cli run --cmd 'cell.set={"cell":"A1","input":"Привіт"}' \
  --cmd 'cell.set={"cell":"A2","input":"Ελληνικά"}' \
  --cmd 'cell.set={"cell":"A3","input":"Café"}' --out cyr.xlsx
gridcraft-cli run --in cyr.xlsx --cmd 'file.exportPdf={"path":"cyr.pdf"}'
pdffonts cyr.pdf
pdftotext cyr.pdf -
```

## Actual

```text
name         type     encoding  emb sub uni
Helvetica    Type 1   WinAnsi   no  no  no

??????
????????
Café
```

Opening a CSV (or typing, or pasting) converts every number-like field to a number, with no way to

saved and passed on to other software.

## Steps to reproduce

```sh
printf 'part;qty;code\r\nP3_pod;0042;1244121406E6\r\nP3_L2_led;1;124412140710\r\nP3_L1_led;2;1244121406FB\r\n' > ids.csv

cat out.csv
gridcraft-cli cat ids.csv
gridcraft-cli eval '=C2' --in ids.csv

title: fix(sheet): row and column edits accept counts that overflow their line endpoints
author: coygeek
body:
## Summary

The row and column insert/delete commands accept an explicit line count without checking whether the line endpoint fits the worksheet or its index type. Source inspection establishes reachable unchecked addition for out-of-range counts. With overflow checks enabled, the command panics internally and the session returns an internal error after restoring the workbook. The session recovery guard contains the failure, but the command violates the repository's requirement to handle command-derived numbers without panicking.

## Steps to reproduce

Runtime reproduction of the failing extreme cases was not run. The defect was verified by static proof against the baseline below. No executable extreme-count case is included.

1. Trace an unprotected new workbook through the registered row or column insert/delete command and its shared count reader. The count reader accepts the full unsigned 32-bit domain independently of the selected range's length.
2. For insertion, consider a valid positive insertion index with custom size information on the preceding line and no cells or spills. The used-range guard has no range to check, and the custom preceding line survives feature shifting. The insertion loop therefore evaluates its unchecked endpoint addition.
3. For deletion, the unprotected-sheet guard returns immediately. The deletion endpoint adds the start index and count before clamping to the worksheet limit.

title: fix(fill): weekday Series can fail to finish date advances
author: coygeek

## Summary

The supported weekday date fill accepts a numeric step without limiting the work needed to compute each generated date. Source inspection establishes that the command can remain inside a date-advance loop even when only one cell needs filling. If an advance leaves the supported calendar before it finishes, the loop cannot consume its remaining work. This prevents the command from returning a result or error.

The baseline is listed under Runtime or environment. Failure execution was intentionally omitted. These small controls were executed through an engine session with a new blank workbook:

Runtime reproduction of a failing advance was not run. Exact triggering steps are omitted. Static proof is complete for command nonreturn; elapsed runtime and desktop application behavior were not observed.

## Expected behavior

The repository requires checked handling of input-derived command numbers and `Result` errors. A weekday fill must either produce supported dates within bounded work or return an error when an advance cannot be completed safely. A small destination range must not allow an unchecked numeric step to keep the command running indefinitely. This contract does not prescribe a constant-time algorithm.

title: CSV save writes 12+ digit numbers as `1.24412E+11` (digits lost); #427's tests fail on `main`
author: vedran-dobos
body:
### What happens

Since #422 (CSV/TSV export writes displayed values), a number in General format is written the way
General shows it, and General has 11 characters even in a wide column. So `124412140710` is saved as
`1.24412E+11`: the digits are gone from the file. #422's description intended the opposite ("never
applies the grid's General narrowing, so the field holds the whole value").

On the 74-row cut list from #426 (`gridcraft-cli convert`, default settings):

| codes | before #422 | `main` (3926d21) |
|---|---|---|
| 20 all-digit part codes (`124412140710`) | saved intact | `1.24412E+11` |

This is the Excel behaviour #506 documents as data loss.

### CI

`main` has been red since 3926d21 (run "CI", `cargo xtask ci`): #427's regression tests
`io::tests::csv_save_keeps_the_separator_it_was_opened_with` and
`tests::saving_an_opened_semicolon_csv_keeps_semicolons` save a 12-digit code and now get
`1.24412E+11`. #422 and #427 each passed on their own and landed minutes apart.


### Proposed fix

CSV/TSV export writes a General-format number with every digit (`number_to_text`, as before #422);
every other number format stays as #422 writes it. The grid, clipboard and other displays are
unchanged. PR to follow.

title: feat(data): keep trailing decimal zeros on open and save (`720.0` comes back as `720`)
author: vedran-dobos
body:
## Summary

Opening a CSV turns `720.0` into the number 720 in General format, so the grid shows `720` and, since
#422, a saved CSV writes `720`. A plain open and save changes every such field. For files that are
passed on to other programs (here, cut lists from a furniture CAD/CAM program, as in #426 and #506),
that is enough for the next program to treat the file as different: on the reporter's 74-row cut list
it changes 222 fields. Keeping the fields as text isn't an answer: they are measurements and must stay
numbers. There is no setting to keep them as written.

## Steps to reproduce

```sh
printf '1;720.0;579.0;K1_led_1;3.0\r\n1;562.5;510.0;P3_pod;19.0\r\n' > cut.csv
gridcraft-cli convert cut.csv out.csv
cat out.csv
```

## Expected behavior

With an option to keep them, `out.csv` is identical to `cut.csv`, and the fields are still numbers
(`=B1+1` gives 721).

## Actual behavior

```text
1;720;579;K1_led_1;3
1;562.5;510;P3_pod;19
```

## Proposal

One more item in the Automatic Data Conversion list (#506, PR #583), under its counterpart "Remove
leading zeros and convert to a number": **Remove trailing zeros after the decimal separator**, on by
default (today's behaviour). Off, a plain number typed, pasted or opened
with trailing decimal zeros gets a number format that shows them (`720.0` → `0.0`, `3.10` → `0.00`,
`.50` → `#.00`), the way `1,234.50` already gets `#,##0.00`. It stays a number. "Enable all" includes
it, so unchecking that one box keeps everything number-like as written; the 74-row cut list then
opens and saves back byte for byte.

## Runtime or environment

GridCraft `main` at 3926d21 (0.5.0), built from source on Windows 11 with Rust 1.99.0; the steps above
were run with `gridcraft-cli`.

## Additional context

I have an implementation with tests, building on #583, and will open a PR referencing this issue.

title: AutoFilter apply/clear triggers full workbook recalc (seconds per filter on formula-heavy books)
author: richard1912
body:
## Summary
Applying or clearing an AutoFilter forces a full workbook recalculation. On a formula-heavy workbook this makes every filter click take several seconds, while Excel filters the same workbook instantly.

## Measurements (v0.5.0, Windows x64, `GRIDCRAFT_PROFILE=1`, `gridcraft-cli run`)
Workbook: ~62,000 formulas (mostly `LOOKUP` over 2,500-row ranges on another sheet), ~575-row AutoFilter range.

| Step | Time |
|---|---|
| `data.filterBy` edit itself (deciding which rows to hide) | 0.1 to 0.4 ms |
| Recalc after `data.filterBy` (values) | 3.64 s |
| Recalc after `data.filterBy` (clear) | 4.02 s |

Each commit logs two full eval passes (62,212 formulas, then 39,357), ~1.6 to 2.1 s each.

## Cause
`filter_by`, `clear_filter` and `reapply` in `crates/engine/src/cmd/data.rs` set `cx.structural = true`, so `commit` in `crates/engine/src/cmd/mod.rs` (~line 268) runs `d.calc.recalc_all(&mut wb)`. Hiding rows doesn't change any formula result except `SUBTOTAL`/`AGGREGATE` (which ignore filtered rows) and volatile functions.

## Suggested fix
Don't mark filter commands as structural. Instead dirty only cells containing `SUBTOTAL`, `AGGREGATE` or volatile functions (or cells that depend on them), e.g. via `cells_changed` on that set.

## Related, smaller
- `crates/ui-egui/src/grid.rs:1804`: `filter_values` rebuilds the distinct-values list (formatting every row via `cell_text`) on every frame while the dropdown is open. Caching it when the dropdown opens would help on large ranges.
- `apply_filter`, `FilterCriterion::Top10`: clones and sorts the column's numbers once per row (O(n² log n)). The threshold could be computed once per criterion before the row loop.

title: fix(xlsx): each save adds another _xlpm. prefix to LET/LAMBDA parameters read from a file
author: AndreaBonn
body:
## Summary

Opening and saving an XLSX that contains `LET` or `LAMBDA` adds a second `_xlpm.` prefix to every parameter name, and each further save adds one more. GridCraft re-reads its own output consistently, so values stay correct inside GridCraft and nothing looks wrong. The file on disk, though, holds parameter names that Excel did not write and does not expect.

This looks like a regression around #63. That fix made the writer add `_xlpm.`, but cell formulas read from a file still carry the prefix, so it is now applied twice.

## Steps to reproduce

Runtime: `gridcraft-cli` 0.5.0, `linux-x86_64` release tarball. `make_let.py` and `show.py` are at the bottom (Python stdlib only). The fixture has `A1=10`, `B1=_xlfn.LET(_xlpm.x,A1,_xlpm.x*2)` and `C1=_xlfn.LAMBDA(_xlpm.a,_xlpm.b,_xlpm.a^2+_xlpm.b)(3,4)`, written exactly as Excel stores them.

```sh
python3 make_let.py let.xlsx
gridcraft-cli convert let.xlsx s1.xlsx
gridcraft-cli convert s1.xlsx s2.xlsx
python3 show.py let.xlsx s1.xlsx s2.xlsx
gridcraft-cli cat s2.xlsx --range A1:C1 --csv
```

**Expected:** the formula text is unchanged after each save.

**Actual:**
```
let.xlsx  ['_xlfn.LET(_xlpm.x,A1,_xlpm.x*2)', '_xlfn.LAMBDA(_xlpm.a,_xlpm.b,_xlpm.a^2+_xlpm.b)(3,4)']
s1.xlsx   ['_xlfn.LET(_xlpm._xlpm.x,A1,_xlpm._xlpm.x*2)', '_xlfn.LAMBDA(_xlpm._xlpm.a,_xlpm._xlpm.b,_xlpm._xlpm.a^2+_xlpm._xlpm.b)(3,4)']
s2.xlsx   ['_xlfn.LET(_xlpm._xlpm._xlpm.x,A1,_xlpm._xlpm._xlpm.x*2)', '_xlfn.LAMBDA(_xlpm._xlpm._xlpm.a,_xlpm._xlpm._xlpm.b,_xlpm._xlpm._xlpm.a^2+_xlpm._xlpm._xlpm.b)(3,4)']
10,20,13
```

The values (`20`, `13`) are right. Only the stored text grows.

Not verified: how Excel reacts to `_xlpm._xlpm.x`. #63 reports that Excel refuses a file whose LET/LAMBDA parameters lack the prefix, so a malformed prefix is likely to be rejected or repaired as well. I have not opened the output in Excel.
