title: fix(ui): Ctrl+wheel zoom drifts, a notch out doesn’t return to the starting percentage
author: vedran-dobos
body:
## Summary

Zooming with Ctrl+mouse wheel changes the percentage by slightly different amounts in and out, so
scrolling back never lands where it started: 100% → 122% → 101% → 123% → 102%. A notch out should
undo a notch in, and the wheel should be able to get back to 100%.

## Steps to reproduce

1. Open GridCraft at 100% zoom.
2. Hold Ctrl and turn the mouse wheel up one notch. The status bar shows 122%.
3. Turn it down one notch: 101%.
4. Up one notch: 123%; down: 102%, and so on.

## Expected behavior

One notch down undoes one notch up, however often it's repeated, and 100% can always be reached
with the wheel.

## Actual behavior

The zoom creeps up by about 1% per up-and-down pair (sometimes 2%, depending on the frame rate).

## Runtime or environment

GridCraft `main` at b3acae6 (0.6.0; the zoom code is unchanged since 3926d21, where it was first seen), built from source on Windows 11 with Rust 1.99.0, a mouse with a
notched wheel.

## Additional context

The cause is in `crates/ui-egui/src/grid.rs`: egui eases one wheel notch (×e^0.2 ≈ 1.2214) in over
several frames, and the grid multiplies the stored whole-number percentage by each frame's share and
rounds it, so the rounding errors add up. Keeping the unrounded zoom fixes it for a wheel with exact
notches, but on my mouse (which sometimes sends uneven parts of a notch) the zoom still didn't
always come back to 100%.

For comparison, Excel steps a fixed 15 points per notch (100 → 115 → 130, and from 112% to 115% or
100%). A PR will propose stepping along a ladder of zoom levels instead.

title: French translations are misaligned: keys paired with other strings' translations (from #413)
author: edurbs
body:
Found while fixing main's red CI (#692): `crates/ui-egui/src/i18n/fr.rs` contains many semantically wrong pairs — the values are real French UI strings but attached to the wrong English keys, looking like a shifted/misaligned table around lines ~300–350:

| key | current fr | expected |
|---|---|---|
| `"Header"` | `Informations` | `En-tête` |
| `"Footer"` | `Feuille de\nprévision` | `Pied de page` |
| `"Save"` | `Type de fichier` | `Enregistrer` |
| `"Open"` | `Enregistrement` | `Ouvrir` |
| `"New"` | `Page suivante` | `Nouveau` |
| `"Sheet Name"` | `Feuille de\ndroite à gauche` | `Nom de la feuille` |
| `"Ruler"` | `Enregistrer sous` | `Règle` |
| … | (dozens more in that range) | |

French users see wrong labels in the ribbon, Header/Footer tab and Backstage.

`i18n::tests::translations_are_unique_and_preserve_unknown_text` only checks that every key has a *non-empty* translation in each language, so it cannot catch this. Other languages (de, es, cs, pt, ru, zh, ko, ja) look correctly aligned in the same ranges.

Likely introduced in #413 (i18n-fr). Suggested fix: regenerate/re-pair the fr table from the Japanese reference table, and spot-check against Excel's French UI. A stricter test (e.g. flagging fr values that equal *another* key's correct translation) would catch this class of bug.

title: [Bug] cell.set / set_cell: a numeric `input` silently clears the cell instead of entering the number
author: akislovag
body:
## Summary

`cell.set` documents `input` as `"text, number or =formula"`, but only the *string* form works. A JSON **number** for `input` resolves to an empty string, so the cell is **cleared**, and the command still reports success:

```sh
gridcraft-cli run --in book.xlsx --cmd 'cell.set={"cell":"Y1","input":123.5}'
# → {"command":"cell.set","result":{"cell":"Y1","value":""}}     ← cleared, reported as success
gridcraft-cli run --in book.xlsx --cmd 'cell.set={"cell":"Y2","input":"123.5"}'
# → {"cell":"Y2","value":"123.5"}                                ← works
```

The *undocumented* `value` alias does convert numbers, so the two spellings of the same parameter disagree:

```sh
gridcraft-cli run --in book.xlsx --cmd 'cell.set={"cell":"Y3","value":77}'       # → value "77"  ✓
gridcraft-cli run --in book.xlsx --cmd 'cell.set={"cell":"Y4","value":"77"}'     # → value "77"  ✓
```

Same through MCP `set_cell`:

```
tools/call set_cell {"cell":"Y9","input":42.5}    → get_cell: value null, type "empty", input ""
tools/call set_cell {"cell":"Y9","input":"42.5"}  → get_cell: value 42.5, type "number"
```

## Environment

GridCraft 0.5.0, flatpak `ai.storyteller.gridcraft` (commit `1f38e97`), Linux, KDE Plasma Wayland, x86_64 — via `gridcraft-cli` and the MCP server on the same build. Also compared against current `main`.

## Expected

A number is accepted exactly as documented — or rejected loudly. It should never be silently turned into an empty input.

## Cause

`crates/engine/src/cmd/edit.rs`, `cell_set`, v0.5.0:

```rust
let input = str_param(p, "input")
    .or_else(|| str_param(p, "value"))
    .map(str::to_string)
    .or_else(|| p.get("value").map(json_to_input))   // ← only the `value` alias is converted
    .unwrap_or_default();                            // ← a number for `input` lands here as ""
```

`str_param` is `p.get(key).and_then(Json::as_str)`, which is `None` for a number; the `json_to_input` fallback (which handles numbers, bools and null) is only appli…

title: fix(xlsx): Excel 2010 (x14) conditional-format extensions are skipped on import (solid data-bar fill, borders, axis, custom icon sets)
author: edurbs
body:
## Summary

Opening an `.xlsx` written by Excel 2010 or later warns `some Excel 2010 conditional format extensions were skipped` and drops the whole worksheet `extLst` → `x14:conditionalFormattings` block. The classic (2006) `<conditionalFormatting>` rules are imported, so the base rule survives, but everything the extension carries is lost:

- data bars: solid vs gradient fill, border and negative-value fill/border colours, axis colour and position, min/max bar length, auto min/max bounds
- icon sets: custom per-icon thresholds and custom icons
- rules that exist only as an x14 extension (no classic counterpart) disappear entirely

Real-world example: `Seção.xlsx` (a bank imprest-fund template) warns on open; many Excel-authored files with non-trivial conditional formatting hit this.

## Steps to reproduce

1. In Excel 2010+, add a data bar, set **Solid fill** and a negative-value colour (or build a custom icon set).
2. Save as `.xlsx`, open in GridCraft (or run `gridcraft-cli info file.xlsx`).
3. The open report contains `some Excel 2010 conditional format extensions were skipped`; the bar renders as gradient with default colours.

File-level repro: a worksheet whose classic `cfRule type="dataBar"` links an x14 rule the way Excel writes it — id ext inside the `<dataBar>` element:

```xml
<dataBar>
  <cfvo type="min"/><cfvo type="max"/>
  <color rgb="FF638EC8"/>
  <extLst><ext xmlns:x14="http://schemas.microsoft.com/office/spreadsheetml/2009/9/main"
       uri="{B025F937-C7B1-47D3-B67F-A62EFF666E3E}"><x14:id>{GUID}</x14:id></ext></extLst>
</dataBar>
```

and whose worksheet `extLst` carries the matching `x14:cfRule type="dataBar"` with `gradient="0"`, `border`, `negativeFill`, `axis`. Reading it with `read_xlsx` yields the warning and drops the extension.

## Evidence

- `crates/xlsx/src/sheet_read.rs`, `read_ext`: `"conditionalFormattings" => cx.warn(...)` — nothing from the block is read.
- #550 (a saved solid data bar reopens as gradient) is one symptom of this …

title: ODS: import formulas (live recalculation), not just cached values
author: edurbs
body:
## Summary

ODS import (PR #100) brings in worksheet data only: a formula cell becomes its last saved result as a constant, so editing inputs does not recalculate. This issue tracks importing the formulas themselves (`table:formula`) so ODS workbooks open with live, recalculating formulas. Cached results are kept as initial values so nothing shifts until recalculation.

## Scope

In scope:
- Translate OpenFormula text to model/Excel syntax: strip `of:=` / `oooc:=` / `msoxl:=` prefixes, argument separator `;` → `,`, bracketed references `[.A1]` → `A1`, `[.$A$1:.B2]` → `$A$1:B2`, quoted sheet names `['Sheet 2'.A1]` → `'Sheet 2'!A1`, drop the sheet-absolute `$`, `COM.MICROSOFT.X` → `X`.
- Error-typed caches (`calcext:value-type="error"`) become error values instead of text; matrix spans (`table:number-matrix-rows/columns-spanned`) mark legacy array formulas.
- Graceful fallback: anything untranslatable (external file references, `~`/`!` reference operators, `ORG.OPENOFFICE.*`/`com.sun.star.*` add-ins, parse failures) keeps the current behaviour — cached value as a constant plus a warning. Never mistranslate.

Out of scope (remaining in [docs/gaps.md](docs/gaps.md) §19 "XLSB/ODS beyond values"): ODS write/export, formatting/charts/images import, XLSB formula import.

## References
- Original request: #16
- Initial ODS data import: #100
- Broader ODF support request: #709

title: fix(xls): iteration settings aren't read from .xls files, so circular models show #CIRC!
author: iluebbe
body:
## Summary

The `.xls` (BIFF8) reader ignores the calculation-settings records: CalcIter, CalcCount, CalcDelta, CalcMode and CalcPrecision. So a workbook saved with **Enable iterative calculation** turned on opens in GridCraft with iteration off, and every cell in or after a circular reference shows `#CIRC!`. Excel opens the same files with iteration on and calculates them.

When Excel saves the same workbooks as `.xlsx`, GridCraft calculates them correctly, because the XLSX reader reads `<calcPr iterate="1">`.

## Found on real files

I ran `gridcraft-cli check` (main `fc45b7f`) on Aswath Damodaran's public valuation spreadsheets (NYU Stern, <https://pages.stern.nyu.edu/~adamodar/New_Home_Page/spreadsh.htm>). It compares GridCraft's results with the values Excel saved in the files. In 7 of the 64 BIFF8 files, 423 cells show `#CIRC!` where Excel has a value:

| file | formula cells | `#CIRC!` instead of Excel's value |
|---|---|---|
| `apv.xls` | 800 | 361 |
| `GrossvsNet.xls` | 39 | 15 |
| `higrowth.xls` | 581 | 15 |
| `fcffneg.xls` | 444 | 10 |
| `employeeoption.xls` | 19 | 9 |
| `fcffginzulambda.xls` | 511 | 7 |
| `warrant.xls` | 16 | 6 |

All seven have CalcIter = 1 in their worksheet substreams. When Excel 365 opens one of them on its own, `Application.Iteration` is `True`.

## Steps to reproduce

```sh
curl -LO https://pages.stern.nyu.edu/~adamodar/pc/apv.xls
gridcraft-cli check apv.xls
gridcraft-cli run --in apv.xls --print "'Adjusted Present Value'!F10:F11"
```

**Expected** (Excel): `$5,750` and `70.00%`.
**Actual:** `#CIRC!` and `#CIRC!`. `check` reports 361 mismatches with the signature `number → #CIRC!`.

Turning iteration on after the file is open doesn't fix it. With `--cmd 'formulas.calculationOptions={"iterative":true}'` both cells show `#DIV/0!`: iteration starts from the error values, not from the values saved in the file. Opening the `.xlsx` that Excel saved from the same workbook gives `$5,750` and `70.00%`.

title: fix(open): files encrypted with Excel's default password (VelvetSweatshop) ask for a password (.xlsx) or are refused (.xls)
author: iluebbe
body:
## Summary

Excel encrypts some workbooks with a built-in default password, `VelvetSweatshop`. It does this, for example, when a file is saved as read-only ([VMware TAU](https://blogs.vmware.com/security/2020/11/velvetsweatshop-when-default-passwords-can-still-make-a-difference.html), [SANS ISC](https://isc.sans.edu/diary/25990)). When Excel opens such a file, it tries that password first and only prompts if it fails, so the user never sees a password prompt and doesn't know one exists.

GridCraft never tries the default password:

- **`.xlsx` (Standard/Agile encryption):** GridCraft asks for a password the user doesn't have:
  `'58616.xlsx' is password-protected. Enter its password to open it.`
  Opening it with the password `VelvetSweatshop` works, since #436 already decrypts these files.
- **`.xls` (RC4):** GridCraft refuses the file:
  `XLS: this .xls workbook is password-protected (encrypted). GridCraft can't open encrypted .xls files; remove the password in Excel and try again.`
  The user can't remove a password they never set.

## Found on real files

| file | encryption | Excel 365 | GridCraft (main `fc45b7f`) |
|---|---|---|---|
| [`SpreadsheetGuide.xls`](https://pages.stern.nyu.edu/~adamodar/pc/SpreadsheetGuide.xls) (Damodaran, NYU Stern; 64 sheets) | FilePass RC4, version 1.1 | opens, no prompt | refused |
| [`50833.xls`](https://github.com/apache/poi/raw/trunk/test-data/spreadsheet/50833.xls) (Apache POI test data) | FilePass RC4, version 1.1 | opens, no prompt | refused |
| [`58616.xlsx`](https://github.com/apache/poi/raw/trunk/test-data/spreadsheet/58616.xlsx) (Apache POI test data) | Standard encryption | opens, no prompt | asks for a password |

How this was checked:

- **Excel:** I opened each file through automation with a wrong password passed in. Excel still opened all three, so it never needed the given password.
- **The two `.xls` files:** `VelvetSweatshop` passes the RC4 password verifier ([MS-OFFCRYPTO] 2.3.6.2; Salt, EncryptedVerifier and E…

title: fix(formula): `_xludf.` is dropped on read: user-defined calls become built-ins, and `_xludf.EOMONTH()` saves as a formula Excel deletes
author: iluebbe
body:
## Summary

Excel writes `_xludf.NAME(…)` for a call it treats as a **user-defined** function, and Excel evaluates it that way even when a built-in function has the same name. GridCraft drops the prefix when it reads the file. As a result:

1. **The call becomes the built-in function.** `_xludf.CONCAT("a","b")` gives `ab` in GridCraft and `#NAME?` in Excel.
2. **On save the prefix is gone,** so Excel then also calculates the built-in function.
3. **Calls with the wrong number of arguments break the saved file.** Excel keeps a call like `_xludf.EOMONTH()` precisely because `EOMONTH()` is not a valid built-in call. GridCraft saves it as `EOMONTH()`, and Excel then has to repair the file and **deletes the formula**.

## Found on a real file

Damodaran's [`SpreadsheetGuide.xls`](https://pages.stern.nyu.edu/~adamodar/pc/SpreadsheetGuide.xls) calls the old Analysis ToolPak `EOMONTH()` with no arguments (`Sensitising_Value_calcs!A21`). Excel 365 saves it as `.xlsx` with `<f>_xludf.EOMONTH()</f>`.

After `gridcraft-cli convert` that `.xlsx` contains `<f>EOMONTH()</f>`. Excel 365 opens it only after a repair, with this log entry: *Removed Records: Formula from /xl/worksheets/sheet27.xml part*. I opened 135 files saved by GridCraft (71 `.xlsx` and 64 `.xls` from Damodaran's collection) in Excel 365, and this was the only one that needed a repair.

## Minimal reproduction

`make_xludf.py` (stdlib only) writes a workbook with five formulas. Its `fullCalcOnLoad` makes Excel calculate them on open.

```python

from xml.sax.saxutils import escape
F = ['_xludf.EOMONTH()', '_xludf.CONCAT("a","b")', '_xludf.SUM(1,2)', 'MYUDF(1)', '_xludf.MYUDF(1)']
rows = "".join(f'<row r="{i}"><c r="A{i}"><f>{escape(f)}</f></c></row>' for i, f in enumerate(F, 1))
ns = 'xmlns="http://schemas.openxmlformats.org/spreadsheetml/2006/main"'
rel = "http://schemas.openxmlformats.org/officeDocument/2006/relationships"

title: fix(xlsx): chart sheets are skipped on open and lost on save
author: iluebbe
body:
## Summary

Excel chart sheets are sheets that hold a single chart (Move Chart › New sheet, or F11). GridCraft skips them when it opens an `.xlsx`, and saving the workbook then writes it without them. The chart sheet, its chart and its drawing are all gone after a save.

On open, GridCraft only warns `sheet "Value&WACC Chart" is a chartsheet and was skipped`. The warning doesn't say the sheet will be lost, and the save itself gives no warning.

## Found on real files

5 of 71 Excel-saved workbooks from Aswath Damodaran's public valuation spreadsheets (<https://pages.stern.nyu.edu/~adamodar/New_Home_Page/spreadsh.htm>) have chart sheets. After `gridcraft-cli convert` (main `fc45b7f`), none of them are left:

| workbook | chart sheets | charts before → after | drawings before → after |
|---|---|---|---|
| [`capstru.xlsx`](https://pages.stern.nyu.edu/~adamodar/pc/capstru.xlsx) | 1 | 1 → 0 | 2 → 1 |
| `eqmult` | 2 | 2 → 0 | 2 → 0 |
| `fcffgen` | 2 | 2 → 0 | 2 → 0 |
| `firmmult` | 1 | 1 → 0 | 1 → 0 |
| `liqdisc` | 1 | 1 → 0 | 1 → 0 |

(The last four are published as `.xls` and were saved as `.xlsx` by Excel 365. The chart sheets' `printerSettings` parts are lost too.)

## Steps to reproduce

```sh
curl -LO https://pages.stern.nyu.edu/~adamodar/pc/capstru.xlsx
gridcraft-cli info capstru.xlsx            # Warning: sheet "Value&WACC Chart" is a chartsheet and was skipped
gridcraft-cli convert capstru.xlsx out.xlsx
unzip -l capstru.xlsx | grep -c chartsheets/sheet   # 1
unzip -l out.xlsx | grep -c chartsheets/sheet       # 0
```

**Expected:** the saved workbook still has the "Value&WACC Chart" sheet and its chart. Failing that, GridCraft should say at save time that the chart sheet will be dropped.

## Root cause

- `crates/xlsx/src/read.rs:205` skips every sheet whose relationship isn't a worksheet.
- `crates/xlsx/src/passthrough.rs:96` lists `chartsheet` in `REWRITTEN`. The pass-through from #330 therefore drops chart sheets too, along with the drawing, chart, chart style…

title: fix(calc): a defined name that refers to several ranges gives #NAME?, and Define Name rejects it
author: iluebbe
body:
## Summary

When a defined name refers to several ranges, Excel stores it as a union with no parentheses around it:

```xml
<definedName name="dates">Aggregating!$C$31:$C$39,Aggregating!$H$31:$H$39,Aggregating!$L$31:$L$39</definedName>
```

Excel's Name Manager also shows and accepts it in that form. GridCraft reads the definition with the cell-formula parser, where a comma at the top level is an error, so:

- every formula that uses such a name evaluates to `#NAME?`;
- **Formulas › Define Name** (`formulas.defineName`) rejects the definition with "There's a problem with this formula."

The same name wrapped in parentheses works.

## Found on a real file

Damodaran's [`SpreadsheetGuide.xls`](https://pages.stern.nyu.edu/~adamodar/pc/SpreadsheetGuide.xls), saved as `.xlsx` by Excel 365, defines `dates` as above. On sheet `Aggregating`, 44 cells show `#NAME?` in GridCraft (main `fc45b7f`): `=MIN(dates)`, `=MAX(dates)+G43` and the cells that depend on them. Excel shows dates and counts there.

## Steps to reproduce

```sh
gridcraft-cli run \
  --cmd 'range.setValues={"range":"A1:C2","values":[[1,0,5],[2,0,7]]}' \
  --cmd 'formulas.defineName={"name":"u","refersTo":"=Sheet1!$A$1:$A$2,Sheet1!$C$1:$C$2"}'
# gridcraft-cli: step 2 (--cmd, formulas.defineName): There's a problem with this formula.

  --cmd 'range.setValues={"range":"A1:C2","values":[[1,0,5],[2,0,7]]}' \
  --cmd 'formulas.defineName={"name":"p","refersTo":"=(Sheet1!$A$1:$A$2,Sheet1!$C$1:$C$2)"}' \
  --cmd 'cell.set={"cell":"E1","input":"=SUM(p)"}' --cmd 'cell.set={"cell":"E2","input":"=AREAS(p)"}' \
  --cmd 'cell.set={"cell":"E3","input":"=MIN(p)"}' --print E1:E3 --quiet
# 15, 2, 1: the parenthesized form works
```

title: fix(numfmt): a negative number that rounds to zero shows -0.00 / -0 (Excel: 0.00 / 0)
author: iluebbe
body:
## Summary

Take a negative number that rounds to zero in its number format, such as `-0.0014` in `0.00`. If the format has no negative section of its own, Excel shows it **without** a minus sign: `0.00`. GridCraft shows `-0.00`. `TEXT()` has the same difference.

Values like this are everywhere in real models, because floating-point residue such as `-2.9E-09` appears wherever two nearly equal numbers are subtracted.

## Observed in Excel 365

I set each value and number format in a cell and read the displayed text (`Range.Text`, column wide enough). GridCraft (main `fc45b7f`) is in the last column:

| format | value | Excel | GridCraft |
|---|---|---|---|
| `0.00` | -0.0033 | `0.00` | `-0.00` |
| `0.00` | -2.89E-09 | `0.00` | `-0.00` |
| `0.00` | -0.005 | `-0.01` | `-0.01` |
| `0` | -0.4 | `0` | `-0` |
| `0` | -0.5 | `-1` | `-1` |
| `0.0` | -0.004 | `0.0` | `-0.0` |
| `#,##0.00` | -0.004 | `0.00` | `-0.00` |
| `0.00%` | -2.89E-09 | `0.00%` | `-0.00%` |
| `0.00%` | -0.0033 | `-0.33%` | `-0.33%` |
| `0.00;(0.00)` | -0.0033 | `(0.00)` | `(0.00)` |
| `0.00;-0.00;"zero"` | -0.0033 | `-0.00` | `-0.00` |
| `0.00E+00` | -2.89E-09 | `-2.89E-09` | `-2.89E-09` |

`TEXT()`: Excel gives `TEXT(-0.0033,"0")` = `0` and `TEXT(-0.4,"0")` = `0`; GridCraft gives `-0` for both.

So the minus sign goes away only when Excel applies the format's first section to a negative number and the rounded digits are all zero. A format with its own negative section keeps that section's text.

## Found on real files

Seven cells in three of Damodaran's valuation workbooks (<https://pages.stern.nyu.edu/~adamodar/New_Home_Page/spreadsh.htm>) show `0.00` in Excel and `-0.00` in GridCraft:

- `apv` 'Adjusted Present Value'!K64 = -0.0014
- `macrodur` 'Sector Averages by SIC'!D113 and D163
- `SpreadsheetGuide` Valuing_Option_calcs!F11:F14 = -2.9E-09

```sh
gridcraft-cli run --cmd 'cell.set={"cell":"A1","input":"-0.0033"}' \
  --cmd 'home.numberFormat={"range":"A1","format":"0.00"}' -…

title: fix(xls): files whose last sector isn't padded are refused as damaged; Excel opens them
author: iluebbe
body:
## Summary

Some programs that write `.xls` files don't pad the file to a full sector after the last stream sector. The Workbook stream's bytes are all in the file; only the final 512-byte sector is cut short. Excel opens these files. GridCraft refuses them:

```
XLS: damaged compound file: sector out of range (the file may be truncated)
```

## Found on real files

Five files from user bug reports in Apache POI's test data (<https://github.com/apache/poi/tree/trunk/test-data/spreadsheet>). Excel 365 opens all five without a repair; GridCraft (main `fc45b7f`) refuses all five:

| file | file size | bytes in the last, partial sector | Workbook stream: size / sectors in chain | stream bytes missing |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `47245_test.xls` | 210,793 | 361 | 207,209 / 405 | none |
| `47251.xls` | 28,937 | 265 | 27,401 / 54 | none |
| `50426.xls` | 18,915 | 483 | 17,379 / 34 | none |
| `53984.xls` | 38,331 | 443 | 36,283 / 71 | none |
| `ex45698-22488.xls` | 4,746,305 | 65 | 4,707,390 / 9,195 | none |

In each file, the last sector in the Workbook chain is the partial one at the end of the file. It holds exactly the bytes the stream's declared size still needs. For example, `47251.xls`: 27,401 = 53 × 512 + 265.

## Steps to reproduce

```sh
curl -LO https://github.com/apache/poi/raw/trunk/test-data/spreadsheet/47251.xls
gridcraft-cli info 47251.xls
# We can't open '47251.xls': the file is not a valid spreadsheet: XLS: damaged compound file: sector out of range (the file may be truncated)
```

## Root cause

`crates/xlsx/src/cfb.rs:227-230` (regular stream chain) reads each sector as `self.bytes.get(s..s + sector_size)`. That returns `None` for a final sector that the file cuts short, even when the stream needs only the bytes that are there.

## Suggested fix

Allow the final sector of a chain to be short when the stream's declared size ends inside the bytes the file has. Read up to the end of the file and pad with zeros, or truncate to the declared size. Keep the error…

title: fix(xls): one FORMAT record with a wrong character count makes the whole .xls fail to open
author: iluebbe
body:
## Summary

A FORMAT record (0x041E) in an `.xls` file whose character count is one more than the characters it holds makes GridCraft refuse the whole workbook:

```
XLS: record is shorter than its contents
```

Excel opens the same file.

## Found on a real file

[`61045_govdocs1_626534.xls`](https://github.com/apache/poi/raw/trunk/test-data/spreadsheet/61045_govdocs1_626534.xls), from Apache POI's test data, comes from the govdocs1 corpus of public US government documents. Excel 365 opens it without a repair; GridCraft (main `fc45b7f`) refuses it.

The workbook globals contain this FORMAT record:

| offset | length | ifmt | cch | flags | characters present |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| 0x143 | 55 | 42 | **51** | 0 | **50**: `_("$"* #,##0_);_("$"* \(#,##0\);_("$"* "-"_);_(@_)` |

The record ends right after the 50th character, and the next record header (`1e 04 2e 00`) follows directly. `Cursor::string()` asks for character 51 and fails. The error propagates and the whole open fails.

The writer of this file also garbled a second FORMAT record (ifmt 44: header `2c 00 00 00 3a`, i.e. `cch = 0`, `flags = 0x3A`, followed by 58 characters). GridCraft reads it as an empty format code without an error.

I located the failing record by temporarily adding the record id and index to the error in `globals()`. The error was `globals record 0x041E #11`.

## Steps to reproduce

```sh
curl -LO https://github.com/apache/poi/raw/trunk/test-data/spreadsheet/61045_govdocs1_626534.xls
gridcraft-cli info 61045_govdocs1_626534.xls
# We can't open '…': the file is not a valid spreadsheet: XLS: record is shorter than its contents
```

## Root cause

- `crates/xlsx/src/xls/mod.rs`, `globals()`, `0x041E` arm: `let code = c.string()?;`. When one record can't be parsed, the error propagates and the whole open fails.
- `crates/xlsx/src/xls/records.rs`, `Cursor::chars()` reads `cch` characters and errors when the record ends first.

title: fix(tables): structured references to a column name with leading or trailing spaces give #REF!
author: iluebbe
body:
## Summary

Structured references to a table column whose name starts or ends with a space evaluate to `#REF!` in most forms. Excel calculates all of them. Headers like this are common in real data, because they are often typed or pasted with a stray trailing space.

## Observed in Excel 365

I made a table `Table1` with the headers `Item` and `Qty ` (trailing space) and values 2 and 3, then entered formulas through the en-US `Formula` property:

| formula | Excel 365 | GridCraft (main `fc45b7f`) |
|---|---|---|
| `=SUM(Table1[Qty ])` | 5 (Excel stores it as `Table1[[Qty ]]`) | `#REF!` |
| `=SUM(Table1[[Qty ]])` | 5 | 5 |
| `=Table1[[#Totals],[Qty ]]` (total row on) | the total | `#REF!` |
| `=SUBTOTAL(109,Table1[Qty ])` | 5 | `#REF!` |
| `=Table1[@[Qty ]]*10` (row 2) | 20 | 20 |
| `=SUM(Table1[Qty])` | rejected (no such column) | `#REF!` |

## Found on real files

title: fix(functions): ROMAN forms 2 and 3 differ from Excel for 92 numbers (99 → IC, 990 → XM, 995 → VM)
author: iluebbe
body:
## Summary

`ROMAN(number, form)` returns the wrong numeral for 92 of the 19,995 combinations of number 1–3999 and form 0–4: 72 in form 2 and 20 in form 3. Forms 0, 1 and 4 match Excel for every number.

## Observed in Excel 365

I filled `=ROMAN(n, form)` for every number and form in Excel 365, saved the workbook and checked it with `gridcraft-cli check` (main `fc45b7f`). Every difference follows one of these patterns:

| number | form | Excel 365 | GridCraft |
|---|---|---|---|
| 99 (and every x99 except 499: 199 … 3899) | 2 | `IC`, `CIC`, … | `VCIV`, `CVCIV`, … |
| 990–999 (and 1990–1999, 2990–2999, 3990–3999) | 2 | `XM`, `XMI` … `XMIX` | `LMXL`, `LMXLI` … `LMIL` |
| 995–999 (and 1995–1999, …) | 3 | `VM`, `VMI` … `VMIV` | `XMV`, `XMVI` … `XMIX` |

Apache POI's [`RomanFunctionTestCaseData.xls`](https://github.com/apache/poi/raw/trunk/test-data/spreadsheet/RomanFunctionTestCaseData.xls) records the same Excel results (`ROMAN(99,2)` = `IC`, `ROMAN(995,3)` = `VM`, …).

```sh
gridcraft-cli eval '=ROMAN(99,2)'    # VCIV, Excel IC
gridcraft-cli eval '=ROMAN(990,2)'   # LMXL, Excel XM
gridcraft-cli eval '=ROMAN(995,3)'   # XMV,  Excel VM
```

## Root cause

`crates/functions/src/math.rs`, `roman_tokens`, models the forms as a maximum subtraction ratio (10, 20, 50, 100, 1000). Excel's form 2 still allows `IC` (ratio 100) and `XM` (ratio 100), and form 3 allows `VM` (ratio 200), so a ratio limit can't produce these results. The greedy pick then reaches them through longer combinations instead.

## Suggested fix

Derive the allowed subtractive pairs per form from Excel's output, not from a ratio. Check in the 92 cases above, or the full 3999 × 5 table as observed data, as a test in `math.rs`. The numerals with no difference confirm the rest of the current table.

title: fix(functions): EDATE and EOMONTH are a day off for serial 0 and February 1900
author: iluebbe
body:
## Summary

`EDATE` and `EOMONTH` differ from Excel for dates in January and February 1900:

- **Serial 0** (an empty date cell) is shifted by a day. `EDATE(0,0)` gives 1, not 0.
- **February 1900 has 28 days in Excel's `EDATE` and `EOMONTH`,** although the sheet itself knows the phantom 29 February (`DATE(1900,2,29)` = 60, #124). GridCraft uses 29 days there.

Empty date cells passed to `EDATE` are common in real models. In the user file from Apache POI bug 61652 ([`61652.xlsx`](https://github.com/apache/poi/raw/trunk/test-data/spreadsheet/61652.xlsx), sheets `Model` and `IRPPCalc`), `=EDATE(A4,1)` with an empty `A4` shows 31 January 1900 in Excel and 1 February 1900 in GridCraft (31 vs 32).

## Observed in Excel 365

Formulas entered through the en-US `Formula` property, compared with GridCraft main `fc45b7f`:

| formula | Excel 365 | GridCraft |
|---|---|---|
| `=EDATE(0,0)` | 0 | 1 |
| `=EDATE(0,1)` | 31 | 32 |
| `=EDATE(0,12)` | 366 | 367 |
| `=EOMONTH(0,1)` | 59 | 60 |
| `=EDATE(31,1)` | 59 | 60 |
| `=EOMONTH(59,0)` | 59 | 60 |
| `=EOMONTH(0,0)`, `=EOMONTH(0,-1)`, `=EDATE(59,1)`, `=EDATE(60,1)`, `=EDATE(61,-1)`, `=EOMONTH(31,0)` | same in both | |
| `=DAY(0)`, `=MONTH(0)`, `=YEAR(0)`, `=WEEKDAY(0)`, `=WEEKNUM(0)`, `=DATE(1900,1,0)` | same in both | |
| `=DATEDIF(0,31,"d")`, `=DAYS360(0,31)`, `=WORKDAY(0,1)`, `=NETWORKDAYS(0,10)`, `=YEARFRAC(0,366)` | same in both | |

So Excel's `EDATE` and `EOMONTH` treat serial 0 as 0 January 1900 and end February 1900 on the 28th (serial 59). The probes from serial 60 on agree.

## Steps to reproduce

```sh
gridcraft-cli eval '=EDATE(0,0)'      # 1  (Excel 0)
gridcraft-cli eval '=EDATE(31,1)'     # 60 (Excel 59)
gridcraft-cli eval '=EOMONTH(59,0)'   # 60 (Excel 59)
```

## Suggested fix

In `EDATE` and `EOMONTH`, convert serials below 61 the way Excel's date functions do: 0 is day 0 of January and February 1900 has 28 days. Don't change the 1900 leap-day handling of `DATE`, `DAY` and the sheet. Add the table above as tests.

title: fix(functions): CELL("width") counts the cell padding (9 for a default 8.43 column; Excel 8)
author: iluebbe
body:
## Summary

`CELL("width", ref)` is often one too high. For a default 8.43 column it gives 9; Excel gives 8.

GridCraft computes the value as `round(pixels / 7)`. Excel returns the column width shown in **Format › Column Width**, in characters of the workbook's default font and without the cell padding, rounded. Excel 365 also returns a second value, `TRUE` when the column has the default width. As a dynamic-array formula, `=CELL("width",A1)` spills `{width, is_default}`; in a legacy formula, implicit intersection keeps only the width.

## Observed in Excel 365

New workbook (default font Aptos Narrow 11, standard width 10.71), `=CELL("width",X1)` per column:

| column width (Format › Column Width) | Excel 365, dynamic | Excel 365, legacy | GridCraft, same width set with `home.columnWidth {"chars": …}` |
|---|---|---|---|
| 10.71 (default) | `11`, `TRUE` | 11 | 11 |
| 12 | `12`, `FALSE` | 12 | **13** |
| 10.57 | `11`, `FALSE` | 11 | 11 |
| 2.86 | `3`, `FALSE` | 3 | **4** |
| 8.43 (GridCraft's default) | | 8 | **9** |

The width also depends on the default font. In Apache POI's [`47804.xlsx`](https://github.com/apache/poi/raw/trunk/test-data/spreadsheet/47804.xlsx), with Verdana 10 as the default font, columns B–D (stored width 12) give 11 in Excel and 12 in GridCraft, and the other six columns give 10 and 11 (all nine cells in row 2 differ).

## Steps to reproduce

```sh
gridcraft-cli run --cmd 'home.columnWidth={"cols":"C:C","chars":12}' \
  --cmd 'cell.set={"cell":"H1","input":"=CELL(\"width\",B1)"}' \
  --cmd 'cell.set={"cell":"H2","input":"=CELL(\"width\",C1)"}' --print H1:H2 --quiet
# 9, 13   (Excel: 8, 12)
```

## Root cause

`crates/calc/src/eval.rs:1278`:

```rust
"width" => Ev::V(Value::number(sheet.map_or(8.43, |s| (s.col_width(c.col) as f64 / 7.0 * 100.0).round() / 100.0).round())),
```

The pixel width includes Excel's 5 px padding, and the 7 px maximum digit width assumes Calibri 11, whatever the workbook's default font is.

Return the…

title: fix(functions): MODE returns #VALUE! for typed text arguments and counts typed TRUE; Excel ignores both
author: iluebbe
body:
## Summary

`MODE` returns `#VALUE!` as soon as any argument is a text value typed into the formula. Excel ignores text arguments, numeric text like `"1"` included, and computes the mode of the remaining numbers. Errors among the arguments still propagate.

Typed logical values have the opposite problem: GridCraft counts `TRUE` as 1, and Excel ignores it.

## Observed in Excel 365

Formulas entered through the en-US `Formula` property, compared with GridCraft main `fc45b7f`:

| formula | Excel 365 | GridCraft |
|---|---|---|
| `=MODE(1,1,"x")` | 1 | `#VALUE!` |
| `=MODE(1,2,"x")` | `#N/A` | `#VALUE!` |
| `=MODE(1,"1",2,3)` | `#N/A` (so `"1"` is not counted as 1) | `#VALUE!` |
| `=MODE("1",1,2,3)` | `#N/A` | `#VALUE!` |
| `=MODE("1",1,#DIV/0!,2,3)` | `#DIV/0!` | `#VALUE!` |
| `=MODE(1,TRUE,TRUE,2)` | `#N/A` | 1 |
| `=MODE(1,1,TRUE)` | 1 | 1 |

Apache POI's `FormulaEvalTestData.xls` (<https://github.com/apache/poi/raw/trunk/test-data/spreadsheet/FormulaEvalTestData.xls>) records the same Excel results, for example `MODE(B8,"1",2,3)` = `#N/A`.

```sh
gridcraft-cli eval '=MODE(1,1,"x")'   # #VALUE!  (Excel 1)
```

## Suggested fix

In `MODE` (and check `MODE.SNGL` and `MODE.MULT` the same way), skip text and logical values given directly as arguments, as Excel does. Propagate error values in argument order. Add the table above as a test. Excel's documentation for `MODE` only covers text in arrays and references; the table is what Excel does with typed text.

title: fix(functions): DGET differs from Excel for computed criteria, empty-string criteria and empty result fields
author: iluebbe
body:
## Summary

`DGET` (and probably the other database functions that share the criteria code) differs from Excel in three ways:

1. **Computed criteria.** A criteria column whose cell holds a formula, such as `=G2<$G$45` or `=age<7`, gives `#VALUE!`. Excel evaluates the formula for every record. This is the documented "formula as criteria" form, with the reference relative to the first data row.
2. **Empty-string criteria.** A criteria cell that holds an empty string (from `=""`) is treated like an empty cell and matches everything. In Excel it matches only records whose field is an empty string; it doesn't match empty cells or 0.
3. **Empty result fields.** `DGET` counts matching records whose result field is empty. Excel ignores them. One matching record with a non-empty field returns that value, and none returns `#VALUE!`.

## Observed in Excel 365

Apache POI's [`DGet.xls`](https://github.com/apache/poi/raw/trunk/test-data/spreadsheet/DGet.xls) is a table of DGET cases, each with the result Excel gave when the file was written. title: fix(functions): four small differences from Excel in MIRR, COUNTIF, INDIRECT and USDOLLAR
author: iluebbe
body:
## Summary

Four small function differences from Excel 365. I found them while checking Apache POI's test workbooks (<https://github.com/apache/poi/tree/trunk/test-data/spreadsheet>) against Excel 365's recalculation, then confirmed each one with formulas entered in Excel 365 through the en-US `Formula` property. GridCraft is main `fc45b7f`.

| formula | Excel 365 | GridCraft | file |
|---|---|---|---|
| `=MIRR({-10000,-3400,-6500,-1000},0.07,0.01)` (no positive cash flow) | -1 | `#DIV/0!` | `mirrTest.xls` |
| `=COUNTIF(H3,"<=")` where `H3` is `=""` | 0 | 1 | `countifExamples.xls` |
| `=INDIRECT("I3",FALSE)` (A1-style text with `a1` = FALSE) | `#REF!` | the value of I3 | `IndirectFunctionTestCaseData.xls` |
| `=USDOLLAR(1)` | currency text, like `DOLLAR(1)` | `#NAME?` | `missingFuncs44675.xls` |

## Notes

- **MIRR:** Excel's documentation says MIRR returns `#DIV/0!` without at least one positive and one negative value, but Excel 365 returns -1 when every value is negative. That is what MIRR's formula gives with a zero present value of the positive flows. The probe `=MIRR({100,200,300},0.07,0.01)` (no negative value) agrees in both.
- **COUNTIF:** A bare operator criterion against an empty string differs: `<=` in my probe, and `<=` and `>=` in `countifExamples.xls`. With an empty cell (no content) instead of `""`, both give the same result, as do `=COUNTIF(H3,"=")` and `=COUNTIF(H3,"")`.
- **INDIRECT:** With `a1` = FALSE, GridCraft falls back to reading A1-style text; Excel returns `#REF!`. (#503 is about R1C1 offsets past the sheet; this is a separate case.)
- **USDOLLAR:** This is a legacy function that formats like `DOLLAR`. GridCraft's function catalog and `docs/function-parity.md` don't list it. It may belong in the catalog as a compatibility function.

```sh
gridcraft-cli eval '=MIRR({-10000,-3400,-6500,-1000},0.07,0.01)'   # #DIV/0!  (Excel -1)
gridcraft-cli eval '=USDOLLAR(1)'                                  # #NAME?   (Excel: currency text)
```

title: ODS: sheet names renamed on import leave translated formulas referencing the original name
author: edurbs
body:
## Summary

Found by the final review of the ODS formula import branch (#711, PR follows).

ODS sheet names that XLSX cannot hold (>31 chars, or any of `:?*\/[]`) are sanitized/truncated by `unique_name` at import (`crates/xlsx/src/ods.rs`, table start handling). But formulas translated from `table:formula` keep the **original** sheet name — e.g. `['ThisSheetNameIsWayLongerThanThirtyOneChars'.A1]` imports as a live formula referencing the pre-truncation name while the sheet is stored truncated.

No recalc is forced on open, so the cached value displays correctly; but any recalculation touching the formula yields `#REF!`. The existing rename warning fires but says nothing about formulas.

## Suggested fix (either)

1. **Cheapest, philosophy-consistent with #711's never-mistranslate rule:** treat formulas that reference a sheet whose stored name differs from the source name as untranslatable → keep the cached value as a constant (existing fallback + warning path).
2. Fuller: rewrite the sheet part of translated references through an original→stored rename map recorded during import.

Either way, add a test with a >31-char sheet name referenced by a formula.

## Related

- #711 (the formula import this gap belongs to)
- #16 (original ODS support request)

title: [Bug] Deleting multiple Ctrl-selected rows only removes the last selected row
author: aaronholoday
body:
**Description**

When multiple nonadjacent rows are selected using Ctrl+click, choosing **Delete** from the right-click context menu deletes only the most recently selected row. The other selected rows remain in the worksheet.

**Steps to reproduce**

1. Open a worksheet containing data in several rows.
2. Click the header for row 2.
3. Hold **Ctrl** and click the headers for rows 4 and 6.
4. Right-click the header of the last selected row.

All selected rows—original rows 2, 4, and 6 in this example—should be deleted in one operation. Unselected rows should remain, shifting upward as appropriate.

Only the last selected row is deleted. The other selected rows remain.

Users must delete nonadjacent rows individually, even though they have already selected all the rows they intend to remove.

title: Windows: dragging the window across monitors with different display scales crashes it (Surface::configure 9048x5757 > 8192)
author: msaulc
body:
## Summary

On Windows 11 with monitors at different display scales, dragging the GridCraft window across the boundary between them (here: onto the top edge of a 100% monitor to snap-maximize it) makes the window balloon to ~2.5× its size and the app quits:

```
ERROR [main] wgpu::backend::wgpu_core: Handling wgpu errors as fatal by default
ERROR [main] gridcraft: internal error: panicked at ...\wgpu-30.0.1\src\backend\wgpu_core.rs:3981:18:
wgpu error: Validation Error
  In Surface::configure
    `Surface` width and height must be within the maximum supported texture size. Requested was (9048, 5757), maximum extent for either dimension is 8192.
```

Any unsaved work is lost.

## Environment

- GridCraft 0.5.0 (release build); also reproduced on `main` (0.6.1, fc45b7f)
- Windows 11 24H2 (build 26100), DirectX 12, Intel Arc + NVIDIA RTX 4070 Laptop
- Monitors: 3440×1440 at **100%** (primary), 3840×2400 laptop panel at **250%** to its right, 1080×1920 at 100% on the left

## Steps to reproduce

1. Put the GridCraft window on the 250% monitor (default size: 3600×2250 physical).
2. Drag it by the title bar so that it straddles both monitors, toward the top edge of the 100% monitor.
3. The window flips between 250% and 100% as it crosses, then grows to 9048×5757 and the app panics.

Reproduced deterministically by a scripted mouse drag (same 9048×5757 every time). Window client size sampled during the drag:

| step | DPI | client size |
|---|---|---|
| 22 | 240 | 3600×2250 |
| 23 | 96 | 1440×900 |
| 24 | 240 | 3600×2250 |

Two problems combine:

1. **winit 0.30.13's `WM_DPICHANGED` handling on Windows 11** (rust-windowing/winit#4041, #4600). During a live drag, winit replaces the rectangle Windows suggests with its own "conservative" one and nudges it back onto the monitor `MonitorFromWindow` reports, which during a drag is still the monitor being left. That triggers another `WM_DPICHANGED`, and the window size gets scaled a …

title: Ctrl+Shift+Arrow (and Shift+Arrow) extending the selection past the visible area doesn't scroll
author: msaulc
body:
## Summary

Extending the selection from the keyboard past the last visible row or column doesn't scroll the grid: the selection keeps growing off-screen while the view stays put. Reported with Ctrl+Shift+Down/Up; Shift+Arrow, Shift+PageUp/PageDown, Alt+Shift+PageUp/PageDown and Ctrl+Shift+Home/End behave the same. Excel scrolls so the moving end of the selection stays visible.

**Environment:** GridCraft 0.5.0 on Windows 11; also on `main` (fc45b7f).

## Steps to reproduce

1. Fill A1:A200 with values.
2. Select A1 and press Ctrl+Shift+Down.
3. Expected: A1:A200 selected and the grid scrolled to row 200. Actual: A1:A200 selected, the grid still shows the top rows.

Plain Ctrl+Down scrolls correctly.

## Cause

`selection.move` with `extend` moves the far corner of the selection and leaves the active cell on the anchor (`crates/engine/src/cmd/edit.rs`, `selection_move`). The keyboard handlers then set `ensure_visible`, but the scroll-into-view step in `grid::show` always targets `selection.active`, which is the anchor and is already on screen. Related but separate: #687 (selection borders disappearing on Ctrl+Shift+Down).

PR to follow.

title: TEXT()/number formats: scientific formats with a literal after E±, a % or a thousands separator disagree with Excel (210 cells in POI NumberFormatApproxTests.xlsx)
author: Mart95Dev
body:
## Summary

`TEXT()` (and number formatting generally, since it's the same formatter) disagrees with Excel on scientific-notation format codes that mix the exponent with other tokens. On Apache POI's `NumberFormatApproxTests.xlsx`, whose cached values come from real Excel, `gridcraft-cli check` reports 210 of 249 formula cells mismatched, all `TEXT(value, format)`. Plain scientific formats in the same file (`0.00E+00`…) match.

File: https://github.com/apache/poi/blob/trunk/test-data/spreadsheet/NumberFormatApproxTests.xlsx (sheet `Tests`: A = `=TEXT(C,B)`, B = format, C = value, D = category).

## The four patterns

**1. A literal right after `E+`/`E-`/`e+`/`e-` (170 cells).** Excel writes the literal *before* the exponent sign. GridCraft keeps the sign glued to the `e`.

| Format          | Value      | Excel           | GridCraft       |
|-----------------|------------|-----------------|-----------------|
| `\|#\|e+\|#\|`        | 123456.789 | `\|1\|e\|+5\|`        | `\|1\|e+\|5\|`        |
| `\|#.#\|E+\|#\|`      | -1.23456789e-05 | `-\|1.2\|E\|-5\|` | `-\|1.2\|E-\|5\|`     |
| `\|####.####\|e+\|#\|` | 123456.789 | `\|12.3457\|e\|+4\|` | `\|12.3457\|e+\|4\|` |

**2. `%` in the mantissa (20 cells).** The exponent is off by 2, because the ×100 is applied in a different order.

| Format     | Value      | Excel     | GridCraft |
|------------|------------|-----------|-----------|
| `\|#%e-#\|`  | 123456.789 | `\|1%e5\|`  | `\|1%e7\|`  |
| `\|#e+#%\|`  | 123456.789 | `\|1e+5%\|` | `\|1e+7%\|` |

**3. Thousands separator just before the `e` (10 cells).** Excel ignores the `,`. GridCraft applies it as a /1000 scaling, so the exponent is off by 3.

| Format     | Value      | Excel     | GridCraft |
|------------|------------|-----------|-----------|
| `\|#,e-#\|`  | 123456.789 | `\|1e5\|`   | `\|1e2\|`   |
| `\|#,e+#\|`  | 123456.789 | `\|1e+5\|`  | `\|1e+2\|`  |

title: Rich text runs in a cell (mixed font colors) are flattened: single color rendered, formatting lost on save
author: edurbs
body:
Extracted from #708 (item 1: "Mixed font colors inside the same cell are not correctly recognized/rendered") so the compatibility bug can be tracked separately from the workflow feature requests in that issue.

## What happens

When a cell's text is stored in XLSX as rich text runs (`<r>` elements with their own `<rPr>`), GridCraft shows the whole string in one format (the cell-level font) instead of the per-run colors, and saving writes a plain string — the run formatting is destroyed. Excel and ONLYOFFICE render these cells with the per-run colors.

## Repro

Test workbook (4 shared strings, cells `A1:A4`):

```xml
<si><t xml:space="preserve">black only text</t></si>
<si><t xml:space="preserve">red only text</t></si>
<si>
  <r><rPr><sz val="11"/><color theme="1"/><rFont val="Calibri"/><scheme val="minor"/></rPr><t xml:space="preserve">this is black,</t></r>
  <r><rPr><sz val="11"/><color indexed="2"/><rFont val="Calibri"/><scheme val="minor"/></rPr><t xml:space="preserve"> this is red,</t></r>
  <r><rPr><sz val="11"/><color theme="1"/><rFont val="Calibri"/><scheme val="minor"/></rPr><t xml:space="preserve"> this is black</t></r>
</si>
<si>
  <r>…black…</r><r>…<color indexed="2"/> red…</r><r><color rgb="FF00B050"/> green…</r>
</si>
```

`A3` = black/red/black, `A4` = black/red/green. Note the runs use all three color encodings — `theme="1"`, `indexed="2"` and `rgb="FF00B050"` — so run colors need the same theme/indexed/rgb resolution cell styles already have.

## Evidence (current main)

- `crates/xlsx/src/xml.rs` `rich_text()`: concatenates `<t>`/`<r><t>` into a plain `String`, discarding every `<rPr>`.
- `crates/core/src/value.rs`: `Value::Text(Arc<str>)` — the data model has no run-level formatting; a cell carries exactly one style.
- `crates/xlsx/src/write.rs`: shared strings written back as `<si><t>…</t></si>`, no `<r>` runs → round-trip loses the formatting.
- The `.xls` (BIFF8) reader flattens the same way (`rich_string()`).

## Expected

- Per-run font prop…

title: [Enhancement] Enterprise-Grade Spreadsheet Engine and Excel Compatibility
author: kaivyy
body:

GridCraft aims to become a powerful cross-platform spreadsheet application capable of handling large workbooks, complex formulas, and professional data-analysis workflows.

- Cached lookup indexes where beneficial.
- Background recalculation without blocking UI interaction.
- Deterministic results and explicit error propagation.

2. XLSX round-trip fidelity

Opening and saving an existing Excel workbook must not silently discard unsupported workbook features.

title: Rich text editing: apply font color to a selection of characters within a cell (in-cell editor / formula bar)
author: edurbs
body:
Follow-up to #774 (rich text runs: import, render, round-trip). Extracted from the discussion in #708 item 1.

## Goal

Excel-style run-level formatting from the UI: select a character range inside the in-cell editor or the formula bar and apply **Font Color** (and later other font properties such as bold/italic) to just that selection, creating or editing rich text runs.

title: Security: cell hyperlinks open any URL scheme without confirmation, and --control server has no auth
author: mendy-cohen
body:
I was looking through the GridCraft source (commit fc45b7f) before trying it out and found two security issues.

### 1) Cell hyperlinks are opened with no scheme check or confirmation

`follow_link` in `crates/ui-egui/src/grid.rs:2284` passes any target containing `://` (or starting with `mailto:`) to `open_url`, which runs `open` / `explorer` / `xdg-open` on it (`open_with_system` in `apps/gridcraft/src/main.rs`). A single click on a link opens it.

So a workbook someone sends you can have a cell link to something like:

- `file:///Users/<name>/Downloads/something.app` or a `.command` / `.sh` file, which launches it
- `smb://attacker-host/share`, which mounts a remote share (and on Windows, `explorer` can leak NTLM credentials)
- custom app URL handlers (`ms-settings:`, `x-apple.systempreferences:`, etc.)

Excel shows a security warning for these. PdfCraft (`DOCUMENT_SCHEMES` in `crates/engine/src/links.rs`) and DeckCraft (`safe_url` in `crates/anim/src/show.rs`) both limit links to `http`, `https` and `mailto`, so GridCraft seems to be the outlier.

**Suggested fix:** use the same allowlist as PdfCraft, and show a confirmation with the full URL before opening.

### 2) The `--control` server has no authentication

`apps/gridcraft/src/control_server.rs` listens on `127.0.0.1:<port>` when started with `--control <port>` or `GRIDCRAFT_CONTROL_PORT`, and runs every JSON line it gets with no token. That includes `app.save` with any `path` (`crates/ui-egui/src/control.rs:377`), so any local process can write files wherever the user can.

It also keeps reading after a line that isn't valid JSON, instead of closing the connection. So a browser request to `http://127.0.0.1:<port>` with a `text/plain` body (no CORS preflight) might get its body line run, after the HTTP header lines fail to parse. Newer Chrome local-network protections may block that, but other browsers may not.

It's opt-in, so this only matters for people who turn it on. But PhotoCraft (`authentication_repl…

title: fix(xlsx): saving drops fileVersion and calcFeatures from workbook.xml, so Excel fully recalculates the file on open (external-workbook lookups open as #CALC!)
author: rex4539
body:
## Summary

When GridCraft saves an XLSX that Excel wrote, it drops two things from `xl/workbook.xml`: the `<fileVersion appName="xl" …/>` element and the `extLst` entry `{B58B0392-4F1F-4190-BB64-5DF3571DCE5F}` (`xcalcf:calcFeatures`). Without **both**, Excel ignores the saved cached values and fully recalculates the workbook on open. Restoring both stops the recalc, and removing either one from an Excel-saved file starts it.

That matters whenever Excel's result differs from the cached one. The common real case is a workbook that reads another workbook through a link, for example `VLOOKUP(x, '[other.xlsx]'!Table[#Data], …)`. Excel can't evaluate a structured reference into a closed workbook, so after a GridCraft save every such cell opens as `#CALC!`. The same file saved by Excel opens with its cached values intact.

## Steps to reproduce

1. Make a workbook and save it once from Excel:

```sh
uv run --with openpyxl python3 -c 'import openpyxl; wb = openpyxl.Workbook(); ws = wb.active; ws["A1"] = 1; ws["B1"] = "=A1*2"; wb.save("excel.xlsx")'
```

Open `excel.xlsx` in Excel, press ⌘S, and close it. B1 is now saved with the cached value `2`.

2. Save it through GridCraft, then give B1 the same stale cache (`99`) in both files, plus a third copy of the GridCraft file with the two workbook.xml elements put back:

```sh
gridcraft-cli run --in excel.xlsx --out gridcraft.xlsx --quiet
python3 patch.py excel.xlsx excel_99.xlsx
python3 patch.py gridcraft.xlsx gridcraft_99.xlsx
python3 patch.py gridcraft.xlsx gridcraft_99_restored.xlsx --restore
```

`patch.py`:

```python
import re, sys, zipfile

src, dst = sys.argv[1], sys.argv[2]
restore = "--restore" in sys.argv
FV = b'<fileVersion appName="xl" lastEdited="7" lowestEdited="7" rupBuild="11008"/>'
EXT = (b'<extLst><ext uri="{B58B0392-4F1F-4190-BB64-5DF3571DCE5F}" '
       b'xmlns:xcalcf="http://schemas.microsoft.com/office/spreadsheetml/2018/calcfeatures"><xcalcf:calcFeatures>'
       b'<xcalcf:feature name="microsoft.com:R…

title: fix(xlsx): Save As to another folder keeps a linked workbook's relative path, so Excel updates the link from the wrong file
author: iluebbe
body:
## Summary

Excel stores the path of a linked workbook relative to the workbook that uses it (`xl/externalLinks/_rels/externalLink1.xml.rels`, `Target="Source.xlsx"`). When Excel saves the workbook into another folder, it rewrites that path (`Target="../Source.xlsx"`). GridCraft keeps external relationship targets as text (`crates/xlsx/src/passthrough.rs:16`). After Save As into another folder, the relative path therefore points next to the new copy:

- If no file of that name is there, the link is broken.
- If there is one, Excel updates the linked formulas from that other file without any warning.

## Observed

Setup: `Source.xlsx` has `Sheet1!A1` = 10. `Dest.xlsx`, made in Excel 365 in the same folder, has `B1 = [Source.xlsx]Sheet1!A1`.

Test: I saved a copy of `Dest.xlsx` into a subfolder `move2\` twice, once with Excel's Save As and once with `gridcraft-cli convert` (main `fc45b7f`; also with #464 merged). `move2\` holds a different `Source.xlsx`, with `Sheet1!A1` = 999. I then opened each copy in Excel 365 with "update links":

| copy in `move2\` | relationship target | Excel's link source | `B1` after updating |
|---|---|---|---|
| saved by Excel | `../Source.xlsx` | `…\links\Source.xlsx` | 10 |
| saved by GridCraft | `Source.xlsx` | `…\links\move2\Source.xlsx` | **999** |

I also saved a GridCraft copy into a subfolder `gc\` that holds no other `Source.xlsx`. There, Excel lists the link as `…\links\gc\Source.xlsx` with status "missing file". The part also keeps the absolute path (`xxl21:absoluteUrl`), but Excel still lists the relative path.

## Suggested fix

On save, when the destination folder differs from the folder the workbook was read from, rebase relative external targets. Resolve each against the original folder, then write it relative to the new folder, or absolute when no relative path exists (another drive), as Excel does. This applies to `externalLinkPath` relationships, and to relative file hyperlinks once they are written as relationships (#80…

title: fix(xls): a defined name that refers to another workbook is dropped, so formulas that use it show #NAME?
author: iluebbe
body:
## Summary

In an `.xls` file, a defined name that refers to another workbook is skipped on open ("Some defined names use references to other workbooks (external links) and were skipped."). Formulas that use the name are still read as formulas, so they calculate to `#NAME?`. Excel shows their saved results. Formulas that refer to the other workbook directly are kept as their saved values and show the right numbers. Only formulas that go through a name break.

## Observed

Made in Excel 365:
1. `Source.xlsx`: `Sheet1!A1:A3` = 10, 20, 30.
2. A new workbook with the name `ExtRange` = `=[Source.xlsx]Sheet1!$A$1:$A$3` and `B6` = `=SUM(ExtRange)`, which gives 60.
3. Saved as `Dest.xls` (Excel 97-2003).

```
gridcraft-cli check Dest.xls      (main fc45b7f, also with #464 merged)
  mismatch Sheet1!B6  =SUM(ExtRange)  expected 60  got #NAME?
```

Excel 365 opens `Dest.xls` (without updating links) with `B6` = 60. The same workbook saved as `.xlsx` gives 60 in GridCraft once #464 is merged.

In Apache POI's test data and Damodaran's spreadsheets, 18 `.xls` files have such names, but `gridcraft-cli check` finds no `#NAME?` from them. The steps above are the reproduction.

## Root cause

`defined_names` (`crates/xlsx/src/xls/mod.rs:764`) skips a name whose formula can't be decoded. The cell formulas that refer to it (`PtgName`) are decoded earlier, without regard to whether the name will be kept.

## Suggested fix

When a cell formula uses a name the reader skips, keep that cell's saved result as a value, as is already done for formulas with external references. A full fix would read the name as a reference into the linked workbook with its cached values (SUPBOOK/CRN), the `.xls` counterpart of #464.

title: fix(xlsx): saving resets the default font (Normal style) to 11 pt, shrinking every default-font cell and moving page breaks
author: rex4539
body:
## Summary

When a workbook's default font (`fonts[0]` in `xl/styles.xml`, the font of the Normal style) is anything other than 11 pt, GridCraft writes it back as 11 pt on save. Every cell that uses the default font changes size: cells with text, empty cells, and anything typed into them later. Rows that auto-fit to the font get shorter, so page breaks move in printed sheets.

title: Perf: TEXT() and chart labels parse the format code for every value
author: vangel76
body:
`TEXT(value, code)` parses the format code on every call (`crates/numfmt/src/lib.rs`, `text_function`). The evaluator calls it once per element, so `=TEXT(A1:A100000,"0.00")` parses the same code 100,000 times. Chart label formatting (`crates/chart/src/resolve.rs`, once per resolved value) does the same.

Parsing depends only on the code text (the date system and the value are applied when formatting), so each distinct code needs parsing once.

Plan: a small bounded per-thread cache of parsed codes inside numfmt (`NumberFormat::parse_cached`), used by `text_function` and the two chart call sites. Results stay identical; tests compare cold, warm and uncached results and count the parses.

I'm working on this.

title: Numfmt: a fraction denominator with 65,536 zeros panics; format codes have no length cap
author: vangel76
body:
**Bug (crash):** a number format code with a fraction denominator of 65,536 or more `0` placeholders panics ("Formatting argument out of range") in `crates/numfmt/src/render.rs` (`format!("{den_s:0>zeros$}")`; Rust format widths are limited to u16).

Repro: code `# ?/` followed by 65,536 `0`, value 0.5, through `format_value` (cell display, chart axes, print, export) and `text_function`. The code can come from an XLSX `numFmt formatCode` (read without a length limit) or a format command.

**Fix plan**
- Build the denominator padding without a `$` width, so no panic path remains.
- Cap format codes at 255 characters (Excel's limit, counted in characters): `NumberFormat::parse` falls back to General for a longer code, `TEXT` returns `#VALUE!`. The stored code is kept as is, so files still open and round-trip.
- Regression tests for both.

I'm working on this.

title: fix(numfmt): format-code parsing is quadratic on long codes, and an unclosed [ splits sections differently from how it tokenizes
author: vangel76
body:
A hostile or just very long number format code makes the format-code parser quadratic, and an unclosed `[` is read differently by its two passes.

**Quadratic time** (`crates/numfmt/src/parse.rs`):
- the tokenizer looked for a `]` after every `[`; with no `]` in the code, n brackets cost O(n²)
- every comma searched ahead for the next non-comma token, so a run of k commas cost O(k²)
- every fraction bar scanned all tokens for an exponent marker, O(n²) for a run of bars

On the pre-fix code, a code of one million `[` did not finish parsing within 20 s (checked); the comma and bar loops are quadratic by reading the code, not timed separately.

**Unclosed `[` disagreement**: `split_sections` kept "inside a bracket" after an unclosed `[`, so later `;` stopped separating sections, while the tokenizer already read that `[` as a literal. `0;[Red-0` with -5 gave `[R19005-0` (the second section was never used as one), and `[0;0` with 5 gave `[0;5` instead of `[5`.

Plan: precompute what the loops need once (last `]`, next non-comma token, last exponent), and make `split_sections` treat an unclosed `[` as a literal like the tokenizer does (the crate has no rejection of unclosed brackets elsewhere; it already treats them as literals). Also parse outside the lock in the engine's format cache.

I'm working on this.

title: PDF writer: text width overflow, all-zero dash arrays, negative stroke widths and NaN sizes
author: vangel76
body:
Review of `crates/pdf` found public-API robustness gaps in `crates/pdf/src/lib.rs`:

- `text_width` sums the glyph widths in a `u32`: roughly 8,000,000 characters of Helvetica `a` overflow it (panic in debug builds, silent wrap in release).
- An all-zero dash array is written as `[0 0] 0 d`, which the PDF specification forbids.
- Zero/negative/NaN stroke widths are written as is (`rect_stroke(width = -3)` writes `-3 w`).
- Guards such as `w <= 0.0` let NaN through: `image_rgba(w = NaN)` stores the image and writes a singular `cm` matrix. Non-finite coordinates are silently turned into 0 and draw at the page origin.

Plan: accumulate widths in `u64`; emit `[] 0 d` (solid) when the sanitised dash array has no positive entry; clamp stroke widths through one helper; skip drawing calls with non-finite or non-positive geometry through one helper, before any image data is stored. Valid input stays byte-identical. Regression tests for each.

title: PDF export: title and author with non-ASCII characters are shown wrong (Info dictionary is WinAnsi, not UTF-16BE)
author: vangel76
body:
PDF export writes the Info dictionary strings (/Title, /Author, /Creator, /Producer) as WinAnsi literal strings. PDF text strings must be PDFDocEncoding or UTF-16BE with a BOM (ISO 32000-1 7.9.2.2), so viewers misread them.

Repro: export a workbook whose title is `Übersicht €5 – “Q1” 日本` (the engine falls back to the file name for the title) and run `pdfinfo` (Poppler). It shows `Übersicht •5 Œ ﬁQ1ﬂ ??`: bytes 0x80-0x9F differ between WinAnsi and PDFDocEncoding, and every character outside Latin-1/WinAnsi becomes `?`.

Fix: keep a literal string for printable ASCII, otherwise write a UTF-16BE hex string `<FEFF…>` (surrogate pairs for characters outside the BMP). Page content text is unchanged (it stays WinAnsi, see #446).

title: PDF writer: q nesting limit, join leak, object buffering, duplicate images, redundant style operators
author: vangel76
body:
Follow-up of the `crates/pdf` review (phase 2: cleanup and optimisation of the writer). Findings in `crates/pdf/src/lib.rs`:

**Correctness**
- Graphics-state nesting is unbounded: `Page::save()` writes any number of `q`, but PDF consumers only have to support 28 nested levels.
- `polyline`/`polygon` set `1 j` without `q`/`Q`, so every rectangle, line or circle stroked afterwards on the page is drawn with round joins.

**Cleanup**
- `/ProcSet` in the page resources is obsolete since PDF 1.4.
- The colour operator formats three floats per operator through a closure.
- Image object and stream assembly is duplicated (RGB image, soft mask, content stream).

**Size / memory**
- `finish()` buffers every object body in a `Vec<(u32, Vec<u8>)>`, sorts it and copies it into the output (page content of up to 64 MB is copied twice).
- The same picture on N pages (or twice on one page) is stored and run-length encoded N times.
- The alpha plane of an opaque image is allocated and filled, then checked in a second pass.
- The full style (colour, width, dash) is re-emitted for every drawing operator.

Not part of this issue: #812 (width overflow, dash, stroke width, NaN), #813 (info strings), compression, metrics/fonts, limits.

Plan: write objects straight into the output (xref needs one offset per id), dedupe images by (size, content hash) with a byte comparison, track the style per page with a q/Q stack and emit only changes, refuse the 29th nested `q` (and ignore its matching `Q`), emit the join explicitly. Tests compare the effective graphics state of every painting operator against a copy of the previous writer over a generated corpus.

title: Numfmt: one built-in format table, no dead render arms, fewer allocations when rendering numbers and General
author: vangel76
body:
Findings S1, S3, O3 and O4 of the `crates/numfmt` review (cleanup, no behaviour change).

**S1: two tables of built-in formats.** `crates/numfmt/src/builtin.rs` and `crates/xlsx/src/tables.rs` hold the same 36-entry table. `gridcraft_numfmt::{builtin_format, builtin_id}` are used by nothing but numfmt's own tests, and the two `builtin_id`s differ (xlsx: exact match, ids 5-8 excluded because their meaning depends on the reader's locale; numfmt: case-insensitive, backslashes ignored). The file-format crates must not depend on numfmt (`cargo xtask layers`), so the table stays with the file formats and numfmt's unused copy goes.

**S3: dead code in `render_number` / `Tok::literal_text`.** The `Tok::At | General | Date | Comma` arm prints nothing, which is what the fallback does anyway (no code ever gives these tokens a piece); `Comma` cannot occur after analysis, `General` and `Date` sections are rendered elsewhere. `literal_text` allocated a `String` per call inside the render loops.

**O3: allocations per number.** `render_number` allocated `pieces`, `before` and `lits` (one `String` per token), `fill_int` built a reversed string per placeholder, and `render_date` rescanned the tokens three times per call (sub-second digits, calendar parts, AM/PM) and built a string per part.

**O4: General.** `significant_digits` formatted into a `String` and collected a `Vec` per number; `format_general_fit` re-ran `fixed_from_digits` (new `Vec` and two `String`s each) for every width it tried.

Plan: one table in xlsx (with tests pinning its lookup rules), no dead arm and no per-call literal strings, one scratch buffer per number instead of per-token strings, the date flags computed once when a section is parsed, and the General width loop reusing its buffers. Output must not change: an equality test compares `format_value`, `TEXT()` (both date systems) and `format_general_fit` with digests recorded from the old code over 152 format codes x 75 values and 555 values x 38 widths.

title: Rows do not auto-fit oversized fonts: 20pt text in a default-height row is clipped (pre-existing, found via #774 mixed-font testing)
author: edurbs
body:
Found while visually verifying #774 with per-run font families/sizes (not a regression of that work — a plain cell without any runs clips identically).

## What happens

A cell whose font (whole-cell or rich-run) is taller than its row height renders top-anchored and clipped: the baseline is placed at `row_top + ascent`, which lands below the row's bottom gridline, so the bottom of every glyph above the baseline is sliced and descenders are erased, while a blank strip sits at the top of the row.

Control repro (plain cell, no rich runs): workbook with `A5 = "plain big bold 20pt"`, whole-cell font Arial 20pt bold, default-height row. Rendered (offscreen snapshot, scale 2, 30px = 15pt rows):

- row 5 interior y 567–596; ink only y 574–597 (24px of an expected ≈37px ascender→descender span, ~35% of glyph height lost)
- flat cut across all glyphs at the bottom gridline; `p`/`g` descenders 100% gone; ~7px blank band at the row top
- 11pt rows (A1–A4) center normally — only rows shorter than the font clip

Rich-run cells with mixed sizes (11/16/20pt runs in one cell) hit the same path via the shared `cell_text_y` call (`crates/ui-egui/src/grid.rs`, single-line paint), consistent with the flat path — parity kept.

## Excel behaviour (to verify against the installed app)

Excel auto-fits row height for rows without `customHeight` when content uses a bigger font, so 20pt text normally gets a taller row on open; rows explicitly marked `customHeight` clip. GridCraft keeps the file/default height and clips either way.

## Possible fix direction

On import (and on font-size edits), grow non-`customHeight` rows to fit their tallest font (line height of the cell font, or max run font for rich cells); leave `customHeight` rows clipping as Excel does.

## Evidence

Offscreen snapshot renders used for measurement are outside the repo (AGENTS.md asset rules); the pixel measurements above are from `image-analyst` inspection. Repro workbooks are trivially rebuilt in code from the descri…

title: Feature request: update checker and in-place updates on Windows and macOS (plus winget/Scoop/Homebrew)
author: richard1912
body:
## Summary
There's no way to update GridCraft from inside the app on Windows or macOS. The Linux AppImage already updates itself via zsync (`docs/releasing.md`), but on Windows (MSI or portable zip) and macOS you have to notice a new release on GitHub, download it and replace the old build by hand. With releases landing every day or two, people end up running old builds and hitting bugs that are already fixed.

## Proposal
In keeping with the project's no-telemetry, no-GridCraft-servers approach:

### 1. Check for updates (opt-in)
- A **File > Account / Help > Check for Updates** command (e.g. `file.checkForUpdates`), plus an optional "check on startup" setting that is **off by default** or asked once on first run.
- Reads the public GitHub Releases API (`/repos/storytold/gridcraft/releases/latest`). No identifiers, no telemetry, nothing sent beyond a normal anonymous HTTPS request.
- Shows the new version and release notes, with a "Download" or "Update" action.
- Like every command, also reachable from the CLI, control channel and MCP (e.g. `gridcraft-cli update --check`).

### 2. In-place update
- Download the matching asset for the current platform/arch and install type (MSI, portable zip, DMG).
- Verify it against the published `SHA256SUMS.txt` (and the existing code signature) before using it.
- Apply after the app exits (a small helper or the MSI's own upgrade path), then relaunch. Never interrupt an open workbook with unsaved changes.
- Portable installs: swap the folder in place so settings and shortcuts keep working.

### 3. Package managers (quick win)
Publish manifests from the release workflow so the OS tools can handle updates:
- Windows: **winget** (`winget upgrade`) and **Scoop**
- macOS: **Homebrew** cask (`brew upgrade`)
- Linux: AUR is already requested in #236; Flatpak builds exist and could go on Flathub.

This is mostly CI configuration and could come before 1 and 2.

## Why
- Matches the "never lose people's work" priority: fixes only help peop…

title: XLSX: XML maps are dropped on save (xmlMaps, xmlColumnPr, singleXmlCells), breaking Business Central package import
author: CouchRiv
body:
## Summary

Saving an `.xlsx` that uses **XML maps** drops the map and every binding to it. On GridCraft 0.6.1 (`main` = `v0.6.1`), `gridcraft-cli convert in.xlsx out.xlsx` (and open → save in the app) removes:

| Part / element | Before | After save |
|---|---|---|
| `xl/xmlMaps.xml` (workbook rel `.../relationships/xmlMaps`) | present | **dropped** |
| `xl/tables/tableSingleCellsN.xml` (sheet rel `.../relationships/tableSingleCells`) | present | **dropped** |
| `<xmlColumnPr mapId xpath xmlDataType>` and `uniqueName` on `<tableColumn>` | 2 | **0** |
| `tableType="xml"` / `connectionId` on `<table>` | present | **dropped** |
| `xl/connections.xml` (the XML connection the map binds to) | present | kept, now orphaned |

`gridcraft-cli check in.xlsx --json` still reports `roundTrip.categories.package: {"diffs": 0, "equal": true}`, so the loss is silent.

## Why it matters: Microsoft Dynamics 365 Business Central

Business Central (RapidStart) exports configuration packages to Excel as exactly this shape: an XML map (`/DataList/<Table>List/...`), an XML table whose columns carry `xmlColumnPr` xpaths, and single XML cells A1 (package code) and C1 (table ID). Its **Import from Excel** needs them:

- `OpenXMLManagement.ExtractXMLSchema` errors with *"The Excel workbook must contain an XML map."* when `WorkbookPart.CustomXmlMappingsPart` is missing (Base Application, `System/OpenXMLManagement.Codeunit.al`, lines 20 and 325-338).
- `ConfigExcelExchange.InitColumnMapping` only reads table columns whose `XmlColumnProperties.XPath` is set (`System/RapidStart/ConfigExcelExchange.Codeunit.al`, `ImportExcel` line 361, `InitColumnMapping` line 747). Without `xmlColumnPr`, no column is imported.

Source: public mirror of the BC Base Application, https://github.com/StefanMaron/MSDyn365BC.Code.History, branch `w1-29`.

body:
## Summary
Excel has a **Close All** command that closes every open workbook in one go, asking Save / Don't Save / Cancel for each one with unsaved changes. Many people pin it to the Quick Access Toolbar and rely on it heavily. GridCraft has no equivalent: each workbook has to be closed one at a time with Ctrl+W, and the title-bar toolbar can't be customised to add it.

## Request
### 1. A `file.closeAll` command
- Closes every open workbook (all windows/processes if workbooks run separately, see #171).
- For each workbook with unsaved changes, shows the existing Save Changes dialog (Save / Don't Save / Cancel). **Cancel stops the whole operation** and leaves the remaining workbooks open, like Excel.
- Reachable like every command: File menu, keytips, CLI/control channel/MCP (with a `force`/`save` param for programmatic use, never opening dialogs when called programmatically).

### 2. Customisable Quick Access Toolbar
- Let users add any command (including Close All) to the title-bar toolbar, and remove or reorder the defaults, persisted in settings.
- At minimum, add Close All to the existing "More commands" menu as a first step.

## Notes
- Depends on the window-close save prompt work in #496 / #846 (for #694, #838, #841), so the same dialog path can be reused and Close All never discards unsaved work.
- If workbooks open in separate processes, Close All needs a way to reach the other instances (e.g. a single-instance/IPC mechanism), which ties in with #171.

title: fix(xlsx): this-row structured references are saved as [@Col], so Excel repairs the file and removes the tables
author: richard1912
body:
## Summary
Saving a workbook whose tables have **calculated columns using this-row structured references** produces a file Excel can't open normally. Excel offers to repair it, and the repair **removes those tables** (and some cell formulas).

## Cause
In the file format, a this-row reference must be written in its long form, `Table1[[#This Row],[Col]]`. `Table1[@Col]` is only the display shorthand Excel shows in the UI and isn't valid in the XML.

GridCraft converts long form to shorthand on read (PR #420, test at `crates/xlsx/src/fmla.rs:152`: `from_file("Sales[[#This Row],Units]*...") == "Sales[@Units]*..."`), but `to_file` / `text_to_file` never convert it back. So every `[@...]` is written verbatim into `<calculatedColumnFormula>` in `xl/tables/tableN.xml`, and into cell `<f>` elements in the sheet XML.

## Repro
1. In Excel, create a table with columns `A` and `B`, and make `B` a calculated column `=[@A]*2`. Save as `.xlsx`.
2. Open it in GridCraft (v0.6.1) and save it without changes (or `gridcraft-cli run --in t.xlsx --out t2.xlsx`).
3. Open `t2.xlsx` in Excel: "We found a problem with some content…". The repair removes the table.

Seen on a real workbook (~15 sheets): Excel's repair log listed `Removed Records: Table from /xl/tables/tableN.xml part (Table)` for **exactly** the 5 tables whose calculated columns used `[@...]`, plus `Removed Records: Formula from /xl/worksheets/sheetN.xml` for a sheet with ~80 cell formulas using `[@...]` (0 using `#This Row`). The 2 tables whose calculated columns didn't use this-row references survived.

Example of what's written (original → saved):
```
tblIsolations[[#This Row],[Station]]&" "&tblIsolations[[#This Row],[Platform]]
tblIsolations[@Station]&" "&tblIsolations[@Platform]
```

## Expected
`to_file` rewrites `Table[@Col]` → `Table[[#This Row],[Col]]`, `Table[@[Col name]]` → `Table[[#This Row],[Col name]]`, and the unqualified `[@Col]` form inside a table the same way, for both cell formulas and `calculatedColumnFor…

title: XLSX: saving silently drops the sensitivity label (LabelInfo.xml), table column formats and sheet custom properties
author: richard1912
body:
## Summary
Opening and saving a real-world `.xlsm` (no edits) silently dropped several parts that aren't in the #330 pass-through list. There was no warning on open or save for any of them.

| Dropped | Effect |
|---|---|
| `docMetadata/LabelInfo.xml` (Microsoft Purview / MIP **sensitivity label**) | The organisation's classification label is removed from the file. In many workplaces this is a compliance problem (labels drive DLP, encryption and handling rules), and the user isn't told. |
| `dataDxfId` / `dataCellStyle` on `<tableColumn>` | Table column default formatting is lost (new rows no longer pick up the column's number format and style). |
| Sheet `<customProperties>` / `<customPr>` and their `xl/customPropertyN.bin` parts | Worksheet custom properties (used by VBA `Worksheet.CustomProperties` and add-ins, here an SAP EPM key) are lost. |
| `xl/drawings/drawingN.xml` anchor for a form-control button (`<xdr:sp>` "Button 2") | The control's VML and ctrlProp are kept, so the button probably still shows; worth checking it stays positioned correctly. |

Also dropped, and fine as far as I can tell: `xl/calcChain.xml`, and `xl/richData/*` holding only `_error` rich values (Excel rebuilds both).

## Suggestion
- Keep `docMetadata/LabelInfo.xml` (and its package relationship) verbatim on save, or at least **warn** that the sensitivity label will be removed. This one matters most.
- Read/write `dataDxfId` and `dataCellStyle` on table columns.
- Add sheet custom properties to the pass-through.

Related: #330 (pass-through), https://github.com/storytold/gridcraft/issues/864 (the same round trip also produced a file Excel had to repair).

body:

title: Saving to an unrecognised extension silently writes an XLSX file under that name
author: SteamSmith
body:
**What happens:** saving to a path whose extension GridCraft doesn't recognise writes an `.xlsx` package under that exact name, with no warning, and the file then becomes the document's file.

**To reproduce** (GridCraft 0.5.0, Windows):

```
gridcraft-cli run --sample sales --out report.foo
```

It prints `wrote …\report.foo (11127 bytes)` and exits 0. The file starts with `PK\x03\x04`: it's an XLSX (ZIP) package named `report.foo`.

**Where** (current `main`, fc45b7f):
- `crates/engine/src/io.rs` `FileKind::from_path` (lines 25–38) returns `None` for any other extension (or none at all).
- `save_bytes` (line 157) then falls back with `FileKind::from_path(path).unwrap_or(FileKind::Xlsx)`.
- `cmd/file.rs` `save` (lines 110–115) applies the same fallback. Because XLSX counts as full fidelity, it clears the dirty flag and sets the document's path to `report.foo`, so later saves keep writing an XLSX there.

**Why it's surprising:** a typo like `report.cvs` or `report.xslx` produces a file that other apps won't recognise, and the save reports success.

**Possible behaviours** (your call):
- Refuse unknown extensions with an error that lists the supported ones.
- Append `.xlsx` when the extension is missing or unknown, the way a Save As dialog adds the default extension, so `report.foo` would become `report.foo.xlsx`.
- At minimum, include a warning in the command's reply.
