title: Calc: SORT/SORTBY (and the order of UNIQUE results) compare text by code point; Excel uses locale collation (hyphens ignored, `_` before digits, accented letters with their base letter)
author: KNUFFIXX
body:
**Summary.** `=SORT(UNIQUE(HKVs[Wohnung]))` over apartment codes orders `JO30-WE-1-` before `JO30-WE01-EGH`; Excel (the cached result in the file and a live COM check) orders `JO30-WE01-EGH` first, because Excel's text sort ignores hyphens and apostrophes at the first level (word sort) and sorts case-insensitively with the locale's collation. Spill ranges therefore differ from Excel row by row.

**Steps to reproduce.** Fixture [`gc_sort_collation.xlsx`](https://github.com/KNUFFIXX/artcraft-fixtures/blob/main/gridcraft/gc_sort_collation.xlsx) ([download](https://github.com/KNUFFIXX/artcraft-fixtures/raw/main/gridcraft/gc_sort_collation.xlsx)) (5 KB): A1:A19 text `x-1, x01, JO30-WE-1-, JO30-WE01-EGH, a-b, ab, AB, a c, a-c, ac, Ärger, Zebra, apfel, Apfel, _x, x_, 1, 10, 2`; C1 `=SORT(A1:A19)`, E1 `=SORTBY(A1:A19,A1:A19,-1)`.
`gridcraft-cli cat gc_sort_collation.xlsx --range C1:E19 --csv`

**Expected (Excel 365, de-DE; en-US gives the same order for this list).** `_x | 1 | 10 | 2 | a c | ab | AB | a-b | ac | a-c | apfel | Apfel | Ärger | JO30-WE01-EGH | JO30-WE-1- | x_ | x01 | x-1 | Zebra`.

**Actual (0.5.0 and 0.6.1).** `1 | 10 | 2 | _x | a c | a-b | a-c | ab | AB | ac | apfel | Apfel | JO30-WE-1- | JO30-WE01-EGH | x-1 | x01 | x_ | Zebra | Ärger` — case-insensitive code-point order: `_` after the digits, `-` before letters, `Ä` after `Z`.

**Analysis.** Excel's documented sort order for text: case-insensitive; apostrophes and hyphens are ignored, except that two strings equal but for a hyphen keep the hyphen-free one first; otherwise the locale's collation (as in `CompareString`/ICU: letters with diacritics next to their base letter, punctuation and symbols before digits before letters). title: Report: a real-world corpus run of 663 workbooks against 0.5.0 — formula oracle, round-trip fidelity, and whether Excel opens what GridCraft saves
author: KNUFFIXX
body:
docs/gaps.md §1 lists "a run over a real-world XLSX corpus, and confirmation that Excel opens what we save with no repair prompt" as the first beta blocker. This is such a run; the individual findings are filed as separate issues, this is the overview.

**Corpus.** 663 distinct workbooks (470 `.xlsx`, 193 `.xlsm`; 285 MB) from a German property-management office: tenant lists, heating-cost and service-charge calculations, meter-reading lists, account sheets, loan schedules — 2017–2026, written by Excel 2003-era versions up to Microsoft 365 (442 last saved by Excel, 9 by openpyxl, the rest without `app.xml`), with tables, dynamic arrays, external links, VBA, conditional formats, data validations, pictures in cells. title: [GridCraft] Short dates do not display properly
author: ticket-craft

title: Keytips: Alt, F doesn't open the File menu (no "F" tab entry, only hidden FA/FC/FO… sequences)
author: richard1912
body:
## Summary
In Excel, pressing **Alt, F** (or F10, F) opens the **File** tab (Backstage view) and shows keytips for its pages (N New, O Open, A Save As, P Print, C Close, I Info, and so on). In GridCraft (v0.6.1, Windows) **Alt, F does nothing visible**: the File menu doesn't open and no keytips appear.

## Cause
In `crates/ui-egui/src/keytips/keytip_table/generated.rs`, every other ribbon tab has a single-letter `Entry::Tab` (H Home, N Insert, P Page Layout, M Formulas, A Data, R Review, W View, plus the legacy E and O), but there's **no `"F"` entry**. File is only reachable through the hidden two-letter sequences (`FA`, `FC`, `FI`, `FN`, `FO`, `FP`), which fire if you already know them but give no visual feedback after the F.

## Expected
- **Alt, F** opens the File menu / Backstage (the same view as clicking File), with keytip badges on its items.
- The second letter then acts as now (Alt, F, O → Open; Alt, F, C → Close; …), and Esc backs out one level, closing the File view.
- Works with F10 as well as Alt, like the other tabs.

## Related
- PR #411 / #412 (table-driven keytip system, the full Excel Alt table)
- #861 (Close All; Alt, F, C is the usual keyboard path to Close)

title: Docs: add a contributing guide and issue templates (bug, parity, feature)
author: richard1912
body:
## Summary
GridCraft has no contributing guide or issue templates (GitHub's community profile shows no `CONTRIBUTING`, no `.github/ISSUE_TEMPLATE`, no PR template). Issues currently arrive in many shapes and title styles: `fix(xlsx): …`, `Parity: …`, `[Parity]: …`, `[Bug] …`, `Feature request: …`, and `[GridCraft] …` from the Discord ticket bot. That makes duplicates harder to spot and triage slower, especially with the volume of agent-written issues and PRs.

## Request
1. **`CONTRIBUTING.md`** (or `docs/contributing.md`, as PhotoCraft has), covering:
   - the preferred issue **title convention** (e.g. `fix(area): …` for bugs, `Parity: …` for missing Excel behaviour, `feat(area): …` for new ideas)
   - what a good report includes: GridCraft version and platform, steps to reproduce, expected vs actual (Excel's behaviour for parity), files or a minimal synthetic repro (never real customer files), and the code location if known
   - etiquette: search first, comment "I'm on this one" before starting a PR (as designcraft#361 suggests), use `Fixes #n` vs `Refs #n`
   - PR expectations: `cargo xtask ci`, tests, one task per commit, `Co-Authored-By` for AI help
2. **Issue forms** in `.github/ISSUE_TEMPLATE/`: Bug, Excel parity gap, Feature request, plus a `config.yml` pointing to Discord `#tickets` for quick questions.
3. Optionally, make the Discord ticket bot fill the same template fields.

## Related
- lightcraft#648 (issue templates) and lightcraft#1184 (no written contribution workflow)
- craft-libs#37 (shared CONTRIBUTING.md across the craft apps). A shared craftrules standard could cover all apps at once.

title: Parity: show the version and About GridCraft in the File view (Excel: File > Account)
author: richard1912
body:
## Summary
GridCraft's **About GridCraft** window (version, Contributors, Models) is only reachable from **Automate > About GridCraft** on Windows and Linux (plus the app menu on macOS). That's hard to find: the File view (`crates/ui-egui/src/backstage.rs`: Home, New, Open, Info, Save As, Print, Export, Options) never shows the version or links to About.

In Excel the equivalent lives in the File view: **File > Account** shows the product and version info, with an **About Excel** button for the full build details.

## Proposal
1. Add an **Account** (or **About**) page to the File view, at the bottom of the page list near Options, showing:
   - GridCraft name and version (`CARGO_PKG_VERSION`), platform/arch, and licence (MIT OR Apache-2.0)
   - an **About GridCraft** button opening the existing dialog (Contributors and Models tabs)
   - a natural home for **Check for Updates** once #859 lands
2. Optionally, show the version as small text at the bottom of the File view's left pane, so it's visible at a glance.
3. Keep **Automate > About GridCraft** if wanted. Keytip **Alt, F, D** would match Excel's Account letter (see #893).

## Related
- #859 (update checker): "Check for Updates" fits on this page
- #893 (Alt, F opening the File view with page keytips)

title: Parity: mouse wheel over the ribbon switches tabs
author: richard1912
body:
## Summary
In Excel for Microsoft 365 on Windows, hovering the mouse over the ribbon (tab row or ribbon body) and turning the scroll wheel **switches ribbon tabs**: down moves to the next tab (Home → Insert → Draw → …), up to the previous one. It's a quick way to browse the ribbon without clicking. In GridCraft (v0.6.1, Windows) the wheel does nothing over the ribbon.

## Cause
`crates/ui-egui/src/ribbon.rs` has no wheel handling for tab switching. The only scroll there is the hidden horizontal `ScrollArea` around the ribbon body (around line 233) for overflow.

## Proposal
- Wheel **down** over the tab row or ribbon body selects the next tab, **up** the previous one. **Stop** at the first and last tab (no wrap-around), as Excel does.
- One tab per wheel notch. Accumulate smooth/trackpad scroll deltas to a threshold so a precision touchpad doesn't race through every tab.
- **Don't** switch while a dropdown, gallery or menu is open, or when the pointer is over a control that scrolls itself (font list, galleries, the horizontal overflow scroll), and don't switch while the File view is open.
- Optional: a setting to turn it off (some users find accidental tab switches annoying).

## Related
- #406 (ribbon improvements)
- PR #675 (responsive ribbon / groups collapsing into dropdowns): the overflow scroll should keep priority when the ribbon is narrow

title: fix(grid): selection waits for mouse release, and a press held 0.8 s or longer selects nothing
author: richard1912
body:
## Summary
GridCraft only changes the selection when the mouse button is **released** (or once the pointer has moved past the drag threshold). Excel selects the cell **the instant the button goes down**. Worse, a press held **0.8 s or longer** that stays within the drag threshold **selects nothing at all**, so a slow click, or "press, nudge within the cell, pause, release", leaves the old selection in place.

**Expected (Excel):** button down on a cell → that cell is selected immediately. Then either release (that cell stays selected) or move while holding (the range extends live from that cell) and release.

## How this was tested
GridCraft v0.6.1, Windows 11, 150% display scaling. **Real OS mouse input** (`SetCursorPos` + `mouse_event` down/up as separate events), with the selection read through the control channel (`document.inspect`) while the button was still held and again after release. Before each run F14 was selected, then the press was on C8 (default column width and row height). Each row was run 3 times with identical results.

### 1. Nothing is selected on press
| Press on C8 | Selection while held | After release |
|---|---|---|
| Quick click (60 ms) | n/a | C8 |
| Held still, checked at 300 ms and 800 ms | **F14** (unchanged) | C8 |
| Moved 1.5 / 3 / 4.5 / 6 px inside C8 | **F14** | C8 |
| Moved 7.5 px or more inside C8 | C8 | C8 |
| Dragged C8 → E10 | C8:E10 (live) | C8:E10 |

So the selection appears only once the pointer travels past egui's drag threshold (~5 points here); below that it waits for release.

### 2. Long presses select nothing
| Press on C8, then release (no checks during the press) | After release |
|---|---|
| Still, 500 / 600 / 650 / 700 / 750 ms | C8 |
| Still, **800 / 850 / 900 ms** | **F14 (nothing selected)** |
| Moved 4.5 px early, then still, total **800 / 850 / 900 ms** | **F14 (nothing selected)** |
| Held 600-1500 ms with 1-unit jitter every 60 ms | C8 |

The cutoff matches egui's default `max_click_duration` (0.8 s). Past …

title: fix(functions): a function name passed as an argument (=BYROW(A1:B2,SUM), =GROUPBY(...,SUM)) returns an error
author: bramheerink
body:
GridCraft 0.6.1 (rpm, Fedora 44, x86_64).

## What we did

Evaluated formulas that pass a function by name, the way Excel writes them:

```sh
gridcraft-cli eval '=SUM(BYROW({1,2;3,4},SUM))'
gridcraft-cli eval '=REDUCE(0,{1,2,3},SUM)'
gridcraft-cli eval '=ROWS(GROUPBY({"a";"b";"a"},{1;2;3},SUM))'
gridcraft-cli eval '=ROWS(GROUPBY({"a";"b";"a"},{1;2;3},_xleta.SUM))'
gridcraft-cli eval '=ROWS(PIVOTBY({"a";"b";"a"},{"x";"x";"y"},{1;2;3},SUM))'
```

## What came out

| Formula | Result |
|---|---|
| `=SUM(BYROW({1,2;3,4},SUM))` | `#VALUE!` |
| `=REDUCE(0,{1,2,3},SUM)` | `#VALUE!` |
| `=ROWS(GROUPBY(...,SUM))` | `#NAME?` |
| `=ROWS(GROUPBY(...,_xleta.SUM))` | `#NAME?` |
| `=ROWS(PIVOTBY(...,SUM))` | `#NAME?` |

Controls that do work: `=SUM(BYROW({1,2;3,4},LAMBDA(r,SUM(r))))` gives 10, and `=ROWS(GROUPBY({"a";"b";"a"},{1;2;3},"SUM"))` (name as text) gives 3.

## Why we think this is wrong

Excel accepts a bare function name wherever a LAMBDA is expected (10, 6 and 3 for the first three formulas above), and it is the documented way to call GROUPBY and PIVOTBY. Excel stores it in the file as `_xleta.SUM`, so a workbook saved by Excel that uses GROUPBY or PIVOTBY this way opens in GridCraft showing `#NAME?`.

title: fix(functions): GROUPBY with a LAMBDA as its function returns #CALC!
author: bramheerink
body:
GridCraft 0.6.1 (rpm, Fedora 44, x86_64).

## What we did

```sh
gridcraft-cli eval '=ROWS(GROUPBY({"a";"b";"a"},{1;2;3},LAMBDA(x,SUM(x))))'
gridcraft-cli eval '=ROWS(GROUPBY({"a";"b";"a"},{1;2;3},"SUM"))'
```

## What came out

The first returns `#CALC!`. The second, with the function given as text, returns 3 (rows a, b and Total).

## Why we think this is wrong

Excel accepts a custom LAMBDA as the `function` argument of GROUPBY, and `LAMBDA(x,SUM(x))` should give the same result as SUM, so the first formula should also return 3. Together with the bare-function-name issue filed separately, this means GROUPBY currently only works when the function is passed as a text string, which is not a form Excel writes.

title: fix(functions): CELL("address") drops the sheet name for a reference to another sheet
author: bramheerink
body:
GridCraft 0.6.1 (rpm, Fedora 44, x86_64).

## What we did

In a workbook with two sheets named `T` and `D`, evaluated on sheet `T`:

```sh
gridcraft-cli eval '=CELL("address",D!C7)' --in book.xlsx --sheet T
```

## What came out

`$C$7`, the same text as for `=CELL("address",C7)` on the sheet itself.

## Why we think this is wrong

Excel includes the sheet (and workbook) name when the reference points at another sheet, for example `[book.xlsx]D!$C$7`. LibreOffice returns `D!$C$7` for the same file. Without the sheet name the result is ambiguous, and a formula that feeds it back into INDIRECT silently reads the wrong sheet.

title: Rich text: copy and fill do not propagate runs — filled or pasted cells come out flat
author: edurbs
body:
Follow-up to #776 (rich-text editing), extracted from its non-goals.

## What

Filling (drag-fill, fill commands) or copying rich cells produces flat text: the runs side-table entries are not propagated to the destination cells. Cut-move, sort, insert/delete row/column and remove-duplicates already translate runs (milestone 1, #774); copy/fill deliberately stayed flat.

## Expected (Excel behavior)

- Fill of a rich cell repeats its runs into each filled cell (offsets re-based per cell).
- Paste of a rich cell reproduces its runs at the destination (Excel does carry rich formatting through its own clipboard).

## Where

`crates/engine/src/cmd/data.rs` (fill) and the paste path in `crates/engine/src/cmd/edit.rs` (a copy already collects runs for cut-move at edit.rs ~:966 — a copy-paste currently drops them). The model helper for re-basing is `CellRuns::edited` or a direct clone (same text).

Note: HTML clipboard fidelity for external paste is a separate follow-up issue.

title: Rich text: runs are lost when a rich cell is copied to the clipboard as HTML (colors don't paste out)
author: edurbs
body:
Follow-up to #776 (rich-text editing), extracted from its non-goals.

## What

A cell with rich-text runs copies out as flat text: the HTML clipboard path (the copy-as-HTML table from #36) emits no per-run `<span style>` colors, so pasting into Excel or a browser loses the run colors. Internal paste already stays flat by design (milestone-1 scope).

## Expected

Copy of a rich cell produces HTML where each run's font delta becomes the corresponding `<span>\> style (color first; then bold/italic/underline/strike/size/name as available), so external targets render the mixed formatting. XLSX round-trip already preserves runs (#774).

## Where

The clipboard write path in `crates/ui-egui` (HTML export) + the runs side-table `Sheet.cell_runs`; the run-to-style mapping can reuse `RunFont::merged`.

title: fix(formula): a flat chain of more than 400 operands (=A1+A2+…) returns #CALC!
author: bramheerink
body:
GridCraft 0.6.1 (rpm, Fedora 44, x86_64).

## What we did

Evaluated a flat sum of 400 and of 401 terms:

```sh
gridcraft-cli eval "=$(python3 -c "print(\"+\".join([\"1\"]*400))")"
gridcraft-cli eval "=$(python3 -c "print(\"+\".join([\"1\"]*401))")"
```

## What came out

400 terms gives `400`. 401 terms gives `#CALC!`. The same limit applies to chains of `*` and `&`.

## Why we think this is wrong

Excel has no limit on the number of operands in a chain; its limits are 8,192 characters and 64 levels of *nested functions*, and a flat chain is not nesting. `=1+1+…` with 401 terms is 802 characters, and `=A1+A2+…+A401` is about 2,000, both well inside what Excel accepts and calculates. Hand-built workbooks that add a long list of individual cells would show `#CALC!` here.

This looks like the depth bound added for #527 (one tree level per operand). The bound itself is reasonable; evaluating or building a left-associative chain iteratively would keep it without rejecting valid formulas.

title: fix(calc): a recursive LAMBDA stops at 131 calls deep with #CALC!
author: bramheerink
body:
GridCraft 0.6.1 (rpm, Fedora 44, x86_64).

## What we did

Called a self-recursive LAMBDA with two parameters that counts down from n:

```sh
gridcraft-cli eval '=LET(F,LAMBDA(me,n,IF(n<=0,0,1+me(me,n-1))),F(F,131))'
gridcraft-cli eval '=LET(F,LAMBDA(me,n,IF(n<=0,0,1+me(me,n-1))),F(F,132))'
```

## What came out

n = 131 gives `131`. n = 132 and anything larger gives `#CALC!`.

## Why we think this is wrong

Excel allows deeper recursion. Its documented limit is an operand stack of 1,024 entries shared across the parameters of each call, which for a two-parameter LAMBDA is several hundred levels, and it reports `#NUM!` when the limit is hit. We did not run this in Excel, so the exact Excel depth is from documentation rather than measured.

A workbook that uses a recursive LAMBDA over a few hundred items (walking a string character by character, for example) calculates in Excel and fails here. Low priority; filed so the limit and the error code are a deliberate choice rather than an accident.

title: Parity: colour menus have no "More Colors…" (custom RGB/hex) or Recent Colors
author: richard1912
body:
## Summary
In v0.6.1 (Windows 11) the Fill Color dropdown, and every other colour menu, only offers the fixed theme and standard swatches. There is no way to apply an exact colour (for example a corporate RGB or hex value), and no row of recently used colours. Excel's colour menus end with **Recent Colors** and **More Colors…**, which opens a picker for any colour.

## Repro
1. Home ▸ Fill Color ▸ dropdown arrow.
2. The menu shows No Fill, Theme Colors and Standard Colors only. Nothing lets you enter or pick a custom colour.

## Cause
All colour menus share `color_palette` in `crates/ui-egui/src/widgets.rs`, which only draws the swatch grid. Its callers: Fill Color and Font Color (`ribbon.rs`), the sheet tab colour (`tabs.rs`), two dialog pickers (`dialogs.rs`) and a pane picker (`panes.rs`). One change there would cover all of them.

## Proposal
- A **More Colors…** item at the bottom of the palette that opens a colour picker: RGB and HSL fields, hex input, a hue/saturation area, and a new/current preview. GridCraft's own drawing; egui's built-in colour picker could be a starting point.
- A **Recent Colors** row showing the last custom colours used (up to 10), kept for the session or stored in preferences.
- Keyboard reachable like the existing swatches, with keytips matching the menu.
- Optional: an eyedropper to pick a colour from the grid.

title: fix(ui): Merge & Center and Wrap Text captions are not clickable, and UI text (ribbon, status bar) is selectable
author: richard1912
body:
## Summary
In v0.6.1 (Windows 11), on Home ▸ Alignment, the "Merge & Center" and "Wrap Text" captions are not part of their buttons. Clicking the words does nothing; instead the text gets selected like page text (a drag highlights part of the caption). Only the icon (and the dropdown arrow for Merge & Center) responds. In Excel the whole button, icon and caption, is one hover/click target.

## Repro
1. Select a few cells, Home tab.
2. Click the word "Merge & Center": nothing merges.
3. Drag across the word: part of the caption is highlighted as selected text.
4. Same for "Wrap Text".

## Cause
`crates/ui-egui/src/ribbon.rs` draws the button and then a separate `ui.label(...)` for the caption:
- Wrap Text: `toggle_button(ui, Icon::Wrap, ...)` at line 734, caption label at line 739
- Merge & Center: `split_button(ui, Icon::Merge, None, ...)` at line 765, caption label at line 770

Labels are selectable because `style.interaction.selectable_labels` is never turned off (egui's default is `true`), so any plain label in the app's chrome can be selected.

## Proposal
- Make the caption part of the button: the icon plus text share one hover highlight and one click target (and for Merge & Center, the split stays between the main part and the arrow), as in Excel.
- Set `selectable_labels = false` for UI chrome (ribbon, dialogs, status bar), keeping selection only where copying text is useful (messages, cell contents).
- Check other ribbon groups for the same button-plus-separate-label pattern.

title: Parity: Zoom dialog is oversized, pre-selects nothing, shows "100.0" and has no Fit Selection
author: richard1912
body:
## Summary
In v0.6.1 (Windows 11) the View ▸ Zoom dialog is much larger than its content and differs from Excel's in several ways:
- about half the dialog is empty space between "Custom (%)" and the buttons;
- no Magnification option is selected even when the sheet is at one of them (100% here);
- the custom box shows `100.0` instead of `100`;
- "Custom" is a separate number field, not a radio choice with its box beside it;
- there is no **Fit Selection** choice (zoom so the selected range fills the window).

Excel's Zoom dialog is a compact single column: 200%, 100%, 75%, 50%, 25%, Fit Selection, Custom [ ]%, then OK/Cancel, with the current zoom pre-selected (or Custom filled in when it matches none).

## Repro
1. View ▸ Zoom (sheet at 100%).
2. Note the empty area, no option selected, and `100.0` in the custom box.

## Cause
The dialog is the generic `Dialog::form("zoom", ...)` in `crates/ui-egui/src/dialogs.rs` (around line 525): a `Choice` with five presets plus a separate `Number { key: "percent" }`, laid out at the form's default size. The initial params set only `percent`, so no preset radio matches, and the number field formats as a float.

## Proposal
- Size the dialog to its content (or give the form a compact size for small dialogs generally).
- One radio group: 200, 100, 75, 50, 25, Fit Selection, Custom; Custom's integer box enabled only when Custom is chosen, typing in it selects Custom.
- Pre-select the radio matching the current zoom, otherwise Custom with the current value.
- Integer display (`100`), clamped to 10 to 400.
- Fit Selection: zoom so the current selection fits the visible grid (clamped 10 to 400%).

## Related
#521 / #634 (preset choices now apply), #779 (status bar zoom control)

title: fix(ribbon): Font Size should be a typeable box, not a filtered list (typing 6 gives 36)
author: richard1912
body:
## Summary
In v0.6.1 (Windows 11) the Home ▸ Font Size box is a button that opens a list with a "Type to filter…" field, rather than an editable box. Worse, typing a size and pressing Enter applies an item from the **filtered list** instead of the number typed, so single-digit sizes can't be typed at all:

| Typed + Enter (cell at 11) | Applied |
|---|---|
| `6` | **36** |
| `2` | **24** |
| `7` | **72** |
| `1` | **14** |
| `13` | 13 |

Tested with real key presses (keytips Alt, H, F, S, then the digits and Enter), font size read back with `cell.get`. Only text matching no list item (like `13`) is applied as typed.

In Excel the size box is an editable combo: click into it (or Alt, H, F, S), type `6`, Enter, and the size is 6. The dropdown arrow opens the plain list of sizes; there's no filter field. Any value from 1 to 409 in 0.5 steps is accepted.

## Cause
`size_combo` in `crates/ui-egui/src/ribbon.rs` (around line 1094) draws the size as a `Button` and reuses `editable_combo`, the font-name combo with a substring filter (`d.to_lowercase().contains(&lower)`, around line 439). On Enter, if the filtered list isn't empty it applies the highlighted filtered item; the highlight starts at the current size's index, clamped into the filtered list, which is why `6` lands on 36 (filtered list 16, 26, 36) and `7` on 72.

## Proposal
**Remove the filtered list from Font Size entirely.** Filtering 16 numbers adds nothing and is what causes the wrong sizes. Font Size should behave like Excel's:
- Make the size box itself an editable text field: click or keytip focuses it with the text selected, typing replaces it, Enter applies exactly the number typed (validated 1 to 409, rounded to 0.5, invalid input reverts with no change), Esc cancels.
- A separate dropdown arrow opens the plain size list, with no filter field, with the current size highlighted, arrows and Enter to pick.
- Regression test: typing `6` + Enter at size 11 gives 6.

title: Parity: Font list is a fixed 22 names, not installed fonts, and typed font names are ignored
author: richard1912
body:
## Summary
In v0.6.1 (Windows 11) the Home ▸ Font list is a fixed set of 22 names (`FONTS` in `crates/ui-egui/src/ribbon.rs`, around line 1075), not the fonts installed on the system. Typing a font that isn't in that list (for example `Comic Sans MS` or `Wingdings`, both installed with Windows) and pressing Enter silently does nothing: the cell stays Calibri.

Excel lists every installed font (each drawn in its own face), with **Theme Fonts** and **Recently Used Fonts** sections at the top, autocompletes as you type, and on Enter applies exactly the name typed, even a font that isn't installed (so a workbook can carry a font name for other machines).

## Repro
1. Select a cell, Alt, H, F, F.
2. Type `Comic Sans MS`, Enter.
3. Font is unchanged. Same for `Wingdings`, or any name not in the built-in list.

## Cause
- `font_combo` builds its items from the static `FONTS` array.
- It only handles `ComboResult::Picked`; `ComboResult::Entered` (typed text with no list match) is dropped, so typed names are discarded.

## Proposal
- Populate the list from the installed system fonts (font enumeration through a font-discovery crate, cached at startup or on first open), keeping the current names as the fallback on web/WASM.
- Sections like Excel's: Theme Fonts (the workbook theme's heading/body fonts), Recently Used Fonts, All Fonts.
- Draw each name in its own face if feasible (optional, with a fallback when the face can't be loaded).
- Enter applies the typed name as-is when nothing matches (the font is stored in the file; rendering falls back as it does for workbooks from other machines).
- Clean-room: fonts come from the user's system; nothing bundled (fonts stay in craft-fonts per the repo rules).

## Related
#932 (Font Size box and the shared Enter bug in `editable_combo`)

title: Parity: tables have no drag handle to resize them
author: richard1912
body:
## Summary
In v0.6.1 (Windows 11) a table can't be resized by dragging. Excel draws a small resize handle at the bottom-right corner of every table; dragging it down/right (or up/left) grows or shrinks the table, with the new range outlined while dragging. GridCraft has no such handle: the only way is Table Design ▸ Resize Table (`table.resize`) and typing a range.

## Repro
1. Insert ▸ Table on A1:B5.
2. Hover the bottom-right corner of the table (B5): no handle, no resize cursor.
3. Dragging from there just selects cells (or uses the fill handle when B5 is selected).

## Cause
The engine has `table.resize` (`crates/engine/src/cmd/extra.rs`, around line 818, with overlap checks and tests), but `crates/ui-egui/src/grid.rs` draws no table corner handle and has no drag mode for it.

## Proposal
- Draw a small corner marker at each visible table's bottom-right cell, and show a diagonal resize cursor over it.
- Dragging it previews the new range with an outline (rows and columns snapping to cells, header row fixed), and on release runs `table.resize` with that range as one undo step.
- Same rules as the command: the header row stays, overlaps with other tables/merges are refused, and structured references follow the new range.
- When the table's corner cell is also the selection's corner, the fill handle and table handle shouldn't fight: Excel shows both, the table marker sits just inside the cell's corner.

## Related
#934 (auto-expand when typing next to a table), #575

title: fix(grid): cursor flickers between arrow and Move while drag-selecting (hover cursor runs during drags)
author: richard1912
body:
## Summary
While drag-selecting cells, the mouse cursor flickers between the normal arrow and the four-way Move cursor (and briefly the crosshair). Excel keeps one cursor for the whole drag. Same on v0.6.1 and the #909 branch (Windows 11, 150% scaling).

## Measurement
Real mouse input (`SetCursorPos` + `mouse_event`): press on a cell, drag diagonally about 10 columns and 12 rows over 2 s, sampling the system cursor (`GetCursorInfo`) every ~4 ms:

| Build | Cursor changes during the drag | Cursors seen (samples) |
|---|---|---|
| Excel (Microsoft 365) | **0** | its cell cursor only (445) |
| GridCraft v0.6.1 | **40** | arrow 313, Move 117, crosshair 17 |
| GridCraft #909 branch | **40** | arrow 320, Move 110, crosshair 19 |

## Cause
The hover-cursor block in `crates/ui-egui/src/grid.rs` (around lines 1820 to 1846) runs every frame regardless of `app.grid.drag`. During `Drag::Select` the selection's edge and its fill handle sit right next to the pointer, so the pointer keeps landing within `on_border`'s 3 pt band (`CursorIcon::Move`) or on the handle (`CursorIcon::Crosshair`), then back on a cell.

Also, `CursorIcon::Cell` (the in-cells cursor) shows as the normal arrow on Windows, while Excel shows its thick white cross over cells.

## Proposal
- While a drag is in progress, fix the cursor to the one for that drag: `Drag::Select` keeps the cell cursor, fill drags keep the crosshair, move drags keep Move, resizes keep their resize cursor. Only run the hover logic when no drag is active.
- Regression test: during a simulated `Drag::Select` across the selection edge the requested cursor stays constant.
- Optional: a GridCraft-drawn cell cursor (a thick plus, original artwork) on platforms where `Cell` falls back to the arrow.

## Related
#900 / #909 (select on press), #874 (selection glide)

title: fix(clipboard): no marching ants while the copied cell is selected, and editing the copied cell leaves copy mode on (Ctrl+V pastes the old value)
author: richard1912
body:
## Summary
On v0.6.1 (Windows 11), tested with real key presses and screenshots:

| Step | GridCraft today | Expected |
|---|---|---|
| Select C3 (`hello`), Ctrl+C | Only the solid selection border; the ants appear only after moving to another cell | Ants on C3 straight away |
| Copy C3, type `bye` into C3, Enter | Ants stay around C3 | Copy mode ends, ants gone |
| ...then Ctrl+V on E6 | Pastes the **old** value `hello`, though C3 now shows `bye` | Nothing pasted (copy mode ended) |
| Copy C3, type into A1, Enter, Ctrl+V on G8 | Ants stay, pastes `hello` | **Keep (design choice, see below)** |

## Design choice: keep copy mode when other cells are edited (deliberate improvement on Excel)

> **This is intentional and should stay.** It is a deliberate deviation from Excel, and an improvement on it.

Excel ends copy mode as soon as data is typed into *any* cell (checked: `CutCopyMode` goes to 0 and Ctrl+V then pastes nothing). That follows from Excel's model, where the paste reads the source range at paste time, so any edit might change it. But it's a common annoyance: copy, fix a typo somewhere, and the copy is gone.

GridCraft's clipboard is a snapshot taken at copy time, so an edit elsewhere can't change what gets pasted. Keeping copy mode is safe and more convenient, and matches Google Sheets and most other apps. Please keep it, record it as an intended difference from Excel wherever deviations are listed (for example `docs/target-app-parity.md`), and cover it with a test so it isn't later "fixed" to match Excel.

The only exception is when the copied range *itself* changes (below), because then the outline and the paste no longer agree.

## The bug: editing the copied range itself
When the copied cells change, the ants still mark them as what's about to be pasted, but Ctrl+V pastes the stale snapshot. What's pasted no longer matches what's outlined, which can silently paste outdated values.

## Causes
- **Ants hidden while selected:** the ants are drawn at `range…

title: fix(tabs): New sheet (+) sits at 60% of the width instead of after the last tab, and the tabs/scrollbar split is not resizable
author: richard1912
body:
## Summary
In v0.6.1 (Windows 11) the New sheet (+) button sits far to the right of the sheet tabs, with empty space between the last tab and the button. In Excel the + sits immediately after the last tab (and the horizontal scrollbar takes the space to the right).

Related: the split between the tab area and the horizontal scrollbar can't be resized. In Excel a small splitter (the vertical dotted grip at the left end of the horizontal scrollbar) can be dragged left or right to give more room to the tabs or to the scrollbar, and double-clicking it resets the split. In GridCraft the split is fixed at 60%.

## Repro
1. New workbook, add a second sheet.
2. The + button stays at about 60% of the window width, not next to Sheet2.

## Cause
`crates/ui-egui/src/tabs.rs`: the tab strip is allocated a fixed `tabs_width = (ui.available_width() * 0.6).max(100.0)` (line 73), and its `ScrollArea::horizontal()` uses `.auto_shrink([false, false])` (line 97), so it always fills that width. The + button (line 215) is laid out after the strip, so it lands at the 60% mark however few tabs there are.

## Proposal
- Add a draggable splitter between the tab strip and the horizontal scrollbar, as in Excel: drag to move the split (resize cursor on hover), double-click to reset to the default, and keep the chosen split per window for the session.
- Size the tab strip to its content, capped at the splitter position (default 60%): `auto_shrink([true, false])` with `max_width(tabs_width)`, so the + follows the last tab.
- When the tabs overflow the cap, the strip scrolls as now and the + sits at the cap.
- The horizontal scrollbar takes the remaining space (it already starts after the +).
- Regression test: with two sheets, the + button's left edge is within a few points of the last tab's right edge.

## Related
#840 (scrollbar in the tab bar), #839 / #851 (All Sheets navigator)

title: fix(format): Merge & Center silently discards cell values, even when the only filled cell isn't upper-left
author: richard1912
body:
## Summary
In v0.6.1 (and main), Merge & Center, Merge Across and Merge Cells keep only the upper-left value and delete the rest, with no warning. When the only filled cell isn't the upper-left one, its value is lost and the merged cell ends up blank.

Compared GridCraft (`home.mergeCenter` on A1:B2) with Excel (Microsoft 365, Alt+H, M, C with real key presses):

| Filled cells in A1:B2 | Excel | GridCraft |
|---|---|---|
| A1 only | No warning, keeps `vA1` | Keeps `vA1` |
| **B2 only** | No warning, keeps **`vB2`** | **Blank, `vB2` deleted** |
| A1 and B2 | **Warns** ("only keeps the upper-left value"), OK keeps `vA1` | No warning, `vB2` deleted |
| **B1 and A2** | Warns, OK keeps **`vB1`** (first filled cell, reading across rows) | **Blank, both deleted** |

## Cause
`merge` in `crates/engine/src/cmd/format.rs` (around line 559) always keeps `r.start` and clears every other cell in the range. The comment says "Only the upper-left value survives (Excel warns about this)", but nothing in the UI warns. Merge Across has the same per-row logic.

## Proposal
1. **Keep the first filled cell:** the merged cell gets the first non-empty value in reading order, moved into the upper-left, and only then are the others cleared (matches Excel, including the single-value case).
2. **Warn before discarding:** when more than one cell in the range holds a value, ask first ("Merging cells keeps only the first value and discards the others", OK / Cancel); same for Merge Across per row. Programmatic calls with explicit params don't prompt, per the no-dialogs rule.
3. **Undo** restores everything in one step.
4. **Regression tests:** only B2 filled gives `vB2`; B1 and A2 filled gives `vB1`; the warning shows only when more than one cell is filled.

## Related
#929 / #942 (Merge & Center caption)

title: Design suggestion: Merge & Center could also centre vertically (deliberate improvement on Excel, maintainer decision)
author: richard1912
body:
## Summary
A design suggestion rather than a bug, and not urgent: no need to decide or close it right away.

Excel's Merge & Center only centres horizontally; the vertical alignment stays at Bottom (checked in Microsoft 365: after Alt+H, M, C the merged cell has horizontal Center, vertical Bottom). GridCraft currently does the same (`apply_style(... st.align.h = HAlign::Center)` in `crates/engine/src/cmd/format.rs`).

For merged cells that span several rows (section headers, labels down the side of a table), text sitting at the bottom usually looks wrong, so most people follow Merge & Center with Middle Align every time.

## Suggestion
Let the maintainers choose one of:
1. **Merge & Center centres both ways** (horizontal and vertical Center): a deliberate improvement on Excel, recorded as an intended difference.
2. **An option** (for example in Options ▸ Advanced, "Merge & Center also centres vertically"), off by default for strict Excel parity.
3. **Keep Excel's behaviour** as is.

Whichever is chosen, the file round-trip is unaffected: vertical alignment is an ordinary cell style that Excel reads and writes.

## Related
#944 (Merge & Center discards values), #929 / #942

title: fix(grid): in-cell editor ignores the cell's alignment (text jumps to the top-left while editing, most visible in merged cells)
author: richard1912
body:
## Summary
In v0.6.1 (Windows 11), while a cell is being edited (F2, double-click or typing) the text is always drawn at the top-left of the cell, whatever the cell's alignment. When editing ends it jumps back to its aligned position. Excel's in-cell editor keeps the text where it is displayed: centre/middle stays centred both ways, bottom stays at the bottom, and so on.

Affects merged cells (most visible, since they are large) and ordinary cells with a taller row or wider column.

## Repro (compared with Excel, Microsoft 365)
| Cell | Excel while editing | GridCraft while editing |
|---|---|---|
| B2:D5 merged, centre + middle, `hello`, F2, type `x` | `hellox` centred both ways | `hellox` at the top-left |
| B2:D5 merged, bottom aligned | `hellox` at the bottom | top-left |
| single cell B2 (tall row, wide column), centre + middle | centred both ways | top-left |
| B2:D5 merged, left + top | top-left | top-left (same) |

Checked with real key presses and screenshots of both apps.

## Cause
`crates/ui-egui/src/grid.rs` (around lines 2700 to 2727): the editor rect is `Rect::from_min_size(rect.min, vec2(w, h))` and the `TextEdit` is placed in a child UI at its top-left. The cell's `st.align.h` / `st.align.v` are read for painting (`cell_text_y`, `wrapped_cell_text_y`, around lines 926 to 941) but not for the editor. The editor also only grows to the right, while centred text in Excel grows both ways.

## Proposal
- Place the editor's text using the same alignment as painting: horizontal (left, centre, right, and General following the value type) and vertical (top, middle, bottom) within the cell or merged area.
- When the text outgrows the cell, grow the editor box in the direction of the alignment (centre grows both ways, right grows left), as Excel does.
- Keep the caret and selection hit-testing in step with the shifted text.
- Regression test: editing a centre/middle merged cell keeps the text's centre at the cell's centre.

## Related
#944, #945 (Merge & Center)…

title: fix(format): Merge & Center on a selection containing merged cells merges everything instead of unmerging (Excel toggles)
author: richard1912
body:
## Summary
In v0.6.1 (and main), pressing Merge & Center with a selection that *contains* merged cells merges the whole selection into one big cell. In Excel, Merge & Center acts as a toggle: if the selection contains any merged cells, it **unmerges** them all (no prompt), whichever cell is active.

## Compared with Excel (Microsoft 365, Alt+H, M, C with real key presses)
Starting with B2:C2 merged (and E5:F5 in the last case):

| Selection (active cell) | Excel | GridCraft |
|---|---|---|
| A1:D4 (A1, not merged) | **Unmerges** B2:C2 | Merges A1:D4 |
| B2:D4 (B2, merged) | Unmerges B2:C2 | Merges B2:D4 |
| A1:D4 (B2) | Unmerges B2:C2 | Merges A1:D4 |
| B2:C2 (exactly the merge) | Unmerges | Unmerges (only this case matches) |
| A1:F6 containing B2:C2 and E5:F5 | **Unmerges both** | Merges A1:F6, and the value in E5 is discarded with no warning (see #944) |

## Cause
`merge` in `crates/engine/src/cmd/format.rs` (around line 559) switches to unmerge only when every selected range *equals* an existing merge (`sh.merges.contains(r)`). Otherwise it removes the intersecting merges and merges the full selection.

## Proposal
- Merge & Center: if any merged area intersects the selection, unmerge every merged area that intersects it (and leave the rest of the selection as is); only merge when the selection contains no merged cells. Matches Excel.
- Keep the toggle state visible: the Merge & Center button shows as pressed when the active cell is merged (check whether this is already the case).
- Merge Across / Merge Cells / Unmerge from the dropdown keep their explicit meaning.
- Regression tests: selection containing one merge unmerges it; containing two unmerges both; no merges merges.

## Related
#944 (merge discards values; @marcoarnulfo is working on `merge()` there, so this may fit the same change), #945, #948

title: Calc: a contested spill area changes hands on Calculate Now and on reopening
author: quantmind-br
body:
When two dynamic arrays want the same cells, entering the second one gives it `#SPILL!` and the first keeps its area, as in Excel. A full recalculation (F9, `formulas.calculateNow`) or saving and reopening the XLSX lays the arrays out again in reading order instead. The area goes to whichever anchor comes first, and the other array turns into `#SPILL!`. The values change without any edit.

Repro on `main` (`84acf62`), empty workbook:

```sh
gridcraft-cli run \
  --cmd 'cell.set={"cell":"C14","input":"=SEQUENCE(1,7)"}' \
  --cmd 'cell.set={"cell":"F13","input":"=SEQUENCE(5,2)"}' \
  --cmd 'sheet.read={"range":"C13:I14"}' \
  --cmd 'formulas.calculateNow={}' \
  --cmd 'sheet.read={"range":"C13:I14"}'
```

```
before F9: [[null,null,null,"#SPILL!",null,null,null],[1,2,3,4,5,6,7]]
after F9:  [[null,null,null,1,2,null,null],["#SPILL!",null,null,3,4,null,null]]
```

Saving right after entering F13 and reopening the file gives the same result as F9. The file can only cache `#VALUE!` for F13 (Excel refuses a cached `#SPILL!`), and the reader drops the dynamic arrays' `ref` (C14 is saved with `ref="C14:I14"`, F13 with `ref="F13"`), so `recalc_all` has nothing to tell the two apart.

Found by the command-sequence fuzz (`[recalc]` and `[xlsx roundtrip]` invariants). The default seeds on `main` don't reach it. A PR that adds command parameters shifts the random sequence (seed 0 on #447), and the shrunk sequence fails on `main` too:

```rust

s.execute("home.insertSheet", json!({"before": 1})).ok();
s.execute("cell.set", json!({"cell": "C14", "input": "=TRANSPOSE(B18:B24)", "sheet": "Sheet1"})).ok();
s.execute("range.fill", json!({"input": "=D14:E18", "range": "E13:F13"})).ok();
// Sheet1!F13 (=I26:J30): #SPILL! in memory, 0 after a full recalc
```

author: richard1912
body:
## Summary

Most GridCraft dialogs open at the same fixed size whatever they contain, so a one-field dialog is a large mostly empty box. Excel sizes each dialog to fit its contents. GridCraft 0.6.1, Windows 11, 150% scaling.

Measured at 100% scale (logical points):

| Dialog | GridCraft | Excel |
|---|---|---|
| Column Width | 380 x 420 | 200 x 105 |

title: XLSX: a picture shared by several sheets is written once per sheet (one media part becomes N copies)
author: KNUFFIXX
body:
## Summary
Excel stores a picture that appears on several sheets (a copied sheet, a copied picture) as one `xl/media` part that each sheet's drawing points to. GridCraft 0.6.1 writes a separate, identical copy for every drawing. A real 16-sheet service-charge workbook that shares one 112 KB PNG grows from 0.4 MB to 1.9 MB on a plain open and save. Excel opens both files; only the size is affected.

## Steps to reproduce
Fixture [`gc_shared_image.xlsx`](https://github.com/KNUFFIXX/artcraft-fixtures/blob/main/gridcraft/gc_shared_image.xlsx) (184 KB, generator [`make_gc_shared_image.py`](https://github.com/KNUFFIXX/artcraft-fixtures/blob/main/gridcraft/make_gc_shared_image.py)): one 160 KB PNG (seeded noise) on four sheets; all four `xl/drawings/_rels/drawingN.xml.rels` target `xl/media/image1.png`.
`gridcraft-cli run --in gc_shared_image.xlsx --out out.xlsx`

## Expected
One media part (shared, or de-duplicated by content); about the same file size.

## Actual (0.6.1 Windows; same on a Linux build of `main` after 0.6.1)
`out.xlsx` is 704 KB with `xl/media/image1.png` … `image4.png`, byte-identical (same SHA-1).

## Environment
GridCraft 0.6.1 (`gridcraft-0.6.1-windows-x64-portable.zip`), Windows 11 25H2 (build 26200); Excel 365 (16.0) opens input and output.

---

author: PierrunoYT
body:
<!-- gridcraft-source-audit:84acf6293b1dc1fc09837524e035d674eb4d6741:F03-cut -->
## Assessment
- **Severity:** High (provisional triage, not CVSS).
- **Confidence:** high in the source-level defect; runtime consequences not reproduced.
- **Baseline:** upstream main [84acf629](https://github.com/storytold/gridcraft/commit/84acf6293b1dc1fc09837524e035d674eb4d6741), rechecked at filing.
- **Verification:** read-only source review. No build, runtime regression, exploit, or destructive test was run. Conditions and test suggestions below are not claims of executed reproduction.

## Source evidence and root cause
- [crates/engine/src/cmd/edit.rs:920–966](https://github.com/storytold/gridcraft/blob/84acf6293b1dc1fc09837524e035d674eb4d6741/crates/engine/src/cmd/edit.rs#L920-L966)

paste_special validates the destination anchor, but not the entire footprint. For a same-document cut with what=all it calls source.take_cells(src); later, an out-of-grid at.offset returns None and the loop continues rather than rejecting the operation.

## Conditions and realistic impact
A multi-cell cut pasted near the last row or column can partly fit: source cells are removed, while overflowing destination cells are skipped. This is silent data loss in the resulting workbook. Partial insertion has a related existing report, #580; this issue isolates cut-paste.

## Recommended remediation
Preflight the complete destination footprint, including transpose and affected features, before removing anything. Refuse atomically when the move cannot fit.

## Suggested regression coverage
Use small cut blocks anchored at bottom/right boundaries, with transpose controls. Assert refusal preserves source, destination, clipboard and history; fitting boundary moves must still succeed.

## Source evidence and root cause
- [crates/engine/src/cmd/data.rs:817–850](https://github.com/storytold/gridcraft/blob/84acf6293b1dc1fc09837524e035d674eb4d6741/crates/engine/src/cmd/data.rs#L817-L850)

title: fix(web): parent-host save marks the workbook clean before persistence acknowledgment
author: PierrunoYT
body:
<!-- gridcraft-source-audit:84acf6293b1dc1fc09837524e035d674eb4d6741:F27 -->
## Assessment
- **Severity:** Medium (provisional triage, not CVSS).
- **Confidence:** high in the source-level finding; runtime consequences not reproduced.
- **Baseline:** upstream main [84acf629](https://github.com/storytold/gridcraft/commit/84acf6293b1dc1fc09837524e035d674eb4d6741).
- **Verification:** read-only source review. No build, runtime regression, exploit, or destructive test was run. Conditions and regression suggestions are not executed reproduction claims.

## Source evidence and root cause
- [apps/gridcraft-web/src/host.rs:82–126](https://github.com/storytold/gridcraft/blob/84acf6293b1dc1fc09837524e035d674eb4d6741/apps/gridcraft-web/src/host.rs#L82-L126)

post_save adds the filename to saved after postMessage succeeds. sync then assigns doc.saved = doc.wb.clone() on the active document and reports dirty=false. The bridge receives open messages but defines no persistence acknowledgment with document/revision identity.

## Conditions and realistic impact
In optional ?host=parent mode, successful handoff to the parent is treated as completed save. Parent persistence failure or missing handling can leave GridCraft reporting clean without durable data. The host is documented to handle failures itself; an independent host pending-save/leave guard mitigates this. This is a save-state contract gap, not a cross-origin vulnerability: origin/source checks are present.

## Recommended remediation
Add acknowledgment tied to document UID, operation ID and saved revision, or explicitly expose pending/failed persistence so the host cannot confuse handoff with durability. Clear only the revision actually persisted.

## Suggested regression coverage
Use a same-origin fake parent with failed, absent and delayed acknowledgments. Cover edits/document switches while saving and verify unsaved changes remain dirty until the matching persisted revision is acknowledged.

title: fix(view): New Window creates independent documents that save over the same file
author: PierrunoYT
body:
<!-- gridcraft-supplemental-audit:84acf6293b1dc1fc09837524e035d674eb4d6741:S01 -->
## Assessment
- **Severity:** High, provisional triage (not CVSS).
- **Confidence:** High in the described source-level defect; runtime consequences were not reproduced.
- **Baseline:** latest upstream main [84acf629](https://github.com/storytold/gridcraft/commit/84acf6293b1dc1fc09837524e035d674eb4d6741), rechecked before filing.
- **Verification:** read-only source inspection. No code changes, build, exploit, destructive test or runtime reproduction. Suggested tests below were not executed.

## Exact source evidence and root cause
- [crates/engine/src/cmd/extra.rs:781–786](https://github.com/storytold/gridcraft/blob/84acf6293b1dc1fc09837524e035d674eb4d6741/crates/engine/src/cmd/extra.rs#L781-L786)

Open a saved workbook, invoke New Window, then make different edits in the two documents and save both. The later save can replace the earlier document’s changes with its divergent snapshot. This is a source-confirmed independent-state/same-path conflict; no overwrite was executed.

Related #162 concerns native window UX, not this same-path state conflict.

title: fix(table): inserting a generated header shifts cells without adjusting references
author: PierrunoYT
body:
<!-- gridcraft-supplemental-audit:84acf6293b1dc1fc09837524e035d674eb4d6741:S03 -->
## Assessment

- **Verification:** read-only source inspection. No code changes, build, exploit, destructive test or runtime reproduction. Suggested tests below were not executed.

With `header:false`, insertion calls `sh.cells.shift_rows_in_cols(...)` and moves cell pictures directly. It sets `cx.structural = true`, but does not apply the formula/reference transformations used by structural cell insertion. Recalculation cannot repair unchanged reference coordinates.

## Conditions and realistic impact
For example, A1=10, A2=20 and B1=SUM(A1:A2), then create a table over A1:A2 with no header. Values move to A2:A3 while the outside formula retains A1:A2, changing which data it sums. This predicted result follows from the source; no runtime test was run.

## Recommended remediation
Reuse the reference-aware insertion operation before writing the header, with its bounds, arrays, object and dependent-reference handling. Keep the entire operation atomic.

## Suggested regression tests
Use header:false with asymmetric values and formulas both inside and outside the moved columns, including references from another sheet. Verify values move and references still identify the same data. Keep header:true as an unchanged control.

- [crates/functions/src/ets.rs:355–365](https://github.com/storytold/gridcraft/blob/84acf6293b1dc1fc09837524e035d674eb4d6741/crates/functions/src/ets.rs#L355-L365)

Walk each gap once, using the previous and next known point to fill its whole interval, or precompute next-known positions in a reverse pass. Preserve endpoint and interpolation semantics.

title: fix(mcp): truncated or mismatched control replies can desynchronize the connection
author: PierrunoYT
body:
<!-- gridcraft-supplemental-audit:84acf6293b1dc1fc09837524e035d674eb4d6741:S18 -->
## Assessment

- **Baseline:** latest upstream main [84acf629](https://github.com/storytold/gridcraft/commit/84acf6293b1dc1fc09837524e035d674eb4d6741), rechecked before filing.
- **Verification:** read-only source inspection. No code changes, build, exploit, destructive test or runtime reproduction. Suggested tests below were not executed.

## Exact source evidence and root cause
- [crates/mcp/src/backend.rs:63–102](https://github.com/storytold/gridcraft/blob/84acf6293b1dc1fc09837524e035d674eb4d6741/crates/mcp/src/backend.rs#L63-L102)

The read is capped by `take(MAX_REPLY).read_line`, but only n==0 is rejected; newline completion is not checked. JSON parse failure leaves self.conn intact, and response IDs are never compared with the request ID. An oversized reply leaves unread bytes on the persistent connection.

## Conditions and realistic impact
A control response exceeds the byte cap or the peer returns malformed/stale replies. A later call may consume the prior response’s remainder instead of its own response, and a syntactically valid wrong-ID reply is accepted. No external peer was contacted or attacked.

## Recommended remediation
Require a complete bounded frame, validate the reply ID/schema, and discard the connection on framing, parse or correlation failure. Do not automatically replay mutations whose completion is unknown.

## Suggested regression tests
Use a local fake transport with a complete reply, exact-boundary reply, oversized line, EOF before newline, invalid JSON and a wrong ID. After each failure, ensure a later call cannot consume stale bytes or accept another call’s response.

Distinct from #1006’s replay of mutations after transport errors; fixes should be coordinated.

author: PierrunoYT
body:
<!-- gridcraft-supplemental-audit:84acf6293b1dc1fc09837524e035d674eb4d6741:S24 -->
## Assessment
- **Severity:** Medium, provisional triage (not CVSS).
- **Confidence:** High in the described source-level finding; runtime consequences were not reproduced.
- **Baseline:** latest upstream main [84acf629](https://github.com/storytold/gridcraft/commit/84acf6293b1dc1fc09837524e035d674eb4d6741), rechecked before filing.
- **Verification:** read-only source inspection. No code changes, build, exploit, destructive test or runtime reproduction. Suggested tests below were not executed.

## Exact source evidence and root cause
- [apps/gridcraft-cli/src/check.rs:207–265](https://github.com/storytold/gridcraft/blob/84acf6293b1dc1fc09837524e035d674eb4d6741/apps/gridcraft-cli/src/check.rs#L207-L265)

collect_inputs/walk return only paths, discarding read_dir failures and per-entry errors via flatten. Depth/file caps return or truncate without a report entry. The command then succeeds if every collected report is clean; an empty report list also satisfies all().

## Conditions and realistic impact
A requested corpus directory is unreadable, contains inaccessible subdirectories, exceeds traversal limits or contributes no checked files. The command can exit successfully without checking all intended inputs and without identifying omissions, undermining its use as a verification gate.

Return discovery diagnostics alongside paths, distinguish intentional hidden/lock-file exclusion from errors/limits, and make incomplete scans visible and non-successful unless explicitly allowed. Decide and document zero-input semantics.

## Suggested regression tests
Use a disposable readable corpus plus a controlled traversal error or injected walker failure. Cover depth/file-limit boundaries and an empty match set. Assert diagnostics and exit status reflect incomplete verification while normal scans stay deterministic.

title: fix(cf): each cell lookup clones the full conditional-format statistics cache
author: PierrunoYT
body:
<!-- gridcraft-supplemental-audit:84acf6293b1dc1fc09837524e035d674eb4d6741:S26 -->
## Assessment
- **Severity:** Medium, provisional triage (not CVSS).
- **Confidence:** High in the described source-level finding; runtime consequences were not reproduced.
- **Baseline:** latest upstream main [84acf629](https://github.com/storytold/gridcraft/commit/84acf6293b1dc1fc09837524e035d674eb4d6741), rechecked before filing.
- **Verification:** read-only source inspection. No code changes, build, exploit, destructive test or runtime reproduction. Suggested tests below were not executed.

## Exact source evidence and root cause
- [crates/engine/src/cf.rs:114–124](https://github.com/storytold/gridcraft/blob/84acf6293b1dc1fc09837524e035d674eb4d6741/crates/engine/src/cf.rs#L114-L124)

Each applicable rule obtains cached RuleStats and immediately calls clone. RuleStats owns the sorted values and count map, so the cache avoids recomputation but still copies its input-sized containers for every cell lookup.

## Conditions and realistic impact
A large conditional-format range is consulted while drawing many visible cells or printing/exporting. Repeated full-statistics copies create per-cell O(range size) CPU/allocation traffic. The cloning is source-confirmed; exact latency and memory peaks were not measured.

## Recommended remediation
Borrow immutable cached statistics for evaluation or store a shared immutable representation. Avoid calculating/copying statistics for rule kinds that do not need them while retaining correct invalidation after edits.

## Suggested regression tests

title: CRITICAL: Opening a second workbook silently discards the first — unsaved work lost with zero warning
author: iskandar221201
body:
### Severity: data loss

**Steps to reproduce**

Open workbook A, type something (do NOT save)
File → Open → workbook B
Workbook A vanishes. No save dialog. No "unsaved changes" prompt. Nothing.

**What happens**

The user's unsaved work in workbook A is gone — silently. No undo, no recovery, no backup prompt.

**Why this is critical**

This isn't a missing feature, it's a data-loss bug. Excel, LibreOffice, ONLYOFFICE — they all either open a new window/tab, or prompt to save. GridCraft silently discards the first file instead.

New users will hit this within minutes: open a second file to compare data → work on the first file is gone. This makes GridCraft unsafe for real work until fixed, no matter how good the engine is.

**Minimum acceptable fix**

If multi-window/tab (#843) isn't ready yet, at minimum: prompt "Save changes to workbook A?" before replacing it — like every other desktop application.

**Environment**

GridCraft 0.6.1 via ArtCraft launcher, Linux x64

title: Flatpak: fonts are looked up only at hard-coded /usr/share/fonts paths, so fonts installed on the host are not discovered
author: musaad-sharikh
body:
In the Flatpak, GridCraft finds fonts only at fixed paths, and none of them is where the sandbox exposes the host's fonts. Fonts installed on the system are not discovered, and in the environment below the default cell font and Arabic text resolve to the runtime's DejaVu Sans.

### Steps to reproduce

1. Install the GridCraft 0.6.1 Flatpak on a Linux desktop that has an Arabic font installed system-wide (for example Vazirmatn under `/usr/share/fonts`).
2. Type `Hello` in A1 and `بسم الله` in A2.
3. Open Format Cells › Font and look for the installed font.

### Actual

- Observed: the font list is short and does not include the fonts installed on the system, and Arabic cell text is not drawn in the installed Arabic font.
- In this environment the only "cell" candidate file that exists inside the sandbox is `dejavu/DejaVuSans.ttf`, which also covers Arabic. Other setups (different runtime, extra filesystem permissions, a workbook font found under `~/.local/share/fonts`) can resolve differently.
- Inferred from the source, not observed: a cell set to a font that the scan did not discover is drawn in the fallback role, because binding a workbook font goes through the same catalogue.

### Expected

Installed fonts are listed and usable, and Arabic falls back to an installed Arabic face. Resolving fonts through fontconfig would cover every layout; at minimum also scan `/run/host/fonts`, `/run/host/user-fonts` and `$XDG_DATA_HOME/fonts`.

### Environment

- GridCraft 0.6.1, Flatpak (`org.freedesktop.Platform` 25.08), x86_64
- CachyOS Linux, niri 26.04, Wayland

### Cause (v0.6.1)

- `system_font_dirs()` in `crates/ui-egui/src/fonts.rs` scans `/usr/share/fonts`, `/usr/local/share/fonts`, `~/.fonts` and `~/.local/share/fonts`. In the sandbox `/usr/share/fonts` is the runtime's (88 font files here); the host's fonts are at `/run/host/fonts` (1,245 files here) and are never read. The app's own permissions expose no font folder.

title: [Bug] Selected columns resize during drag instead of applying the group width on mouse release
author: mgjaggers
body:
## Summary

When multiple columns are selected, dragging the resize boundary of one selected column changes the widths of all selected columns continuously while the mouse button is still held down.

The expected interaction is the Excel behavior described by the user: preview the resize on the column being dragged, then apply the final width to all selected columns on mouse release.

## Steps to reproduce

1. Open a worksheet in GridCraft.
2. Select multiple columns using the column headers (for example, A through C).
3. Press and hold the resize boundary of one selected column.
4. Drag to change its width while keeping the mouse button held down.
5. Observe the other selected columns before releasing the mouse button.
6. Release the mouse button.

## Actual behavior

All selected columns change width during the drag.

## Expected behavior

During the drag, only the column whose boundary is being dragged should show the width change. The other selected columns should keep their current widths until mouse release. On release, apply the final width to all selected columns.

## Environment

- GridCraft 0.6.1, official standalone macOS app
- macOS 27.0
- Apple silicon (arm64)

This is a user-observed GUI issue; it has not been independently reproduced by the reporting assistant.

## Related

#341 concerns resizing multiple selected columns, but does not describe when width changes should propagate during a drag.

title: Data validation list dropdown shows only ~3 items; should show up to 8 without scrolling (Excel parity)
author: LinKappa
body:
**Version:** GridCraft 0.6.1, macOS (universal build)

### Problem
The in-cell dropdown of a list data validation (`list_picker` in `crates/ui-egui/src/grid.rs`) shows only about three items, even when the list is short. With a five-item list (`"Hatha Yoga,Vinyasa Flow,Yin Yoga,Morning Yoga,Prenatal Yoga"`), the popup shows roughly three entries and a scrollbar, so the user has to scroll to see all choices. The popup height comes from `ScrollArea::vertical().max_height(200.0)`, and the popup does not grow to fit its content.

### Steps to reproduce
1. Add a list validation to a range, e.g. `F2:F200` with source `"Hatha Yoga,Vinyasa Flow,Yin Yoga,Morning Yoga,Prenatal Yoga"`.
2. Select a cell in the range and click the dropdown arrow.
3. Only about three of the five items are visible; the rest need scrolling.

### Expected (Excel behaviour)
Excel's validation dropdown shows up to **8 items** without scrolling and sizes itself to the list. Lists of 8 or fewer items are fully visible, and a scrollbar appears only for longer lists.

### Suggestion
Size the popup to its content up to about 8 rows (row height × min(items, 8)). Show a scrollbar only when there are more items, and keep the popup within the available screen space (flip above the cell near the bottom edge).

title: XLSX files are detected as application/octet-stream by PHP
author: JorgRios
body:
I'm experiencing a potential compatibility issue with XLSX files generated by this tool when uploading them to a Laravel application.

The generated file is rejected by Laravel's MIME validation because PHP detects its MIME type as `application/octet-stream` instead of `application/vnd.openxmlformats-officedocument.spreadsheetml.sheet`.

Interestingly, opening the generated file in Microsoft Excel and saving it again as an XLSX file resolves the issue.

## Environment

- PHP: 8.1.34

title: Linux: with a real-world 8,000-row workbook the UI thread runs at 100% for as long as you scroll or click, while a small workbook stays at about 10%
author: myredroom
body:
**Version:** GridCraft 0.6.1 (.deb), Linux Mint 22.3, Cinnamon 6.6.9 on X11, kernel 7.0.0, AMD Radeon RX 6750 XT (Mesa 25.2.8, RADV)

### What happens

With my health-tracking workbook open, GridCraft feels sluggish: scrolling lags and clicks take a moment to land. With a small workbook it feels normal.

I measured the process with `top -H` (per thread, 1-second samples) while doing the same thing in each file: scrolling up and down a sheet and clicking cells for about 15 seconds.

| Workbook | Idle | While scrolling and clicking | Feel |
|---|---|---|---|
| Small test workbook (3 sheets, 45 formulas) | 0% | 5–14% of one core | normal |
| Health workbook (see below) | 0% | **99–100% of one core**, the whole time | slow |

- All the work is on the **main thread**. The other 19 threads stay at 0%.
- When interaction stops, CPU drops straight back to 0%. There is no background loop; each interaction just costs a lot.
- It is using the GPU: the process has `/dev/dri/renderD128` open, not llvmpipe.
- The **engine is not the bottleneck**: `gridcraft-cli` opens and evaluates the same workbook in 0.9 s.

### The workbook

A long-running personal tracking workbook created in Excel:
- main sheet: 8,276 rows × 44 columns, about 60,000 formulas (one row per day, with formulas pre-filled years ahead);
- 7 other sheets, 4 of them chart sheets with 6 charts plotting thousands of points;
- 1 frozen header row.

### What I ruled out

- **Conditional formatting:** the main sheet has an alternate-row shading rule stored as `A2:AQ476052` (about 20 million cells). Trimming it to `A2:AQ8276` made **no difference**: still 100% while scrolling.
- **A sheet full of volatile `RANDBETWEEN` cells:** deleted, no difference.
- **Network share:** the same thing happens with a local copy.

I can't share the workbook (personal health data), but I'm happy to run a profiling build or a diagnostic command if that would help.

### Expected

Like Excel, work proportional to what is **visible or changed*…

title: Linux X11 with fractional scaling: on first open the window shows part of the OTHER monitor's screen until it repaints
author: myredroom
body:
**Version:** GridCraft 0.6.1 (.deb), Linux Mint 22.3, Cinnamon 6.6.9 on X11, AMD Radeon RX 6750 XT (Mesa 25.2.8, RADV)

### What happens

Every time GridCraft opens, its window initially shows **a picture of the other monitor**: the content at the matching position on the second screen, not what was behind the window. The real GridCraft UI appears after it repaints.

### Setup

Two 2560×1440 monitors side by side, each scaled by Cinnamon's fractional scaling to **4096×2304** (xrandr transform), giving an X screen of **8192×2304**:

```
 0: +*DisplayPort-0 4096/597x2304/336+4096+0
 1: +HDMI-A-0       4096/597x2304/336+0+0
```

### Guess at the cause

The first presented frame looks like an uninitialised or wrongly offset surface. With a scaling transform, logical window positions and framebuffer positions differ by monitor offsets, so the first frame seems to be read from or presented at the wrong offset. Possibly related to #760 (surface sizing across monitors with different scales). Same machine as #1098.

### Expected

The first frame shows GridCraft's own UI, or a blank background, never another monitor's contents.

title: Keyboard shortcuts: measure Spanish Excel's shortcuts and key tips
author: iluebbe
body:
GridCraft's keyboard shortcuts follow the interface language, as Excel's do (#1124). German Excel's are measured and in `crates/ui-egui/src/keymap/de.rs`. Spanish Excel has its own shortcuts as well. Until someone measures them, GridCraft's Spanish interface uses the English ones.

We need one person with **Excel for Windows (Microsoft 365) in Spanish** to press the keys below and write down what happens. It takes about 30–45 minutes, and no programming is needed.

## What Microsoft's Spanish list says

Microsoft's Spanish [keyboard shortcut page](https://support.microsoft.com/es-es/office/keyboard-shortcuts-in-excel-1798d9d5-842a-42b8-9c99-9b7213f0040f) differs from the English one here:

| Action | English Excel | Spanish list |
|---|---|---|
| Open | Ctrl+O | Ctrl+A |
| Save | Ctrl+S | Ctrl+S (also given for Underline) |
| Bold | Ctrl+B | Ctrl+N in one row, Ctrl+Alt+N in another |
| Italic | Ctrl+I | Ctrl+K |
| Underline | Ctrl+U | Ctrl+S |
| Insert Hyperlink | Ctrl+K | Ctrl+Alt+K |
| Function Arguments (after a function name) | Ctrl+A | Ctrl+E |
| Flash Fill | Ctrl+E | Ctrl+Mayús+E |
| Fill Color key tip | Alt, H, H | Alt, O, H (but Home is Alt, H in another row) |

These lists aren't reliable. The German one names Strg+0 for hiding columns, but German Excel uses Strg+8; it says Strg+Umschalt+_ removes the border, but it adds one. That's why we measure.

## How to measure

**Setup**
1. Set Excel's interface to Spanish: File › Options › Language › Office display language: Español. Restart Excel.
2. Use the keyboard layout you normally type with, and note which one it is (we expect Spanish (Spain) or Latin American).
3. Open a new blank workbook and type this into A1:D4. Column D is formulas, and 1,5 is one and a half, typed with your decimal separator:

title: Perf: charts are resolved and rendered again on every frame
author: vangel76
body:
Follow-up to #1098 (and #1136).

**Problem.** `chartview::paint_objects` calls `gridcraft_chart::resolve` and `gridcraft_chart::render` for every chart that intersects the viewport on every frame, with no cache. The cost is O(points) per chart per frame, so a workbook with several charts that plot thousands of points keeps the UI thread busy while the user scrolls or clicks, even though nothing in the document changed. The reporter of #1098 has 4 chart sheets and 6 charts with thousands of points.

**Plan.**
- Cache the rendered primitives (`Vec<Prim>`) of each chart across frames. A frame in which nothing relevant changed does no `resolve` and no `render`.
- Invalidation: the cache holds a `Weak<Workbook>` of the document it was built from. The workbook is an `Arc` that is only ever changed through `Arc::make_mut` (or replaced), and `make_mut` on an `Arc` that has a `Weak` always moves the value to a new allocation, so "the document's `Arc` is the one I cached" is a sound, mutation-path-independent test (no per-command counter that a new code path could forget).
- Also keyed on the chart's place in the workbook, the zoom, the pixels-per-point and the font set (text is measured with egui's fonts).
- Capped in entries and bytes, least recently used out, entries of closed workbooks dropped.
- Tests: a counter test that N frames of an unchanged workbook build each chart once and that each kind of change rebuilds exactly once, and an equality test of cached against fresh output.

Painting the cached primitives into egui shapes stays O(primitives) per visible chart; that is not changed here.

I'm tracking this under #1098.

title: Regional number formats: currency, separators and dates are fixed to en-US (needs pt-BR: R$ 1.234,56, dd/mm/aaaa)
author: budugoos-oss
body:
**Version:** `gridcraft-web-0.6.1.zip`, Chrome on Windows 11, interface language Português (Brasil).

With the Portuguese (Brazil) interface, the ribbon and dialogs are translated ("Moeda", "Contábil"), but number and date formatting stay en-US. Brazilian users expect Excel pt-BR behaviour, and today a currency cell doesn't look the way it does in Excel.

### What we see
- Home › Number: the Currency/Accounting button shows **$**, and the built-in codes in the build are `"$"#,##0.00` and `_("$"* #,##0.00_);_("$"* \(#,##0.00\);_("$"* "-"??_);_(@_)`.
- We found no setting for decimal/group separators or currency symbol, and the built-in short date is `m/d/yyyy`.
- So, as far as we can tell, there is no way to get `R$ 1.234,56` (comma decimal, dot grouping) in a cell.

### What Excel does with a pt-BR locale
| | Excel pt-BR |
|---|---|
| Currency | `R$ 1.234,56` (code `"R$" #,##0.00`) |
| Accounting | `R$ 1.234,56` aligned, `R$ -` for zero (code `_-"R$" * #,##0.00_-;-"R$" * #,##0.00_-;_-"R$" * "-"??_-;_-@_-`) |
| Negative currency | `-R$ 50,00` |
| Short date | `13/10/2026` (`dd/mm/aaaa`) |
| Input | `1234,56` and `1.234,56` are numbers; `13/10/2026` is a date |

### Suggestion
A regional setting (File › Options, or following the interface language / `navigator.language`) that controls:
1. decimal and group separators for display and input parsing,
2. the default currency symbol and placement for the Currency/Accounting buttons and the Format Cells list,
3. default short/long date order.

Format codes stored in the .xlsx would stay locale-independent (as in OOXML), so files keep opening correctly in Excel. Happy to test a build.

title: [Feature Request] Native VBA macro support — editing, execution, and Excel compatibility
author: artemKerimoff
body:
## Summary

I would like to propose adding native VBA (Visual Basic for Applications) support to GridCraft, including the ability to **create, edit, save, and execute VBA macros**, with compatibility with existing Microsoft Excel `.xlsm` workbooks as the long-term goal.

I understand that implementing a fully compatible VBA environment would be a substantial undertaking, especially for a cross-platform application written in Rust. However, I believe this could become one of GridCraft's most valuable features, particularly for users who want to migrate away from Microsoft Excel without losing their existing automation workflows.

Related discussions:
- #6 — VBA Macros support
- #356 — Possibility of Macros

## Motivation

VBA remains widely used in professional Excel workflows, including financial models, reporting, data processing, document generation, and internal business tools.

For many users, the primary obstacle to replacing Excel is not spreadsheet functionality itself, but the inability to execute existing macros.

GridCraft already provides:
- A spreadsheet engine written in Rust.
- A command-based architecture.
- Built-in automation, scripting, CLI, and MCP interfaces.
- `.xlsm` support with VBA project preservation.

These capabilities could provide a useful foundation for integrating a VBA runtime.

The goal would not simply be to introduce another scripting language, but to eventually allow existing Excel VBA macros to run in GridCraft without requiring users to rewrite them.

## Proposed functionality

### 1. VBA macro execution

Allow users to execute VBA procedures from existing `.xlsm` workbooks.

For example:

```vb
Sub Example()
    Worksheets("Sheet1").Range("A1").Value = 42
    Worksheets("Sheet1").Range("A2").Value = "Hello from VBA"
End Sub
```

Ideally, basic macros like this would work without modification.
